2. Sidewall Riser Ducts - Removal (Figure 401 or Figure 402 or Figure 403)

A. General

(1) This procedure contains the tasks to remove and install the sidewall riser ducts between the distribution bay and the overhead distribution ducts. (a) The sidewall riser duct installation consists of these components: 1) Six ducts 2) Three support assemblies 3) Six flexible hoses 4) Six flexible sleeves 5) A transition duct assembly. 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169 6) Tape, clamps and plastic ties 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224 7) Clamps and plastic ties 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 8) Plastic ties ALL (2) There are three sets of riser ducts, two on the left side of the passenger cabin and one set on the right side. (3) Access to the sidewall riser ducts is through the sidewall panels directly above the distribution bay in the main passenger cabin. 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224 (4) There are two configurations of the installation where the sidewall riser ducts connect to the spuds on the transition duct. One configuration consists of the sidewall riser ducts directly connected to the spuds on the transition duct with a clamp to secure each riser duct and spud together. The other configuration uses a flex sleeve between each riser duct and transition duct spud with two clamps to secure the connections. EFFECTIVITY ALL 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 (5) There are two configurations of the installation where the sidewall riser ducts connect to the spuds on the transition duct. One configuration consists of the sidewall riser ducts directly connected to the spuds on the transition duct with a tie-strap to secure each riser duct and spud together. The other configuration uses a flex sleeve between each riser duct and transition duct spud with an upper tie strap and lower clamp to secure the connections. ALL

E. Sidewall Riser Ducts Installation

SUBTASK 21-23-04-160-001 (1) If you removed the transition duct [12] with the sidewall riser ducts [4], then remove all the sealant between the faying surfaces of the transition duct [12] and elbow duct [10] as follows: (a) Lightly abrade the surfaces with old adhesive with 320 grit or finer abrasive cloth, B00102, until the old adhesive is removed. (b) Wet a cotton wiper, G00034, with solvent, B00083, or alcohol, B00130, and wipe all faying surfaces until all traces of the old adhesive are gone. 1) Wet the wiper by pouring the solvent onto the wiper, not by dipping the wiper into the solvent source. (c) Remove excess solvent with a clean cotton wiper, G00034. (d) Do a final cleaning of the surfaces with a cotton wiper, G00034, wet with alcohol, B00130. (e) Immediately wipe all cleaned surfaces with a new cotton wiper, G00034, until all alcohol is removed from the surfaces. (f) Put on clean protective gloves, G50140, and avoid contact with the cleaned surfaces. SUBTASK 21-23-04-390-001 (2) Apply the sealant to the faying surfaces on the elbow duct [10] and transition duct [12] as follows: (a) Prime the surfaces as follows: EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Do not thin the primer or use primer that is cloudy or milky. 2) Brush or spray the surfaces with a thin coat of red or clear PR-1200 primer, C00580, or PR 1204 primer, A50126. 3) Allow the primer to dry at 82.5 ±17.5°F (28.1 ±9.8°C) for a minimum of 30 minutes and 4 hours maximum. (b) Apply a continuous layer of adhesive, A00027, over both surfaces to be bonded. NOTE: The inside bottom surface of the transition duct and the outside top surface of the elbow duct are the bonding surfaces. (c) Install the transition duct [12] over the elbow duct [10] as soon as possible after the application of the adhesive. (d) Install the four washers [9] and screws [8]. (e) Allow the adhesive to cure for a minimum of 24 hours at 82.5 ±17.5°F (28.1 ±9.8°C). SUBTASK 21-23-04-210-001 (3) Make sure that the bottom of the transition duct [12] is approximately 8 in. F. Sidewall Riser Ducts Post-Installation Test

SUBTASK 21-23-04-860-003 (1) Supply conditioned air to the passenger cabin (TASK 21-00-00-800-801). SUBTASK 21-23-04-790-001 (2) Make sure that there are no leaks in the sidewall riser ducts as follows: (a) Do a check for leaks at all the joints in the sidewall risers. (b) A leak exists if airflow can be felt on a hand a minimum of 2 in. (5 cm) away from a joint or surface. (c) Make sure that there is no whistling, vibration or other excessive air noise from the riser ducts. (d) Repair any leaks that are found. SUBTASK 21-23-04-860-004 (3) Remove the conditioned air from the airplane (TASK 21-00-00-800-802).

G. Sidewall Diffuser Orifice Cleaning

SUBTASK 21-23-07-100-001 (1) Clean the sidewall diffuser [3] as follows: (a) Disconnect the flexible duct [2] from the sidewall diffuser [3]. 1) Remove the adjustable plastic strap. (b) Clean the orifice [1] with the stiff bristle brush, STD-133. 1) If it is necessary, vacuum the debris with vacuum cleaner, STD-183. Reference Description STD-858 Tag - DO NOT OPERATE STD-6435 Respirator - Particulate (Meets NIOSH 42 CFR 84 Class N95, EN149 Class FFP2, or Better) STD-6437 Goggles - Safety, Non Vented STD-6439 Coveralls - Hooded

C. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification B00130 Alcohol - Isopropyl TT-I-735 B50280 Cleaner - Disinfectant - Zip-Chem Products Calla 1452 BAC5150 B50364 Cleaner - Disinfectant - Matrix #3 BAC5150 G00624 Bag - Plastic, General Purpose G50140 Gloves - Protective, Latex or Nitrile

D. Location Zones

Zone Area 126 Air Conditioning Distribution Bay - Right 212 Flight Compartment - Right

E. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 21-25-01-860-003 (1) Put the L RECIRC FAN and the R RECIRC FAN switches, on the P5-10 panel, to the OFF position and install the DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-25-01-865-001 (2) To prevent accidental recirculation fan operation during the removal of the recirculation filter, open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-3 Row Col Number Name E 7 C00911 A/C RECIRC FAN LEFT CABIN AIR E 9 C01156 A/C RECIRC FAN LEFT CONT F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name E 2 C01023 A/C RECIRC FAN RIGHT CONT. E 4 C00884 AC RECIRC FAN RIGHT CABIN AIR SUBTASK 21-25-01-010-001 (3) Open the forward cargo compartment door. SUBTASK 21-25-01-010-006 (4) Remove the left and right aft bulkhead liners in the forward cargo compartment (TASK 25-52-17-000-801). SUBTASK 21-25-01-941-001 WARNING PUT ON THE PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT BEFORE YOU TOUCH THE FILTER. THE FILTER REMOVES SMALL PARTICLES (SMOKE, DUST, LINT, FIBERS, POLLEN) AND INFECTIOUS MATERIALS (BACTERIA, VIRUSES, MOLD SPORES, FUNGI) FROM THE AIR WHICH CAN CAUSE ILLNESSES AND INJURIES TO PERSONS. (5) Before you touch the filter, put on the personal protective equipment listed below: (a) hooded coveralls, STD-6439 (b) safety goggles, STD-6437 (c) particulate respirator, STD-6435 (d) protective gloves, G50140. SUBTASK 21-25-01-500-001 (6) The plastic bag, G00624, must be larger than the filter dimensions of 20 in. (51 cm) in length, 20 in. (51 cm) in width, 5.5 in. (14 cm) in height and tape suitable for sealing the bag closed.

F. Recirculation Air Filter Removal

SUBTASK 21-25-01-020-011 (1) Remove the left recirculation air filter [3]. (a) Remove the screws [6] from the retainer [7] on the filter housing [8]. (b) Remove the retainer [7] from the filter housing [8]. WARNING DO NOT LET THE FILTER TOUCH YOUR SKIN. DO NOT SHAKE OR HIT THE FILTER. DO NOT LET THE FILTER FALL. DO NOT USE COMPRESSED AIR TO CLEAN THE FILTER OR FILTER HOUSING. THIS CAN CAUSE THE INFECTIOUS MATERIAL TO BECOME AIRBORNE. DISCARD THE FILTER IN A PLASTIC DISPOSAL BAG. OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. EFFECTIVITY ALL (WARNING PRECEDES) CAUTION DO NOT LET THE RECIRCULATION FILTER TOUCH THE WIRE BUNDLE THAT IS IMMEDIATELY FORWARD OF THE FILTER. THE FORWARD AND AFT LOWER OUTBOARD CORNERS OF THE FILTER HAVE SHARP EDGES. THE SHARP EDGES CAN CUT THE INSULATION ON THE WIRE BUNDLE. (c) If possible, slide the plastic bag, G00624, over the filter when removing the recirculation air filter [3] from the filter housing [8] to minimize contamination. (d) Seal the bag closed with tape. WARNING OBEY THE AIRLINE POLICY, LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT, AND LAW ENFORCEMENT REGULATIONS WHEN YOU DISCARD THIS MATERIAL. OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (e) Discard the bag with the filter. Refer to the airline, local health, safety and regulatory procedures for disposal of material. SUBTASK 21-25-01-020-012 (2) Remove the right recirculation air filter [3]. (a) Release the quarter-turn fasteners [1] which attach the access panel [2] to the filter housing [4]. (b) Remove the access panel [2]. WARNING DO NOT LET THE FILTER TOUCH YOUR SKIN. DO NOT SHAKE OR HIT THE FILTER. DO NOT LET THE FILTER FALL. DO NOT USE COMPRESSED AIR TO CLEAN THE FILTER OR FILTER HOUSING. THIS CAN CAUSE THE INFECTIOUS MATERIAL TO BECOME AIRBORNE. DISCARD THE FILTER IN A PLASTIC DISPOSAL BAG. OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (c) If possible, slide the plastic bag, G00624, over the filter when removing the recirculation air filter [3] from the filter housing [4] to minimize contamination. (d) Seal the bag closed with tape. WARNING OBEY THE AIRLINE POLICY, LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT, AND LAW ENFORCEMENT REGULATIONS WHEN YOU DISCARD THIS MATERIAL. OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (e) Discard the bag with the filter. Refer to the airline, local health, safety and regulatory procedures for disposal of material. EFFECTIVITY ALL

G. Post-Filter Removal Cleanup

SUBTASK 21-25-01-670-003 WARNING ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL IS POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE. USE PROTECTION EQUIPMENT. MAKE SURE THAT YOU USE ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL IN AN AREA WITH AIRFLOW. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. (1) Disinfect hard non-porous surfaces near the filter with a solution of alcohol, B00130, Calla 1452 cleaner, B50280, or Matrix #3 cleaner, B50364. NOTE: Follow the disinfectant manufacturer's instruction and refer to the EPA List N for applicable contact/dwell time. NOTE: Refer to the EPA List N or local health authority guidance for required contact/dwell time for Isopropyl Alcohol to be used as a disinfectant. SUBTASK 21-25-01-670-001 (2) Disinfect all tools used for filter replacement. Refer to the airline procedures and policies for the disinfecting of tools. SUBTASK 21-25-01-020-020 WARNING DISCARD ALL PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT AFTER YOU USE IT ONE TIME. DO NOT TRY TO CLEAN IT. DISCARD THE EQUIPMENT IN A PLASTIC DISPOSAL BAG. OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (3) Remove the personal protective equipment and put them in a plastic bag, G00624. (a) Seal the bag closed with tape. WARNING OBEY THE AIRLINE POLICY, LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT, AND LAW ENFORCEMENT REGULATIONS WHEN YOU DISCARD THIS MATERIAL. OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (b) Discard the bag with the personal protective equipment. Refer to the airline, local health, safety and regulatory procedures for disposal of material. SUBTASK 21-25-01-110-001 WARNING CLEAN YOUR HANDS WITH SOAP AND FLUSH WITH HOT WATER. DIRTY HANDS WITH CONTAMINATION CAN CAUSE DISEASE AND ILLNESSES TO PERSONS. (4) Clean your hands with soap and running hot water.

E. Recirculation Air Filter Installation

SUBTASK 21-25-01-420-007 (1) Install the left recirculation air filter [3]. (a) Make sure that there is no unwanted material or contamination in the filter housing [8] which could cause damage to the recirculation fan. CAUTION DO NOT LET THE RECIRCULATION FILTER TOUCH THE WIRE BUNDLE THAT IS IMMEDIATELY FORWARD OF THE FILTER. THE FORWARD AND AFT LOWER OUTBOARD CORNERS OF THE FILTER HAVE SHARP EDGES. THE SHARP EDGES CAN CUT THE INSULATION ON THE WIRE BUNDLE. (b) Put the new recirculation air filter [3] in the filter housing [8]. (c) Check the spring clips. 1) Make sure that the spring clips apply pressure to keep the filter in position. 2) Make sure that all spring clips are installed and not damaged. (d) Hold the retainer [7] in its position on the filter housing [8]. (e) Install the screws [6] for the retainer [7] on the filter housing [8]. SUBTASK 21-25-01-420-008 (2) Install the right recirculation air filter [3]. (a) Make sure that there is no unwanted material or contamination in the filter housing [4] which could cause damage to the recirculation fan. EFFECTIVITY ALL CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE AFT SPRING CLIPS OF THE RECIRCULATION AIR FILTER ARE IN TIGHT CONTACT WITH THE FILTER RAIL. IF THE AFT SPRING CLIPS ARE NOT IN THE CORRECT POSITION, THEN THE FLOATING SPRING CLIPS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE RECIRCULATION FAN AND FILTER HOUSING DURING INSTALLATION. (b) Put the new recirculation air filter [3] in the filter housing [4]. (c) Check the spring clips. 1) Make sure that the spring clips apply pressure to keep the filter in position. 2) Make sure that all spring clips are installed and not damaged. (d) Put the access panel [2] in its position and turn the quarter-turn fastener [1] to attach the access panel [2] to the filter housing [4].

SUBTASK 21-25-01-410-003 (2) Close the forward cargo compartment door. SUBTASK 21-25-01-865-002 (3) To restore recirculation fan operation after installation of the recirculation filter, remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-3 Row Col Number Name E 7 C00911 A/C RECIRC FAN LEFT CABIN AIR E 9 C01156 A/C RECIRC FAN LEFT CONT F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name E 2 C01023 A/C RECIRC FAN RIGHT CONT. E 4 C00884 AC RECIRC FAN RIGHT CABIN AIR SUBTASK 21-25-01-860-007 (4) Put the L RECIRC FAN and R RECIRC FAN switches in the AUTO position and remove the DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858.

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 125 Air Conditioning Distribution Bay - Left 126 Air Conditioning Distribution Bay - Right

SUBTASK 21-25-03-020-004 (1) Remove the recirculation fan check valve, do this task: Recirculation Fan Check Valve Removal, TASK 21-25-03-000-801.

E. Recirculation Fan Check Valve Inspection

SUBTASK 21-25-03-210-002 (1) Examine the recirculation fan check valve as follows: (a) Use your finger or a pencil to push on each flapper to open them. (b) Make sure that each flapper opens freely and moves smoothly to the stop tube. (c) Make sure that each flapper closes smoothly and touches fully on the face of the check valve body. (d) Make sure that there is no damage to the flappers: 1) Measure the thickness of the area on the flappers where the flappers contact the stop tube. 2) Make sure that the stop-tube contact area on the flappers is a minimum of 0.020 in. (0.508 mm) thick. a) Measure with a micrometer, STD-595, a vernier caliper (0 - 6 inch, readable to 1/1000 inch), STD-1097, or an equivalent tool. 3) Repair or replace check valves that do not meet the minimum thickness. (e) Make sure that there is no corrosion or lint on the flappers or the hinge pin. EFFECTIVITY ALL

F. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 21-25-03-420-003 (1) Install the recirculation fan check valve, do this task: Recirculation Fan Check Valve Installation, TASK 21-25-03-400-801.

C. Galley Ceiling Ventilation Grill Cleaning

SUBTASK 21-26-03-100-001 (1) Do these steps to clean the ventilation grill: (a) Prepare a cleaning solution of a general purpose household detergent cleaner, B00541 diluted with water in accordance with the instructions on the detergent container. (b) Clean the grill with a cotton wiper cotton wiper, G00034 that is moist with the cleaning solution. (c) If the cotton wiper, G00034 with the cleaning solution did not remove all dirt deposits or contamination from the grill, clean the grill with a cotton wiper, G00034 that is moist with alcohol, B00130. (d) Flush the grill with clean water until all traces of the detergent solution or alcohol are removed. (e) Dry the grill with a dry, clean cotton wiper, G00034.

SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-370 CAUTION OBEY THE SPECIFIED TIME LIMIT. IF YOU IGNORE THE TIME LIMIT, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT WILL OCCUR. (1) Make sure if you operate the electrical/electronic equipment in the electrical/electronic equipment bay that you close the fan circuit breaker in less than 5 minutes after you open it. NOTE: Electrical/electronic equipment can become too hot. EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name D 1 C01444 A/C OVERBOARD EXHAUST VALVE CONT D 2 C01445 A/C OVERBOARD EXH VALVE RECONFIG CONT (b) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door WARNING WHEN YOU OPEN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS, MAKE SURE THAT THE OUTER DOOR STAYS AS OPEN AS POSSIBLE. IF THE OUTER DOOR TURNS IN, THE ATTACHED DOOR COMPONENTS COULD TOUCH THE INNER DOOR COMPONENTS. THIS CAN CAUSE AN ARC CONDITION WHEN YOU SUPPLY POWER. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE CONDUCTORS IN THE P91 AND P92 PANELS. BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU GET ACCESS TO THE CIRCUIT BREAKERS ON THE INNER SIDE OF THE P91 AND P92 PANELS (ROW F). IF IT IS POSSIBLE, REMOVE AIRPLANE ELECTRICAL POWER FIRST. THE P91 AND P92 PANELS HAVE HIGH VOLTAGES AND CURRENTS. ELECTRICAL VOLTAGE AND CURRENT CAN KILL YOU OR CAUSE INJURIES. (c) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: Power Distribution Panel Number 1, P91 Row Col Number Name A 8 C00935 EQPT CLG SPLY FAN PWR-ALTN E 1 C00836 EQPT CLG EXH FAN PWR-NORM Power Distribution Panel Number 2, P92 Row Col Number Name 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103 A 8 C00934 EQPT CLG SPLY FAN PWR-NORM A 10 C00837 EQPT CLG EXH FAN PWR-ALTN 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 D 10 C00934 EQPT CLG SPLY FAN PWR-NORM D 12 C00837 EQPT CLG EXH FAN PWR-ALTN ALL (d) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door

F. Equipment Cooling System Tryout

NOTE: This tryout is to make sure these components in the equipment cooling system are in a zero energy state. • Equipment Cooling Supply Fan EFFECTIVITY ALL • Equipment Cooling Exhaust Fan • Equipment Cooling Overboard Exhaust Valve NOTE: Wait a minimum of 60 seconds after deactivation before you do the tryout steps. SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-371 (1) For the equipment cooling supply and exhaust fans, do these steps: (a) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811. (b) Make sure that the EQUIP COOLING SUPPLY switch on the equipment cooling panel is in the NORM position. (c) Make sure that the EQUIP COOLING EXHAUST switch on the equipment cooling panel is in the NORM position. (d) Make sure that the EQUIP COOLING SUPPLY OFF light is on. (e) Make sure that the EQUIP COOLING EXHAUST OFF light is on. (f) Put the EQUIP COOLING SUPPLY switch in the ALTN position. (g) Put the EQUIP COOLING EXHAUST switch in the ALTN position. (h) Wait a minimum of 60 seconds. (i) Make sure that the EQUIP COOLING SUPPLY OFF light is on. (j) Make sure that the EQUIP COOLING EXHAUST OFF light is on. (k) Do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812. SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-372 (2) For the equipment cooling overboard exhaust valve, do these steps: (a) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811. (b) Do this task: Supply Conditioned Air with a Cooling Pack, TASK 21-00-00-800-803. (c) Make sure that these switches, on the P5-10 Air Conditioning Panel, are in the AUTO position: 1) L RECIRC FAN 2) R RECIRC FAN (d) Make sure that these switches, on the P5 Overhead Panel, are in the NORM position: 1) EQUIP COOLING, EXHAUST 2) EQUIP COOLING, SUPPLY WARNING OBEY THE PROCEDURE THAT PUTS THE AIRPLANE IN THE AIR MODE. IF YOU DO THE PROCEDURE INCORRECTLY, INJURIES TO PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (e) Do this task: Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-801. 21-27-00-720-802Equipment Cooling - Functional TestPDF p. 519

5. Equipment Cooling - Functional Test (Figure 502)

A. General

(1) This task does a functional test of the equipment cooling. The exhaust cooling system pressures (measured in inches of water) are recorded at different locations. This test will find the minimum static pressure for the test ports.

B. Tools/Equipment

NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional. Reference Description COM-4917 Fitting - Hose, Barbed Brass Part #: 707002-0202 Supplier: 25795 COM-10778 Meter - Pressure/Vacuum Part #: 220-2PSI Supplier: 0UJL0 COM-11876 Static pressure probe - 1/8 inch diameter Part #: A-302 Supplier: 85274 SPL-11929 Probe - Needle, E/E Cooling Part #: B21006-1 Supplier: 81205 STD-11875 1/8 inch ID plastic tubing

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 117 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Left 118 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Right 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

D. Access Panels

Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door

E. Prepare for the Functional Test

SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-450 (1) Open the following DISPLAY circuit breakers on the P6-1 panel: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name D 9 C01362 DISPLAY DEU 2 HOLDUP D 10 C01361 DISPLAY DEU 1 HOLDUP D 11 C01360 DISPLAY DEU 2 PRI 378-999 D 12 C01936 ATTENDANT PANELS ALL E 10 C01364 DISPLAY F/O OUTBD E 11 C01366 DISPLAY F/O INBD EFFECTIVITY ALL (Continued) F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-1 Row Col Number Name E 12 C01373 DISPLAY CTR LWR SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-452 (2) Open the following DISPLAY circuit breakers on the P18-2 panel: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name 507-999; 013, 014 POST SB 737-34-2379 A 7 C01238 FMCS MCDU 1 ALL D 2 C01372 DISPLAY CTR UPR D 3 C01365 DISPLAY CAPT INBD D 4 C01363 DISPLAY CAPT OUTBD D 5 C01359 DISPLAY DEU 1 PRI SUBTASK 21-27-00-010-017 (3) Get access to the Electrical / Electronic (E/E) bay. (a) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door

F. Equipment Cooling - Functional Test

SUBTASK 21-27-00-700-005 (1) Before you do the test: (a) Make sure that there are no missing electrical boxes from the equipment bay racks. (b) Make sure that all empty locations on the equipment bay racks have blanking plugs installed. SUBTASK 21-27-00-780-001 (2) Measure the exhaust cooling system pressures at the locations shown in the table below: (a) Make sure that the EQUIP COOLING SUPPLY switch, on the equipment cooling panel, is in the alternate position. (b) To measure the pressure at the P92 Power Distribution Panel (PDP) test point location, do these steps: 1) Connect the pressure/vacuum meter, COM-10778 to the needle probe, SPL-11929. 2) Put the needle probe, SPL-11929, through the flex hose located below the PDP to a depth of approx. 1.25 in. (3.18 cm). a) Turn the probe to get the maximum indication of the pressure 3) Use the pressure/vacuum meter, COM-10778, to record the pressure value. (c) For other test point locations, do these steps: 1) Use the barbed brass hose fitting, COM-4917 to connect the tube, STD-11875, to the pressure/vacuum meter, COM-10778. 2) Connect the probe, COM-11876, to the other end of the tube, STD-11875. 3) Put the probe, COM-11876, through the test port locations. EFFECTIVITY ALL 4) Use the pressure/vacuum meter, COM-10778, to record the pressure value. (d) For the E5-2 shelf pressure, put the probe, COM-11876, through one of the 3/8 inch diameter plenum holes at the bottom of the shelf. (b) To measure the pressure at the P92 PDP test point location, do these steps: 1) Connect the pressure/vacuum meter, COM-10778 to the needle probe, SPL-11929. 2) Put the needle probe, SPL-11929, through the flex hose located below the PDP to a depth of approx. 1.25 in. (3.18 cm). a) Turn the probe to get the maximum indication of the pressure 3) Use the pressure/vacuum meter, COM-10778, to record the pressure value. 9. Equipment Cooling Overboard Exhaust Valve Smoke Clearance Mode - Operational Test (Figure 501)

A. General

(1) This task does a test of the equipment cooling overboard exhaust valve in the smoke removal mode. (2) When persons are in the airplane during this test, they must be in good physical condition. When a person feels pain during a pressure change, you must make the pressure stable immediately or it must be lowered. Do this until the person can make the pressure equal in their ears, or be removed from the airplane.

B. References

Reference Title 21-00-00-800-804 Remove Conditioned Air Supplied by a Cooling Pack (P/B 201) 24-22-00-860-811 Supply Electrical Power (P/B 201) 24-22-00-860-812 Remove Electrical Power (P/B 201) 27-51-00-860-803 Extend the Trailing Edge Flaps (P/B 201) 27-51-00-860-804 Retract the Trailing Edge Flaps (P/B 201) 32-09-00-860-801 Put the Airplane in the Air Mode (P/B 201) 32-09-00-860-802 Return the Airplane to the Ground Mode (P/B 201) 36-00-00-860-801 Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System (Selection) (P/B 201)

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-044 (1) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811. SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-215 (2) Extend the trailing edge flaps to position 1. To extend the flaps, do this task: Extend the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-803. SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-082 WARNING OBEY THE PROCEDURE THAT PUTS THE AIRPLANE IN THE AIR MODE. IF YOU DO THE PROCEDURE INCORRECTLY, INJURIES TO PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (3) Do this task: Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-801. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-045 WARNING MAKE SURE YOU OBEY THE PROPER PROCEDURES FOR COMPRESSION AND DECOMPRESSION WHEN YOU USE PERSONS IN A PRESSURIZED AREA. PRESSURE CHANGES THAT CAUSE PAIN MUST NOT BE DONE. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY THE PRECAUTIONS, INJURY TO PERSONS CAN OCCUR. (4) Do these steps to pressurize the airplane cabin to 2.0 Psi (13.79 kPa) differential pressure: (a) Close all exterior doors. (b) Make sure that the flight compartment sliding windows are closed. (c) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System (Selection), TASK 36-00-00-860-801. (d) Set the L PACK and R PACK switches on the P5-10 air conditioning panel to the AUTO position. (e) Set the R RECIRC FAN switch on the P5-10 air conditioning panel to the AUTO position. (f) Set the CONT CAB, FWD CAB and AFT CAB temperature selectors on the P5-17 cabin temperature control panel to the AUTO position. (g) Put the Cabin Pressurization Switch on the Cabin Pressure Control Panel to the MAN position. (h) Begin to close the cabin pressurization outflow valve with the cabin pressurization valve OPEN and CLOSE switch on the Cabin Pressure Control Panel: 1) Look at the VALVE position indicator to see the position of the valve. WARNING DO NOT ALLOW THE INDICATION ON THE CABIN CLIMB GAUGE TO SHOW MORE THAN 1000 FEET PER MINUTE. WHEN YOU ALLOW A RATE OF CABIN CLIMB OF MORE THAN 1000 FEET PER MINUTE, DAMAGE TO THE AIRPLANE STRUCTURE OR INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. (i) Slowly increase the cabin pressure with the OPEN/CLOSE toggle switch on the P5-6 panel so that the indication on the CABIN CLIMB gauge shows a rate of approximately 300 feet per minute. 1) Do not change the cabin pressure at a rate of more than 1000 feet per minute. (j) Increase the cabin pressure until the cabin DIFF PRESS indicator on the Cabin Pressure Control Panel shows a differential pressure of 2.0 psi (13.79 kPa). SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-083 (5) Make sure that the L PACK and R PACK switches on the P5-10 Air Conditioning Panel are in the AUTO position. SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-084 (6) Make sure that the R RECIRC FAN switch, on the P5-10 Air Conditioning Panel, is in the AUTO position. SUBTASK 21-27-00-710-020 (7) Make sure that there is no air flow out of the equipment cooling overboard exhaust valve port: (a) Put your hand at the valve exhaust port on the bottom of the airplane to feel for airflow. NOTE: The exhaust port is just aft of the E/E bay access door. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-096 WARNING DO NOT ALLOW THE INDICATION ON THE CABIN CLIMB GAUGE TO SHOW MORE THAN 1000 FEET PER MINUTE. WHEN YOU ALLOW A RATE OF CABIN CLIMB OF MORE THAN 1000 FEET PER MINUTE, DAMAGE TO THE AIRPLANE STRUCTURE OR INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. (8) Put the L PACK switch to HIGH. NOTE: The cabin pressure can increase at more than 1000 feet per minute when the pack is in the high flow mode. Manually opening the outflow valve will reduce the rate of cabin pressurization. (a) If necessary, operate the OPEN-CLOSE toggle switch on the P5-6 pressurization control panel so that the CABIN CLIMB indication on the P5-16 cabin altitude and rate of climb panel does not exceed 1000 feet per minute. SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-181 (9) Put the R PACK switch to OFF. SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-170 (10) Put the R RECIRC FAN switch to the OFF position. SUBTASK 21-27-00-710-025 (11) Make sure that there is air flow out of the equipment cooling overboard exhaust valve port. NOTE: The CABIN CLIMB indication on the P5-16 cabin altitude and rate of climb panel will indicate that the cabin pressure is climbing. SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-182 WARNING DO NOT ALLOW THE INDICATION ON THE CABIN CLIMB GAUGE TO SHOW MORE THAN 1000 FEET PER MINUTE. WHEN YOU ALLOW A RATE OF CABIN CLIMB OF MORE THAN 1000 FEET PER MINUTE, DAMAGE TO THE AIRPLANE STRUCTURE OR INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. (12) Put the R PACK switch to HIGH. NOTE: The cabin pressure can increase at more than 1000 feet per minute when the pack is in the high flow mode. Manually opening the outflow valve will reduce the rate of cabin pressurization. (a) If necessary, operate the MANUAL OPEN-CLOSE switch on the P5-6 pressurization control panel so that the CABIN CLIMB indication on the P5-16 cabin altitude and rate of climb panel does not exceed 1000 feet per minute. SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-183 (13) Put the L PACK switch to OFF. SUBTASK 21-27-00-710-040 (14) Make sure that there is airflow out of the equipment cooling overboard exhaust valve port. NOTE: The CABIN CLIMB indication on the P5-16 cabin altitude and rate of climb panel will indicate that the cabin pressure is climbing.

21-27-00-700-807Smoke Clearance Mode - Operational TestPDF p. 536

10. Smoke Clearance Mode - Operational Test NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. General

(1) This task does an operational test of the equipment cooling overboard exhaust valve. The interfaces of the exhaust fans, supply fans, recirculation fans, and smoke detection system with the overboard exhaust valve system are also tested. (2) The equipment cooling overboard exhaust valve will be referred to by the acronym OEV in this test. 043, 044, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 056-063, 067-078, 081 POST SB 737-26A1122 (3) In the event of a forward cargo fire, the cargo smoke detectors will detect smoke and annunciate to the flight crew of the forward cargo fire. The flight crew will then take the appropriate action for smoke clearance from the flight deck which results in the following: (a) Power to the E/E cooling supply normal and alternate fans is removed for 5 minutes (b) The E/E cooling supply low flow sensor warning is inhibited for 5 minutes (c) The OEV opens to the SMOKE position for the duration of the flight (d) Power to the E/E cooling exhaust normal and alternate fans is removed for the duration of the flight (e) The E/E cooling exhaust low flow sensor warning is inhibited for the duration of the flight. ALL

SUBTASK 21-27-00-860-377 (1) If the operational test is not satisfactory, do a system fault isolation as follows: (a) For the left or right recirculating fan, refer to FIM 21-25 TASK 802. (b) For the alternate exhaust fan, M99, refer to FIM 21-27 TASK 805. (c) For the normal exhaust fan, M98, see: FIM 21-27 TASK 806. (d) For the alternate supply fan, M1323, refer to FIM 21-27 TASK 807. (e) For the normal supply fan, M1322, refer to FIM 21-27 TASK 808. (f) For the OEV, refer to FIM 21-27 TASK 809. 043, 044, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 056-063, 067-078, 081 POST SB 737-26A1122 (g) If the supply fans do not shut off when commanded, refer to FIM 21-27 TASK 810. (h) If the exhaust fans do not shut off when commanded, refer to FIM 21-27 TASK 811. ALL (2) Do the operational test again until the test is satisfactory.

ATA 21-27-01

2 tasks
21-27-01-000-801Equipment Cooling Air Filter RemovalPDF p. 549

2. Equipment Cooling Air Filter Removal (Figure 401) NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. General

(1) You must remove electrical power from the airplane before you remove an equipment cooling air filter. This will make sure the electrical/electronic equipment does not receive electrical power when the equipment cooling system is not in operation.

B. References

Reference Title 24-22-00-860-812 Remove Electrical Power (P/B 201) 25-52-16-000-801 Forward Cargo Compartment Forward Bulkhead Liner - Removal (P/B 401) 52-31-00-580-801 Open the Cargo Door (P/B 201) 52-31-00-580-802 Close the Cargo Door (P/B 201)

C. Tools/Equipment

Reference Description STD-6435 Respirator - Particulate (Meets NIOSH 42 CFR 84 Class N95, EN149 Class FFP2, or Better) STD-6437 Goggles - Safety, Non Vented STD-6439 Coveralls - Hooded

D. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification B00130 Alcohol - Isopropyl TT-I-735 B50280 Cleaner - Disinfectant - Zip-Chem Products Calla 1452 BAC5150 B50364 Cleaner - Disinfectant - Matrix #3 BAC5150 G00624 Bag - Plastic, General Purpose G50140 Gloves - Protective, Latex or Nitrile

E. Location Zones

Zone Area 118 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Right 122 Forward Cargo Compartment - Right EFFECTIVITY ALL

F. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 21-27-01-860-001 CAUTION MAKE SURE YOU REMOVE ELECTRICAL POWER FROM THE AIRPLANE. IF YOU SUPPLY ELECTRICAL POWER TO THE ELECTRICAL/ELECTRONIC EQUIPMENT WHEN THE EQUIPMENT COOLING SYSTEM IS NOT IN OPERATION, THE ELECTRICAL/ELECTRONIC EQUIPMENT CAN BECOME TOO HOT. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ELECTRICAL/ELECTRONIC EQUIPMENT. (1) Do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812. SUBTASK 21-27-01-010-001 (2) Open the forward cargo compartment door (Open the Cargo Door, TASK 52-31-00-580-801). SUBTASK 21-27-01-010-002 (3) Remove the forward right bulkhead liner in the forward cargo compartment. To remove the liner, do this task: Forward Cargo Compartment Forward Bulkhead Liner - Removal, TASK 25-52-16-000-801. SUBTASK 21-27-01-940-001 WARNING PUT ON THE PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT BEFORE YOU TOUCH THE FILTER. THE FILTER REMOVES SMALL PARTICLES (SMOKE, DUST, LINT, FIBERS, POLLEN) AND INFECTIOUS MATERIALS (BACTERIA, VIRUSES, MOLD SPORES, FUNGI) FROM THE AIR WHICH CAN CAUSE ILLNESSES AND INJURIES TO PERSONS. (4) Before you touch the equipment cooling air filter [2] put on the following personal protective equipment listed below: (a) hooded coveralls, STD-6439 (b) safety goggles, STD-6437 (c) particulate respirator, STD-6435 (d) protective gloves, G50140 SUBTASK 21-27-01-500-001 (5) Select a plastic bag, G00624 larger than the filer and tape suitable for sealing the bag closed.

G. Equipment Cooling Air Filter Removal

SUBTASK 21-27-01-010-003 (1) If it is necessary, close the forward cargo compartment door (TASK 52-31-00-580-802). NOTE: The forward cargo compartment door can be lowered to provide access to remove the equipment cooling air filter. SUBTASK 21-27-01-020-001 (2) Release the latch assemblies [3] that are on the top and the bottom of the filter housing assembly [1]. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-27-01-020-002 WARNING DO NOT LET THE FILTER TOUCH YOUR SKIN. DO NOT SHAKE OR HIT THE FILTER. DO NOT LET THE FILTER FALL. DO NOT USE COMPRESSED AIR TO CLEAN THE FILTER OR FILTER HOUSING. THIS CAN CAUSE THE INFECTIOUS MATERIAL TO BECOME AIRBORNE. DISCARD THE FILTER IN A PLASTIC DISPOSAL BAG. OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (3) If possible, slide the plastic bag, G00624, over the filter when removing the equipment cooling air filter [2] from the filter housing assembly [1] to minimize contamination. Seal the bag closed with tape. SUBTASK 21-27-01-800-001 WARNING OBEY THE AIRLINE POLICY, LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT, AND LAW ENFORCEMENT REGULATIONS WHEN YOU DISCARD THIS MATERIAL. OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (4) Discard the bag with the filter. Refer to the airline, local, health, safety and regulatory procedures for disposal of material. SUBTASK 21-27-01-010-004 (5) If necessary, open the forward cargo compartment door (Open the Cargo Door, TASK 52-31-00-580-801).

H. Post-Filter Removal Cleanup

SUBTASK 21-27-01-670-002 WARNING ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL IS POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE. USE PROTECTION EQUIPMENT. MAKE SURE THAT YOU USE ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL IN AN AREA WITH AIRFLOW. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. (1) Disinfect hard non-porous surfaces near the filter with a solution of 70% alcohol, B00130, or Calla 1452 cleaner, B50280, or Matrix #3 cleaner, B50364. NOTE: Follow the disinfectant manufacturer's instruction and refer to the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) List N for applicable contact/dwell time. NOTE: Refer to the EPA List N or local health authority guidance for required contact/dwell time for Isopropyl Alcohol to be used as a disinfectant. SUBTASK 21-27-01-670-001 (2) Disinfect all tools used for filter replacement. Refer to the airline procedure and policies for the disinfecting of tools. SUBTASK 21-27-01-020-005 WARNING DISCARD ALL PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT AFTER YOU USE IT ONE TIME. DO NOT TRY TO CLEAN IT. DISCARD THE EQUIPMENT IN A PLASTIC DISPOSAL BAG. OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (3) Remove the personal protective equipment and put them in a plastic bag, G00624. Seal the bag closed with tape. EFFECTIVITY ALL WARNING OBEY THE AIRLINE POLICY, LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT, AND LAW ENFORCEMENT REGULATIONS WHEN YOU DISCARD THIS MATERIAL. OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (a) Discard the bag with the personal protective equipment. Refer to the airline, local health, safety and regulatory procedures for disposal of material. SUBTASK 21-27-01-110-001 WARNING CLEAN YOUR HANDS WITH SOAP AND FLUSH WITH HOT WATER. DIRTY HANDS WITH CONTAMINATION CAN CAUSE DISEASE AND ILLNESSES TO PERSONS. (4) Clean your hands with soap and running hot water.

IF YOU SUPPLY ELECTRICAL POWER TO THE ELECTRICAL/ELECTRONIC EQUIPMENT WHEN THE EQUIPMENT COOLING SYSTEM IS NOT IN OPERATION, THE ELECTRICAL/ELECTRONIC EQUIPMENT CAN BECOME TOO HOT. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ELECTRICAL/ELECTRONIC EQUIPMENT. (1) Do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812. (a) Make a record of the orientation of the electrical connector [6] so that you can install the equipment cooling supply fan [1] with the electrical connector [6] in the same position. SUBTASK 21-27-02-020-002 (2) For the normal equipment cooling supply fan [1], do these steps: 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224 (a) Remove the nut [5], washer [3], washer [10], and screw [2]. 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 (b) Remove the nut [5], washer [3], washer [11], washer [10], and screw [2]. ALL (c) Disconnect and stow the bonding jumper [4] and bonding jumper [9]. SUBTASK 21-27-02-020-005 (3) For the alternate equipment cooling supply fan [1], do these steps: 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224 (a) Remove the nut [5], washer [3], washer [10], and screw [2]. 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 (b) Remove the nut [5], washer [3], washer [11], washer [10], and screw [2]. ALL (c) Disconnect and stow the bonding jumper [9]. SUBTASK 21-27-02-020-003 (4) Loosen the clamps [7]. SUBTASK 21-27-02-020-004 (5) Remove the equipment cooling supply fan [1] and the sleeves [8]. SUBTASK 21-27-02-420-001 (1) Put the equipment cooling supply fan [1] and the sleeves [8] in their position. (a) Make sure that the fan impeller is aft of the fan check valve flappers so that the flow of air is in the correct direction. (b) Make sure that the electrical connector [6] is oriented the same as it was on the removed cooling supply fan [1]. SUBTASK 21-27-02-420-002 (2) Install the clamps [7]. (a) Tighten the clamps [7] to 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) - 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m). SUBTASK 21-27-02-420-003 (3) For the normal equipment cooling supply fan [1], do these steps: 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224 (a) Use cotton wiper, G00034, moist in solvent, B00184, to final clean the mating surfaces of the airplane structure, washer [10], bonding jumper [4], and bonding jumper [9]. (b) Install the screw [2], washer [10], bonding jumper [9], bonding jumper [4], washer [3], and nut [5]. 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 (c) Use cotton wiper, G00034, moist in solvent, B00184, to final clean the mating surfaces of the airplane structure, washer [10], washer [11], bonding jumper [4], and bonding jumper [9]. (d) Install the screw [2], washer [10], bonding jumper [9], washer [11], bonding jumper [4], washer [3], and nut [5]. ALL (e) Tighten the nut [5] to 35 in-lb (4.0 N·m) - 45 in-lb (5.1 N·m). (f) Measure the electrical resistance between the bonding jumper [4] and airplane structure (SWPM 20-20-00). 1) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. 2) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.01 ohm (10.0 milliohm) or less. SUBTASK 21-27-02-420-005 (4) For the alternate equipment cooling supply fan [1], do these steps: 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224 (a) Use cotton wiper, G00034, moist in solvent, B00184, to final clean the mating surfaces of the airplane structure, washer [10], and bonding jumper [9]. EFFECTIVITY ALL 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224 (Continued) (b) Install the screw [2], washer [10], bonding jumper [9], washer [3], and nut [5]. 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 (c) Use cotton wiper, G00034, moist in solvent, B00184, to final clean the mating surfaces of the airplane structure, washer [10], washer [11], and bonding jumper [9]. (d) Install the screw [2], washer [10], washer [11], bonding jumper [9], washer [3], and nut [5]. ALL (e) Tighten the nut [5] to 35 in-lb (4.0 N·m) - 45 in-lb (5.1 N·m). (f) Measure the electrical resistance between the bonding jumper [4] and airplane structure (SWPM 20-20-00). 1) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. 2) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.01 ohm (10.0 milliohm) or less. SUBTASK 21-27-02-420-004 (5) Connect the electrical connector [6] to the equipment cooling supply fan [1]. NOTE: If identifying location decals are on the equipment cooling supply fan, carefully remove the marker and relocate to ducting nearby to each location per approved standard maintenance practices (TASK 20-30-11-910-801).

H. Equipment Cooling Supply Fan Installation Test

SUBTASK 21-27-02-860-002 (1) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811. SUBTASK 21-27-02-710-001 (2) Do these steps if you installed the normal supply fan [1]: (a) Make sure that the EQUIP COOLING SUPPLY switch, on the equipment cooling panel, is in the NORMAL position. (b) Make sure that the normal fan operates. NOTE: Put your hand on the fan to feel that it operates. (c) Examine the fan connections for leaks. NOTE: If you find a leak you must repair it. SUBTASK 21-27-02-710-002 (3) Do these steps if you installed the alternate supply fan [1]: (a) Make sure that the EQUIP COOLING SUPPLY switch, on the equipment cooling panel, is in the ALTERNATE position. (b) Make sure that the alternate fan operates. NOTE: Put your hand on the fan to feel that it operates. (c) Examine the fan connections for leaks. NOTE: If you find a leak you must repair it. (d) Put the EQUIP COOLING SUPPLY switch on the Equipment Cooling Panel to the NORMAL position. EFFECTIVITY ALL

G. Equipment Cooling Exhaust Fan Installation

SUBTASK 21-27-04-420-001 (1) Put the equipment cooling exhaust fan [1] and sleeves [8] in their positions. (a) Make sure that the AIRFLOW arrow on the equipment cooling exhaust fan [1] is pointed to the inboard direction. (b) Make sure that the fan impeller is aft of the fan check valve flappers so that the flow of air is in the correct direction. (c) Make sure that the electrical connector is oriented the same it was on the removed equipment cooling exhaust fan [1]. SUBTASK 21-27-04-420-002 (2) Install the clamps [7] and tighten to 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) - 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m). SUBTASK 21-27-04-420-003 (3) For the normal equipment cooling exhaust fan [1], do these steps: (a) Use cotton wiper, G00034, moist in solvent, B00184, or alcohol, B00130, to clean the mating surfaces of the equipment cooling exhaust fan [1], washers [3], bonding jumper [4], and bonding jumper [9]. (b) Install the screw [2], washers [3], bonding jumper [4], bonding jumper [9], and nut [5]. (c) Tighten the nut [5] to 32 in-lb (3.6 N·m) - 38 in-lb (4.3 N·m). (d) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the bonding jumper [4], bonding jumper [9], and airplane structure (SWPM 20-20-00). 1) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. 2) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.01 ohm (10.0 milliohm) or less. SUBTASK 21-27-04-420-009 (4) For the alternate equipment cooling exhaust fan [1], do these steps: (a) Use cotton wiper, G00034, moist in solvent, B00184, or alcohol, B00130, to clean the mating surfaces of the equipment cooling exhaust fan [1], washers [3], and bonding jumper [4]. (b) Install the screw [2], washers [3], bonding jumper [4], and nut [5]. (c) Tighten the nut [5] to 32 in-lb (3.6 N·m) - 38 in-lb (4.3 N·m). (d) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the bonding jumper [4] and airplane structure (SWPM 20-20-00). 1) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. 2) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.01 ohm (10.0 milliohm) or less. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-27-04-420-004 (5) Connect the electrical connector [6] to the applicable equipment cooling exhaust fan [1]. NOTE: If identifying location decals are on the equipment cooling exhaust fan, carefully remove the marker and relocate to ducting nearby to each location per approved standard maintenance practices (TASK 20-30-11-910-801). (a) Make sure that the clearance between the electrical connectors [6] wiring and alternate equipment cooling exhaust fan [1] is 0.25 in. (6 mm) or more. 1) If the clearance is less than 0.25 in. (6 mm), do the following steps: a) Loosen the clamps [7] for the alternate equipment cooling exhaust fan [1]. b) Slightly rotate the alternate equipment cooling exhaust fan [1] axially to provide clearance of 0.25 in. (6 mm) or more. c) Tighten the clamps [7] to 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) - 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m).

H. Equipment Cooling Exhaust Fan Installation Test

SUBTASK 21-27-04-860-002 (1) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811. SUBTASK 21-27-04-710-001 (2) Do these steps if you installed the normal equipment cooling exhaust fan [1]: (a) Make sure that the EQUIP COOLING EXHAUST switch, on the equipment cooling panel, is in the NORM position. (b) Make sure that the normal equipment cooling exhaust fan [1] operates. NOTE: You can put your hand on the fan to feel that it operates. (c) Examine the fan connections for leaks. 1) If a leak is found, repair it. SUBTASK 21-27-04-710-002 (3) Do these steps if you installed the alternate equipment cooling exhaust fan [1]: (a) Make sure that the EQUIP COOLING EXHAUST switch, on the equipment cooling panel, is in the ALTN position. (b) Make sure that the alternate equipment cooling exhaust fan [1] operates. NOTE: You can put your hand on the fan to feel that it operates. (c) Examine the fan connections for leaks. 1) If a leak is found, repair it. (d) Put the EQUIP COOLING EXHAUST switch, on the equipment cooling panel, to the NORM position.

2. Equipment Cooling Exhaust Fan Cleaning Figure 21-27-04-990-801

A. General

(1) The equipment cooling exhaust fans may not operate correctly if they are dirty. (2) This procedure cleans only the impellers of the equipment cooling exhaust fans and the air passages. (3) You must do an overhaul of the equipment cooling exhaust fans if it is necessary to disassemble them for a more thorough cleaning. (4) This procedure is applicable for all of the fans in the equipment cooling system.

B. References

Reference Title 21-27-04-000-801 Equipment Cooling Exhaust Fan Removal (P/B 401) 21-27-04-400-801 Equipment Cooling Exhaust Fan Installation (P/B 401) 21-27-04-990-801 Figure: Equipment Cooling Exhaust Fan Installation (P/B 401)

Reference Description Specification B00039 Cleaner - Brulin Formula 815MX B00074 Solvent - Degreasing MIL-PRF-680 (Supersedes P-D-680)

E. Preparation for Cleaning

SUBTASK 21-27-04-020-005 (1) Remove the equipment cooling exhaust fan by following this procedure: (a) Equipment Cooling Exhaust Fan Removal, TASK 21-27-04-000-801 SUBTASK 21-27-04-930-001 (2) Make marks on the impellers so you can reinstall them in the same position they were in when you removed them. SUBTASK 21-27-04-030-001 (3) Remove the nut and washer at each impeller. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-27-04-020-006 (4) Move the impeller from side to side to remove it from the rotor shaft. NOTE: You can lightly hit the rotor shaft with a rubber mallet while you pull on the impeller to make it easy to remove.

F. Cleaning the Equipment Cooling Exhaust Fan

SUBTASK 21-27-04-160-001 (1) Soak the impellers in Brulin Formula 815MX cleaner, B00039 or solvent, B00074 until contamination loosens. NOTE: Use the solvent, B00074 if the Brulin Formula 815MX cleaner, B00039 does not completely clean the impellers. SUBTASK 21-27-04-160-002 (2) Remove the contamination with a soft bristle brush, STD-123. SUBTASK 21-27-04-160-003 CAUTION MAKE SURE TO DRY THE MOTOR FULLY WITH WARM AIR OR IN AN OVEN IF WATER GETS IN IT. IF THE MOTOR IS NOT FULLY DRIED BEFORE IT OPERATES, DAMAGE CAN OCCUR. (3) Flush the impellers fully with clean water if you used Brulin Formula 815MX cleaner, B00039. SUBTASK 21-27-04-160-004 (4) Dry the impellers with a soft cloth or with dry, compressed air. SUBTASK 21-27-04-420-005 (5) Install the keys and the impellers on the motor shaft. NOTE: Use the marks on the impellers to install them. SUBTASK 21-27-04-420-006 (6) Make sure the key is correctly engaged in each impeller. SUBTASK 21-27-04-420-007 (7) Install the washer and the self-locking nut. (a) Torque the nut to 40 in-lb (5 N·m) to 50 in-lb (6 N·m). SUBTASK 21-27-04-420-008 (8) Install the equipment cooling exhaust fan by following this procedure: (a) Equipment Cooling Exhaust Fan Installation, TASK 21-27-04-400-801

2. Pressurization System Manual Mode Test (Figure 501 or Figure 502) NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. General

(1) This task does an operational test of these components: (a) The outflow valve manual mode motor (b) The outflow valve selector panel (c) The outflow valve position indicator (d) The outflow valve feedback module for the outflow valve position indicator

B. References

Reference Title 24-22-00-860-811 Supply Electrical Power (P/B 201) 24-22-00-860-812 Remove Electrical Power (P/B 201)

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right

D. Prepare for the Test

SUBTASK 21-31-00-860-001 (1) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811. SUBTASK 21-31-00-860-002 (2) Make sure that these circuit breakers are closed: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 1 C01273 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL LCD LTG F 3 C01270 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 1 F 5 C01271 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL (Continued) F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL F 7 C01272 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL IND

E. Pressurization System Manual Mode Test

SUBTASK 21-31-00-860-003 CAUTION MAKE SURE ONE OF THE EXTERNALS DOORS OR WINDOWS IS OPEN BEFORE YOU CONTINUE WITH THE TEST. UNCONTROLLED PRESSURIZATION OF THE CABIN CAN OCCUR WHEN THE OUTFLOW VALVE IS CLOSED. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) Make sure at least one exterior door or window is open or that the L and R PACK switches on the P5 forward overhead panel are in the OFF position. SUBTASK 21-31-00-860-004 (2) Set the mode selector switch on the P5-6 cabin pressure control module to the MAN position. SUBTASK 21-31-00-710-001 (3) Make sure the MANUAL light on the P5-10 air conditioning module comes on. SUBTASK 21-31-00-860-005 (4) Set the LIGHTS switch on the P2 center instrument panel to DIM. SUBTASK 21-31-00-710-002 (5) Make sure the MANUAL light becomes dim. SUBTASK 21-31-00-860-006 (6) Set the LIGHTS switch on the P2 center instrument panel to BRT. SUBTASK 21-31-00-710-003 (7) Make sure the MANUAL light becomes bright. SUBTASK 21-31-00-710-004 (8) Push and hold the CLOSE/OPEN toggle switch on the pressure control module to the CLOSE position until the outflow valve is fully closed. SUBTASK 21-31-00-710-005 (9) Make sure the outflow valve is fully closed. SUBTASK 21-31-00-710-006 (10) Make sure the needle on the position indicator gage for the outflow valve is within approximately two needle widths of the fully closed mark. SUBTASK 21-31-00-710-007 (11) Push and hold the CLOSE/OPEN toggle switch on the pressure control module to the OPEN position until the outflow valve is fully open. SUBTASK 21-31-00-710-008 (12) Make sure the outflow valve is fully open. SUBTASK 21-31-00-710-009 (13) Make sure the needle on the position indicator gage for the outflow valve is within approximately two needle widths of the fully open mark. EFFECTIVITY ALL

F. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 21-31-00-860-037 (1) Make sure the mode selector switch on the cabin pressurization control panel, P5-6, is returned to the AUTO position. SUBTASK 21-31-00-860-007 (2) Do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812.

SUBTASK 21-31-00-860-009 (1) Put the mode selector switch on the P5-6 pressure control module to the AUTO position. SUBTASK 21-31-00-860-010 (2) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 3 C01270 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 1 SUBTASK 21-31-00-710-010 (3) Make sure that the AUTO FAIL and ALTN lights on the P5-10 air conditioning module come on in less than 5 seconds. E. Test the FLT ALT and LAND ALT Displays

SUBTASK 21-31-00-700-005 (1) Do these checks of the LCD segment displays on the cabin pressure control module: (a) Do this task: Master Dim and Test - Operational Test, TASK 33-18-00-710-802. (b) Make sure that all of the LCD segments (all eights) on the LAND ALT and FLT ALT displays come on for two seconds and then go off for one second again and again. SUBTASK 21-31-00-700-004 (2) Do a check of the cabin pressure control module LCD lighting: (a) Rotate the PANEL light control knob on the upper center section of the P5 forward overhead panel to the maximum BRIGHT position (fully clockwise). (b) Make sure that both the FLT ALT and LAND ALT displays increase in intensity. EFFECTIVITY ALL (c) Rotate the PANEL light control knob to the minimum BRIGHT position (fully counterclockwise). (d) Make sure that both the FLT ALT and LAND ALT displays decrease in intensity. SUBTASK 21-31-00-700-003 (3) Do this check of the displays of the altitude range settings in the FLT ALT and LAND ALT windows: (a) Set altitudes in the FLT ALT window from -1000 to 42000. (b) Make sure that all the digits are complete and clearly visible at each selection. (c) Set altitudes in the LAND ALT window from -1000 to 14000. (d) Make sure that all the digits are complete and clearly visible at each selection.

SUBTASK 21-31-01-910-002 CAUTION DO NOT TOUCH THE COMPONENT BEFORE YOU DO THE PROCEDURE FOR DEVICES THAT ARE SENSITIVE TO ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE. ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE COMPONENT. (1) Do the necessary steps to protect the pressure controller No. 1 [2] and pressure controller No. 2 [1] from electrostatic discharge. Do this task: ESDS Handling for Metal Encased Unit Installation, TASK 20-40-12-400-802. SUBTASK 21-31-01-420-002 (2) Make sure the shipping protection cap [2] is removed from the cabin pressure port on the faceplate of the controller. SUBTASK 21-31-01-020-002 CAUTION DO NOT TOUCH THE CONDUCTOR PINS OR OTHER CONDUCTORS ON THE COMPONENT. IF YOU TOUCH THESE CONDUCTORS, ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE COMPONENT. (3) Remove any protective caps or bags from the pressure controller No. 1 [2] and pressure controller No. 2 [1]. Do this task: Conductive Dust Cap and Connector Cover Removal, TASK 20-40-12-000-804. EFFECTIVITY ALL ALL; AIRPLANES WITH CABIN PRESSURE CONTROLLERS P/N 7121-19971-01AA/01AB/01AC/01BA SUBTASK 21-31-01-211-001 (4) Visually inspect the installed copper tape on the cabin pressure controller to determine if any of these conditions exist: (a) Abrasions to the copper tape at the corners of the front cover (b) Splitting/tearing of the copper tape at these locations: 1) Along the edges of the front cover at the juncture with the side covers 2) At the four corners of the front cover. (c) Disbonding/peeling of the copper tape away from the controller front cover (d) If any of the above conditions exist, replace all of the copper tape. SUBTASK 21-31-01-420-004 (5) Replace damaged copper tape as follows: (a) Remove all the installed tape. (b) Clean the surfaces to be taped as follows: 1) Use a cotton wiper, G00034 that is moist with solvent, B00062 or Limonene solvent, B00634 to clean the surface of tape residue. 2) Use a cotton wiper, G00034 to remove all traces of solvent from the surfaces to be taped until the surfaces are dry. (c) Install the 1-inch wide 3M 1181 copper foil tape, G50630 to the controller front cover and the interfacing controller sides as shown on Figure 401 or Figure 402 : 1) Make sure the tape overlaps the front cover of the controller a minimum of 1.5 mm and a maximum of 2.2 mm with the remainder of the tape applied to the sides of the controller. 2) Make sure the tape blocks all optical openings into the controller where the controller front cover interfaces with the sides of the controller. 3) Apply multiple layers of tape as necessary to make sure all openings into the controller are blocked: a) Make sure that all openings at the front cover corners are blocked. 4) Do not cover the BITE instruction label. SUBTASK 21-31-01-410-002 (6) If the Added Layer Of Protection (ALOP) tape is not installed on the cabin pressure controller do the following steps: NOTE: The additional tape layer should not replace the required copper tape. It is installed to protect the copper tape from damage. (a) Make sure the existing copper tape has been inspected and replaced as necessary. (b) Install the ALOP moisture barrier tape, G50179 or ALOP moisture barrier tape, G51207 over the copper tape on the four corners and edges of the cabin pressure controller front cover as shown on Figure 401 or Figure 402 . 1) Make sure the tape overlaps the front cover of the controller a minimum of 0.375 in. (9.525 mm) and maximum of 0.45 in. (11.43 mm) a) Trim the ALOP tape at the handle and BITE module. b) Make sure the ALOP tape overlaps the side of the BITE module. EFFECTIVITY ALL ALL; AIRPLANES WITH CABIN PRESSURE CONTROLLERS P/N 7121-19971-01AA/01AB/01AC/01BA (Continued) 2) Apply the remainder of the ALOP tape width to the sides of the cabin pressure controller. a) Make sure the ALOP overlaps the existing copper tape. 3) Do not cover the cooling holes on the sheet metal. (c) Make sure that the modification level sticker at the front is still readable. (d) Make sure that the bite instruction label is not covered with tape. ALL SUBTASK 21-31-01-420-001 ALL; AIRPLANES WITH CABIN PRESSURE CONTROLLERS P/N 7121-19971-01AA/01AB/01AC/01BA CAUTION REMOVE AND INSTALL THE PRESSURE CONTROLLER CAREFULLY TO PREVENT DAMAGE TO THE COPPER TAPE ON THE FRONT OF THE PRESSURE CONTROLLER. THE COPPER TAPE PREVENTS ELECTROMAGNETIC INTERFERENCE. IF YOU ARE NOT CAREFUL, DAMAGE TO THE COPPER TAPE WILL OCCUR. ALL (7) Install the cabin pressure controller No. 2 [1] or the cabin pressure controller No. 1 [2]. To install the controller, do this task: E/E Box Installation, TASK 20-10-07-400-801. SUBTASK 21-31-01-860-002 (8) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 3 C01270 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 1 F 5 C01271 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 2

SUBTASK 21-31-02-910-002 CAUTION DO NOT TOUCH THE COMPONENT BEFORE YOU DO THE PROCEDURE FOR DEVICES THAT ARE SENSITIVE TO ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE. ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE COMPONENT. (3) Before the cabin pressure control module [1] is touched, do this task: ESDS Handling for Metal Encased Unit Installation, TASK 20-40-12-400-802. SUBTASK 21-31-02-020-002 CAUTION DO NOT TOUCH THE CONDUCTOR PINS OR OTHER CONDUCTORS ON THE COMPONENT. IF YOU TOUCH THESE CONDUCTORS, ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE COMPONENT. (4) Remove the protective covers from the cabin pressure control module [1], do this task: Conductive Dust Cap and Connector Cover Removal, TASK 20-40-12-000-804. SUBTASK 21-31-02-420-001 (5) Install the P5-6 cabin pressure control module [1] into the P5 forward overhead panel as follows: (a) Put the cabin pressure control module [1] into the P5 forward overhead panel and hold it in position. (b) Turn the quarter-turn fasteners on the cabin pressure control module [1] to attach the module to the P5 forward overhead panel. (c) Connect the two electrical connectors to the cabin pressure control module [1]. SUBTASK 21-31-02-010-003 (6) Lift the P5 forward overhead panel to the closed position and turn the quarter-turn fasteners. SUBTASK 21-31-02-860-002 (7) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 1 C01273 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL LCD LTG F 3 C01270 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 1 F 5 C01271 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 2 F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL F 7 C01272 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL IND

E. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 21-31-03-860-001 WARNING DO NOT OPERATE THE OUTFLOW VALVE. INJURIES TO PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE VALVE GATES STAY FULLY CLOSED DURING TRANSPORTATION, REPAIR OR OVERHAUL. DAMAGE CAN OCCUR TO THE SEALS AND MOVABLE PARTS IF NOT PREPARED CORRECTLY. (1) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 3 C01270 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 1 F 5 C01271 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 2 F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-31-03-010-002 (2) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 822 Aft Cargo Door SUBTASK 21-31-03-010-003 (3) Do this task: Aft Cargo Compartment Aft Bulkhead Liner - Removal, TASK 25-52-19-000-801.

F. Outflow Valve Assembly Removal

ALL; OUTFLOW VALVES WITH JAGGED GATES SUBTASK 21-31-03-020-008 (1) Use care not to damage the antiskating foil on the forward and aft gates of the outflow valve when you reach through the opening of the valve to disconnect electrical connectors or other components (Figure 402). NOTE: The purpose of the antiskating foil is to help reduce any noise made by the air as it passes through the valve. ALL SUBTASK 21-31-03-020-001 (2) Disconnect these electrical connectors from the aft outflow valve [1]: NOTE: You can access the connectors through the valve door opening. (a) ELACT 1 electrical connector [3] (b) ELACT 2 electrical connector [2] (c) feedback module connector 1 [5] (d) feedback module connector 2 [6]. SUBTASK 21-31-03-020-002 (3) Remove the nut [7] and washer [8] that attach the bonding jumper [9] to the aft outflow valve [1]. SUBTASK 21-31-03-020-003 (4) Disconnect the bonding jumper [9] from the aft outflow valve [1]. SUBTASK 21-31-03-020-010 (5) Loosen the three aft screws [12] until the three aft lugs [11] can be turned. SUBTASK 21-31-03-020-009 (6) Turn the three aft lugs [11] so that they face inboard-to-outboard. SUBTASK 21-31-03-860-002 WARNING DO NOT PUT YOUR HANDS OR TOOLS IN THE OUTFLOW VALVE WHEN THE VALVE IS IN OPERATION. IF YOU PUT YOUR HANDS OR TOOLS IN THE OUTFLOW VALVE WHEN IT OPERATES YOU CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (7) Do these steps to position the aft outflow valve [1] gates so that the valve can be moved through the fuselage opening: EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL (b) Put the mode select switch on the cabin pressure control module, on the P5 overhead panel, to the MAN position. (c) Position the aft outflow valve [1] as follows: 1) Use the service interphone system to make sure that there is communication between the technician at the aft outflow valve location and the technician in the flight deck. 2) Push and hold the CLOSE/OPEN toggle switch, on the P5-6 pressure control module, to the CLOSE position until the technician at the aft outflow valve location states that the valve is approximately in the specified position (View B-B, Figure 401). SUBTASK 21-31-03-860-003 (8) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL SUBTASK 21-31-03-020-004 (9) Do these steps to remove the aft outflow valve [1]: CAUTION DO NOT APPLY TOO MUCH FORCE TO FORWARD ROW SCREWS AT THE AFT OUTFLOW VALVE AFTER THEY STOPPED. TOO MUCH FORCE APPLIED CAN CAUSE ROTATION OF THE LATCH LUGS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE AIRCRAFT STRUCTURE CAN OCCUR. (a) Turn the forward three screws [12] in the counterclockwise direction until they stop to release forward lugs [11] without their rotation. (b) Slowly push up and aft against the aft end of the aft outflow valve [1]. (c) Turn the aft outflow valve [1] as necessary until you can get to the manual motor electrical connector [4]. (d) Disconnect the manual motor electrical connector [4]. (e) Lift and turn the aft outflow valve [1] so that it is diagonal to the skin opening of the airplane and so that the valve motors are up. (f) Carefully remove the aft outflow valve [1] through the skin opening of the airplane. NOTE: Remove the aft outflow valve such that the valve motors come out last. (g) Remove the gasket [10]. ALL; OUTFLOW VALVES WITH JAGGED GATES SUBTASK 21-31-03-210-001 (10) Visually examine the condition of the antiskating foil on the forward and aft gates of the aft outflow valve [1] as follows (Figure 402): ALL (a) If the antiskating foil is missing, you may make a decision to do one of these actions: EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Remove any adhesive or dirt that remains on the valve gates and not replace the foil as the outflow valve is functionally serviceable with the antiskating foil missing. 2) Repair the antiskating foil per the vendor component maintenance manual at the next convenient maintenance opportunity. (b) If the antiskating foil is damaged or peeled away from the gate surface, trim the damaged or loose portion of the foil from the gate.

G. Prepare for Transportation of the Outflow Valve Assembly

SUBTASK 21-31-03-860-010 (1) The aft outflow valve [1] must be in the fully closed position for transportation. (a) If you do not have outflow valve installation extension cable, SPL-14208, available, do these steps to close the outflow valve gates for transportation: 1) Lift the aft outflow valve [1] sufficiently so that you can connect the manual motor electrical connector [4] on the valve. 2) Connect the manual motor electrical connector [4] on the aft outflow valve [1]. 3) Put the aft outflow valve [1] on a suitable support so that the valve doors will be free to move. WARNING DO NOT PUT YOUR HANDS OR TOOLS IN THE OUTFLOW VALVE WHEN THE VALVE IS IN OPERATION. IF YOU PUT YOUR HANDS OR TOOLS IN THE OUTFLOW VALVE WHEN IT OPERATES YOU CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. 4) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL 5) Put the mode select switch on the cabin pressure control module, on the P5 overhead panel, to the MAN position. 6) Position the aft outflow valve [1] as follows: a) Use the service interphone system to make sure that there is communication between the technician at the aft outflow valve location and the technician in the flight deck. b) Push and hold the CLOSE/OPEN toggle switch, on the P5-6 pressure control module, to the CLOSE position until the aft outflow valve is fully closed. 7) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL 8) Disconnect the manual motor electrical connector [4] from the aft outflow valve [1]. SUBTASK 21-31-03-860-011 (2) The aft outflow valve [1] must be in the fully closed position for transportation. (a) If the outflow valve installation extension cable, SPL-14208, is available, do these steps to close the outflow valve gates for transportation: 1) Position the aft outflow valve [1] so that the valve gates are free to move and are not obstructed. EFFECTIVITY ALL 2) Connect J1 connector of the outflow valve installation extension cable, SPL-14208, to connector D10730 on the ship's wiring inside the outflow valve opening in the fuselage. 3) Connect P1 of the outflow valve installation extension cable, SPL-14208, to the J5 manual motor electrical connector [4] on the aft outflow valve DC motor. WARNING DO NOT PUT YOUR HANDS OR TOOLS IN THE OUTLET OF THE OUTFLOW VALVE. THE VALVE IS MOTOR-OPERATED. INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. 4) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL 5) Put the mode select switch, on the P5-6 cabin pressure control module, to the MAN position. 6) Position the aft outflow valve [1] as follows: a) Use the service interphone system to make sure that there is communication between the technician at the aft outflow valve location and the technician in the flight deck. b) Push and hold the CLOSE/OPEN toggle switch, on the P5-6 pressure control module, to the CLOSE position until the aft outflow valve [1] is fully closed. 7) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL 8) Disconnect the outflow valve installation extension cable, SPL-14208, from the aft outflow valve connector J5 and connector D10730 on the ship's wiring.
