G. Outflow Valve Assembly Installation

SUBTASK 21-31-03-860-012 (1) Make sure that these circuit breakers are open and have safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 3 C01270 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 1 F 5 C01271 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 2 F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL SUBTASK 21-31-03-860-007 (2) Make sure that there is electrical power and that the BAT switch on the electrical meters, battery, and galley power module, P5-13, is in the ON position. SUBTASK 21-31-03-420-004 (3) Make sure that all shipping plugs are removed from the vent ports of the two electronic actuators. NOTE: The vent ports are below the electronic actuators. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-31-03-640-001 (4) If a screw [12] is replaced for any reason or if a screw [12] was difficult to loosen, apply a light and even application of compound, D50004, to the threads and shank of the screw [12]. ALL; OUTFLOW VALVES WITH JAGGED GATES SUBTASK 21-31-03-420-006 (5) Use care not to damage the antiskating foil on the forward and aft gates of the outflow valve (Figure 402) when you reach through the opening of the valve to connect electrical connectors or other components. (a) If you install the same outflow valve that you removed and the foil is damaged or peeled away from the gate, the foil can be removed or cut away until all loose foil has been removed. ALL SUBTASK 21-31-03-980-001 (6) If the aft outflow valve [1] to be installed is in the fully open position or closed position and you do not have outflow valve installation extension cable, SPL-14208, available, do these steps to position the outflow valve gates so that the valve can be moved through the fuselage opening: NOTE: If you are re-installing the same outflow valve that you removed, then you do not need to change the position of the valve gates. (a) Lift the aft outflow valve [1] sufficiently so that you can connect the manual motor electrical connector [4] on the valve. (b) Connect the manual motor electrical connector [4] on the aft outflow valve [1]. (c) Put the aft outflow valve [1] on a suitable support so that the valve doors will be free to move. WARNING DO NOT PUT YOUR HANDS OR TOOLS IN THE OUTFLOW VALVE WHEN THE VALVE IS IN OPERATION. IF YOU PUT YOUR HANDS OR TOOLS IN THE OUTFLOW VALVE WHEN IT OPERATES YOU CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (d) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL (e) Put the mode select switch on the cabin pressure control module, on the P5 overhead panel, to the MAN position. (f) Position the aft outflow valve [1] as follows: 1) Use the service interphone system to make sure there is communication between the technician at the aft outflow valve location and the technician in the flight deck. 2) Push and hold the CLOSE/OPEN toggle switch, on the P5-6 pressure control module, to the OPEN position until the technician at the aft outflow valve [1] location states that the valve is approximately in the specified position (View B-B, Figure 401). EFFECTIVITY ALL (g) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL (h) Disconnect the manual motor electrical connector [4] from the aft outflow valve [1]. SUBTASK 21-31-03-480-001 (7) If the aft outflow valve [1] to be installed is in the fully open position or closed position and outflow valve installation extension cable, SPL-14208, is available, do these steps to position the outflow valve gates so that the valve can be moved through the fuselage opening: NOTE: If you are re-installing the same outflow valve that you removed, then you do not need to change the position of the valve gates. (a) Position the aft outflow valve [1] so that the valve gates are free to move and are not obstructed. (b) Connect J1 connector of the outflow valve installation extension cable, SPL-14208, to connector D10730 on the ship's wiring inside the outflow valve opening in the fuselage. (c) Connect P1 of the outflow valve installation extension cable, SPL-14208, to the manual motor electrical connector [4] (J5) on the aft outflow valve [1] DC motor. WARNING DO NOT PUT YOUR HANDS OR TOOLS IN THE OUTLET OF THE OUTFLOW VALVE. THE VALVE IS MOTOR-OPERATED. INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (d) Close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL (e) Put the mode select switch, on the P5-6 cabin pressure control module, to the MAN position. (f) Position the aft outflow valve [1] as follows: 1) Use the service interphone system to make sure there is communication between the technician at the aft outflow valve location and the technician in the flight deck. 2) Push and hold the CLOSE/OPEN toggle switch, on the P5-6 pressure control module, to the OPEN position until the technician at the aft outflow valve [1] location states that the valve is approximately in the specified position (View B-B, Figure 401). (g) Open this circuit breaker and install safety tag: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL (h) Disconnect the outflow valve installation extension cable, SPL-14208, from the aft outflow valve [1] connector J5 and connector D10730 on the ship's wiring. SUBTASK 21-31-03-420-001 (8) Do these steps to install the aft outflow valve [1]: EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Make sure that the three aft lugs [11] are turned so they face inboard to outboard. NOTE: The lugs will be 1/4 turn away from the installed position. (b) Put the aft outflow valve [1] through the skin opening on the airplane so that the motors go in first with the valve diagonal to the skin opening. NOTE: The motors will be on the inboard side of the skin opening. (c) Set the aft outflow valve [1] down on the inside of the airplane so that you can connect the manual motor electrical connector [4]. (d) Connect the manual motor electrical connector [4] to the aft outflow valve [1]. (e) Install the gasket [10] in its position on the airplane skin opening with the thinner rubber side against the airplane (down). (f) Do these steps to put the aft outflow valve [1] in its position: 1) Put the aft outflow valve [1] above the skin opening with the motors facing inboard. 2) While you tilt the aft outflow valve [1], put the forward end of the valve under the three forward lugs [11], then lower the aft end of the valve. 3) Turn the three aft lugs [11] 90 degrees counterclockwise so that they face aft to forward. (g) Tighten the screws [12] to 55 in-lb (6.2 N·m) - 65 in-lb (7.3 N·m) as follows: 1) Tighten the screws [12] no more than one turn at a time in sequence (1 thru 6) as shown (View D, Figure 401). 2) Continue to tighten the screws [12] until all of the latches are in contact with the valve. 3) Use a torque screwdriver, STD-10994, set at 55 in-lb (6.2 N·m) - 65 in-lb (7.3 N·m) with a bit, COM-10996, to tighten the screws no more than 1/2 turn at a time in the sequence shown in (View D, Figure 401). 4) Continue to tighten the screws [12] in sequence until all latch screws [12] are tightened to 55 in-lb (6.2 N·m) - 65 in-lb (7.3 N·m). 5) If a screw [12] does not turn when the final application of torque is applied, back that screw [12] off one turn and tighten it to the final torque value. WARNING DO NOT PUT YOUR HANDS OR TOOLS IN THE OUTFLOW VALVE WHEN THE VALVE IS IN OPERATION. IF YOU PUT YOUR HANDS OR TOOLS IN THE OUTFLOW VALVE WHEN IT OPERATES YOU CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (h) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL (i) Put the mode select switch on the cabin pressure control module, on the P5 overhead panel, to the MAN position. (j) Use the service interphone system so that the technician at the aft outflow valve location can communicate the position of the aft outflow valve to the technician in the flight deck. (k) Push and hold the manual control switch to the OPEN position until the aft outflow valve [1] is in the full open position. EFFECTIVITY ALL (l) Open this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL SUBTASK 21-31-03-420-002 (9) Connect these electrical connectors to the aft outflow valve [1]: NOTE: You can access the connectors through the valve door opening. (a) ELACT 1 electrical connector [3] (b) ELACT 2 electrical connector [2] (c) feedback module connector 1 [5] (d) feedback module connector 2 [6]. SUBTASK 21-31-03-020-005 (10) Put the bonding jumper [9] in its position on the stud of the aft outflow valve [1]. SUBTASK 21-31-03-420-003 (11) Install the nut [7] and washer [8] that attach the bonding jumper [9] to the aft outflow valve [1]. (a) Measure the bonding resistance between the bonding jumper [9] and aft outflow valve [1] (SWPM 20-20-00). 1) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. 2) Make sure that the bonding resistance is 0.001 ohm (1 milliohm) or less. SUBTASK 21-31-03-860-004 (12) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 3 C01270 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 1 F 5 C01271 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 2 F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL

H. Outflow Valve Assembly Installation Test

SUBTASK 21-31-03-710-001 (1) Do a test of the manual mode, do this task: Pressurization System Manual Mode Test, TASK 21-31-00-710-801. SUBTASK 21-31-03-710-002 (2) Do a cabin pressure control system ground test, do this task: Pressurization System Ground Test, TASK 21-31-00-700-802.

I. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 21-31-03-410-001 WARNING SEAL THE CARGO COMPARTMENT WITH THE LINING. OBEY THE INSTRUCTIONS IN THE SPECIFIED PROCEDURE WHEN YOU INSTALL THE LINING. IF YOU INSTALL THE LINING INCORRECTLY, THE FIRE EXTINGUISHING AGENT OR SMOKE CAN CAUSE INJURIES. (1) Do this task: Aft Cargo Compartment Aft Bulkhead Liner - Installation, TASK 25-52-19-400-801. 2. Positive Pressure Relief Valve - System Test with the Use of Hamilton Sundstrand Test Equipment (Figure 501) NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. Tools/Equipment

NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional. Reference Description SPL-6692 Vacuum Tank - Pressure Relief Valve Tester Part #: A21010-203 Supplier: 81205 Part #: GS15047-1 Supplier: 99167 Opt Part #: A21010-187 Supplier: 81205 Opt Part #: A21010-188 Supplier: 81205 Opt Part #: A21010-189 Supplier: 81205 Opt Part #: A21010-190 Supplier: 81205 STD-1114 Air Source - Regulated, Dry, Filtered 0-150 PSIG with Pressure Gauge Range 0-100 PSIG, 1 PSIG Increment, and +/-1 PSI Minimum Accuracy

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 146 Aft Cargo Compartment Equipment Bay - Right

C. Prepare for the Test

SUBTASK 21-32-01-860-001 (1) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 3 C01270 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 1 F 5 C01271 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 2 F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-32-01-840-002 (2) Make sure that there is no blockage or unwanted materials at these locations: (a) The fuselage skin in the area of the relief valves. (b) The overboard vent tube opening in the center of each relief valve. (c) The ambient sense tube in the fuselage pedestal mount. SUBTASK 21-32-01-840-003 (3) Close the pressure regulator on the pressure relief valve tester, SPL-6692. SUBTASK 21-32-01-840-001 (4) Connect the Regulated Dry Filtered Air Source, STD-1114, to the pressure regulator of the pressure relief valve tester, SPL-6692.

D. Positive Pressure Relief Valve System Test

NOTE: This test can only be done on one relief valve at a time. Do the test on the outboard relief valve, then do the test again on the inboard relief valve. SUBTASK 21-32-01-730-001 WARNING DO NOT PUT YOUR HANDS OR TOOLS IN THE OUTFLOW VALVE WHEN THE VALVE IS IN OPERATION. IF YOU PUT YOUR HANDS OR TOOLS IN THE OUTFLOW VALVE WHEN IT OPERATES YOU CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) Do these steps to do a test of the positive pressure relief valve: (a) Put the pressure relief valve tester, SPL-6692, on the relief valve of the fuselage. (b) Put the locating crossbar on the pressure relief valve tester, SPL-6692, forward of the deflector tube on the relief valve and hold the fixture in position. NOTE: The fixture is installed to make sure that the test fixture gasket is not on the opening in the valve. (c) Open the air pressure regulator on the pressure relief valve tester, SPL-6692, to start the flow of air. (d) Adjust the air pressure regulator so that the indication on the vacuum gage increases 2.21 psi/minute (15.24 kPa/minute) until the vacuum gage shows 7.76 psig (53.50 kPa). WARNING MANUALLY HOLD THE TEST FIXTURE AGAINST THE FUSELAGE. WHEN THE VALVE OPENS, IT CAN CAUSE THE TEST FIXTURE TO FALL. INJURIES TO PERSONNEL, AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (e) When the vacuum gage shows 7.76 psig (53.50 kPa), manually hold the test fixture against the airplane fuselage. (f) When the vacuum gage shows 7.76 psig (53.50 kPa), adjust the air pressure regulator to increase the vacuum in 0.05 psi (0.34 kPa) increments. (g) Stop the increase of vacuum for 10 seconds between each increase of 0.05 psi (0.34 kPa). (h) Continue the intermittent vacuum increases of 0.05 psi (0.34 kPa) until the valve opens as noted by these indications: 1) The cracking point pressure of the valve occurs when the vacuum gauge needle stops increasing, then suddenly decreases slightly, then increases slightly again and then stabilizes. EFFECTIVITY ALL (i) Monitor the indication on the vacuum gage when the valve opens. (j) Make sure that the valve opens between 8.69 psig (59.92 kPa) to 9.09 psig (62.67 kPa) (17.70 in/Hg - 18.50 in/Hg). (k) If the pressure relief valve cracks open at a vacuum gauge indication greater than 9.09 psig (62.67 kPa) (18.50 in/Hg), make sure that there are no leaks anywhere on the valve test fixture. (l) Adjust the vacuum regulator valve to increase the differential pressure to approximately 7.5 psid (51.7 kPa) - 7.0 psid (48.3 kPa) (15.04 in/Hg - 14.02 in/Hg) at a rate not more than 2.00 psig/minute (13.79 kPa/minute) (4.07 inches Hg/minute). 1) Make sure that the relief valve closes. NOTE: The indication that the relief valve has closed is seen on the differential pressure gauge when the gauge stops, and then starts to increase and then becomes stable. (m) Adjust the air pressure regulator to reduce the indication on the vacuum gage to 0 psig (0 kPa) (0 in/Hg) at a rate of 4.0 psig/minute (27.58 kPa/minute) (8.14 inches Hg/minute) or slower. (n) Close the pressure regulator on the pressure relief valve tester, SPL-6692. (o) Remove the pressure relief valve tester, SPL-6692, from the airplane. (p) Disconnect the Regulated Dry Filtered Air Source, STD-1114, from the pressure regulator. SUBTASK 21-32-01-730-002 (2) Do the test for the other relief valve. SUBTASK 21-32-01-860-002 (3) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 3 C01270 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 1 F 5 C01271 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 2 F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL

A. Tools/Equipment

Tool part numbers that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional. Reference Description SPL-6692 Vacuum Tank - Pressure Relief Valve Tester Part #: A21010-203 Supplier: 81205 Part #: GS15047-1 Supplier: 99167 Opt Part #: A21010-187 Supplier: 81205 Opt Part #: A21010-188 Supplier: 81205 Opt Part #: A21010-189 Supplier: 81205 Opt Part #: A21010-190 Supplier: 81205 STD-1114 Air Source - Regulated, Dry, Filtered 0-150 PSIG with Pressure Gauge Range 0-100 PSIG, 1 PSIG Increment, and +/-1 PSI Minimum Accuracy

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 146 Aft Cargo Compartment Equipment Bay - Right

C. Prepare for the Test

SUBTASK 21-32-01-860-003 (1) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 3 C01270 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 1 F 5 C01271 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 2 F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL SUBTASK 21-32-01-210-001 (2) Make sure there is no blockage or unwanted materials at these locations: (a) The fuselage skin in the area of the relief valve. (b) The overboard vent tube opening in the center of each relief valve. (c) The ambient sense tube in the fuselage pedestal mount.

D. Positive Pressure Relief Valve System Test

NOTE: This test can only be done on one relief valve at a time. Do the test on the outboard relief valve, then do the test again on the inboard relief valve. SUBTASK 21-32-01-480-001 WARNING DO NOT PUT YOUR HANDS OR TOOLS IN THE OUTFLOW VALVE WHEN THE VALVE IS IN OPERATION. IF YOU PUT YOUR HANDS OR TOOLS IN THE OUTFLOW VALVE WHEN IT OPERATES YOU CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (1) Do these steps to connect the pressure relief valve tester, SPL-6692, to the relief valve: EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Make sure that all the valves on the pressure relief valve tester, SPL-6692, are closed. (b) Connect the Regulated Dry Filtered Air Source, STD-1114, to the quick-disconnect connection on the pressure relief valve tester, SPL-6692. (c) Adjust the air control valve on the pressure relief valve tester, SPL-6692, until the indication on the pressure gage is 70 ±10 psi (482.6 ±68.9 kPa). (d) Adjust the vacuum regulator valve until the differential pressure is approximately 2.0 psi (13.8 kPa) (4.07 in/Hg). 1) Turn the vacuum regulator valve counter-clockwise to increase the vacuum (differential pressure). NOTE: The arrow on the vacuum regulator valve indicates an increase of pressure not vacuum. (e) Put and hold the vacuum head assembly over the relief valve. (f) Open the vacuum head assembly valve. 1) Make sure that the vacuum head assembly is sealed to the airplane skin. SUBTASK 21-32-01-730-003 (2) Do these steps to find the differential pressure when the relief valve opens: (a) Adjust the vacuum regulator valve so the indication on the vacuum rate gage does not exceed 2.4 psi/minute (16.5 kPa/minute). WARNING YOU MUST HOLD THE VACUUM HEAD ASSEMBLY MANUALLY AGAINST THE AIRPLANE FUSELAGE WHEN THE DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE GAGE INDICATION IS 8.25 PSID (56.88 KPA). WHEN THE VALVE OPENS, THE VACUUM HEAD ASSEMBLY CAN FALL FROM THE FUSELAGE SURFACE. INJURY TO PERSONNEL OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (b) When the differential pressure gage shows 8.25 psid (56.88 kPa), manually hold the vacuum head assembly against the fuselage. (c) When the differential pressure gage shows 8.25 psid (56.88 kPa), adjust the vacuum regulator valve to increase the differential pressure in 0.05 psid (0.345 kPa) increments. (d) Stop the increase of vacuum for 10 seconds between each increase of 0.05 psid (0.345 kPa). (e) Continue the intermittent vacuum increases of 0.05 psid (0.345 kPa) until the relief valve opens. (f) Monitor the indication on the differential pressure gage when the relief valve opens. NOTE: The indication that the relief valve has opened is seen on the differential pressure gage when the pressure starts to decrease. (g) Make sure that the valve opens at a differential pressure of 8.69 psid (59.92 kPa) to 9.09 psid (62.67 kPa) (17.7 to 18.5 in/Hg). NOTE: When the valve opens the differential pressure will decrease to near 0 psid. (h) If the relief valve opens at a differential pressure more than 9.09 psid (62.67 kPa) (18.51 in/Hg), make sure that there are no leaks at any of the tubing connections on the vacuum tank assembly. (i) Adjust the vacuum regulator valve to increase the differential pressure to approximately 7.5 psig (51.71 kPa) to 7.0 psig (48.26 kPa) (15.04 to 14.02 in/Hg) at a rate not more than 2.00 psig/minute (13.79 kPa/minute) (4.07 inches Hg/minute). EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Make sure that the relief valve closes. NOTE: The indication that the relief valve has closed is seen on the differential pressure gage when the gage stops, and then starts to increase and then becomes stable. SUBTASK 21-32-01-080-001 (3) Adjust the vacuum regulator valve fully clockwise and reduce the differential pressure to 0 psig (0.0 kPa) (0 in/Hg), at a rate of 4.0 psig/min (27.58 kPa/min) (8.14 inches Hg/min) or slower. SUBTASK 21-32-01-080-002 (4) Close the vacuum head assembly valve and remove the vacuum head assembly. SUBTASK 21-32-01-730-004 (5) Do the test for the other relief valve. SUBTASK 21-32-01-860-004 (6) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name F 3 C01270 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 1 F 5 C01271 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL AUTO 2 F 6 C01269 PRESSURIZATION CONTROL MANUAL

2. Positive Pressure Relief Valve Filter Removal (Figure 401) NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. References

Reference Title 21-31-03-000-801 Aft Outflow Valve Assembly Removal (P/B 401) 38-11-01-000-801 Water Tank Removal (P/B 401) 53-21-00-000-801 Passenger Cabin Floor Panel - Removal (P/B 401)

B. Tools/Equipment

Reference Description STD-6435 Respirator - Particulate (Meets NIOSH 42 CFR 84 Class N95, EN149 Class FFP2, or Better) STD-6437 Goggles - Safety, Non Vented STD-6439 Coveralls - Hooded

C. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification B50073 Alcohol - Isopropyl ASTM D 770 G00624 Bag - Plastic, General Purpose G50140 Gloves - Protective, Latex or Nitrile

D. Location Zones

Zone Area 142 Aft Cargo Compartment - Right

E. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 21-32-02-010-004 (1) Do one of the tasks that follow to get access to the positive pressure relief valves [1]: (a) Remove the potable water tank (TASK 38-11-01-000-801). (b) Remove the aft outflow valve (TASK 21-31-03-000-801). (c) Remove the applicable floor panels above the positive pressure relief valve (TASK 53-21-00-000-801). EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-32-02-940-001 WARNING PUT ON THE PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT BEFORE YOU TOUCH THE FILTER. THE FILTER REMOVES SMALL PARTICLES (SMOKE, DUST, LINT, FIBERS, POLLEN) AND INFECTIOUS MATERIALS (BACTERIA, VIRUSES, MOLD SPORES, FUNGI) FROM THE AIR WHICH CAN CAUSE ILLNESSES AND INJURIES TO PERSONS. (2) Before you touch the positive pressure relief valve filter [3], put on the personal protective equipment listed below: (a) hooded coveralls, STD-6439 (b) particulate respirator, STD-6435 (c) safety goggles, STD-6437 (d) protective gloves, G50140. SUBTASK 21-32-02-500-001 (3) Select a plastic bag, G00624, larger than the filters and tape suitable for sealing the bag closed.

F. Positive Pressure Relief Valve Filter Removal

SUBTASK 21-32-02-020-001 (1) Remove the cover [4] from the top of the positive pressure relief valve [1]. SUBTASK 21-32-02-020-002 (2) Remove the filter [3] and packing [2] from the positive pressure relief valve [1]. SUBTASK 21-32-02-020-003 WARNING DO NOT LET THE FILTER TOUCH YOUR SKIN. DO NOT SHAKE OR HIT THE FILTER. DO NOT LET THE FILTER FALL. DO NOT USE COMPRESSED AIR TO CLEAN THE FILTER OR FILTER HOUSING. THIS CAN CAUSE THE INFECTIOUS MATERIAL TO BECOME AIRBORNE. DISCARD THE FILTER IN A PLASTIC DISPOSAL BAG. OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (3) If possible, slide the plastic bag, G00624, over the filter [3] with the packing [2] when removing from the positive pressure relief valve [1] to minimize contamination. (a) Seal the bag closed with tape. WARNING OBEY THE AIRLINE POLICY, LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT, AND LAW ENFORCEMENT REGULATIONS WHEN YOU DISCARD THIS MATERIAL. OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (b) Discard the bag with the filter. NOTE: Refer to the airline, local health, safety and regulatory procedures for the disposal of material. EFFECTIVITY ALL

G. Post-Filter Removal Cleanup

SUBTASK 21-32-02-080-001 WARNING ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL IS POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE. USE PROTECTION EQUIPMENT. MAKE SURE THAT YOU USE ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL IN AN AREA WITH AIRFLOW. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. (1) Disinfect the filter cover, filter housing and exterior surfaces of the valve with alcohol, B50073. NOTE: Refer to the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) List N or local health authority guidance for required contact/dwell time for Isopropyl Alcohol to be used as a disinfectant. SUBTASK 21-32-02-670-001 (2) Disinfect all tools used for filter replacement. NOTE: Refer to the airline procedure and policies for the disinfecting of tools. SUBTASK 21-32-02-020-004 WARNING DISCARD ALL PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT AFTER YOU USE IT ONE TIME. DO NOT TRY TO CLEAN IT. DISCARD THE EQUIPMENT IN A PLASTIC DISPOSAL BAG. OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (3) Remove the personal protective equipment and put them in a plastic bag, G00624. (a) Seal the bag closed with tape. WARNING OBEY THE AIRLINE POLICY, LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT, AND LAW ENFORCEMENT REGULATIONS WHEN YOU DISCARD THIS MATERIAL. OBEY THESE INSTRUCTIONS TO PREVENT INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (b) Discard the bag with the personal protective equipment. NOTE: Refer to the airline, local health, safety and regulatory procedures for disposal of material. SUBTASK 21-32-02-110-001 WARNING CLEAN YOUR HANDS WITH SOAP AND FLUSH WITH HOT WATER. DIRTY HANDS WITH CONTAMINATION CAN CAUSE DISEASE AND ILLNESSES TO PERSONS. (4) Clean your hands with soap and running hot water.

SUBTASK 21-32-03-420-001 (1) Do the steps which follow to install the spring [7] on the door assembly [6]: (a) Put the spring [7] on the spring support [8]. (b) Put the end of the spring [7] in the door hole. (c) Put the end of the spring support [8] in the large hole in the door. (d) Turn the spring [7] approximately one full turn and hold it in that position. (e) Put the free end of the spring support [8] in the slot of the door assembly [6]. (f) Slowly release the free end of the spring [7], until it rests against the edge of the door assembly [6]. (g) Put the shim [12] and the retainer [9] in their position. (h) Install the bolt [10] and the washer [11]. (i) Install the washer [13] and the nut [14]. 1) Tighten the nut [14] to 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m) - 25 in-lb (2.8 N·m). SUBTASK 21-32-03-210-001 (2) Examine the condition of the seal [15] and replace it, if it is damaged. SUBTASK 21-32-03-420-002 (3) Do the steps which follow to install the door assembly [6] in the frame: (a) Lubricate the bolts [1] with the grease, D00013. (b) Put the door assembly [6] in its position. 1) Hold the door assembly [6] in an approximately 45° open position while you turn the free end of the spring [7] and insert it into the frame hole. (c) Install the bushings [3]. EFFECTIVITY ALL (d) Install the bolts [1] and the washers [2]. (e) Install the washers [4] and the nuts [5]. 1) Tighten the nuts [5] to 60 in-lb (6.8 N·m) - 70 in-lb (7.9 N·m). SUBTASK 21-32-03-720-001 (4) Do this task: Negative Pressure Relief Valve Adjustment/Test, TASK 21-32-03-700-801.

F. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 21-32-03-410-001 (1) Install the sidewall liner. To install the sidewall liner, do this task: Cargo Compartment Sidewall Lining - Installation, TASK 25-52-06-400-801

21-32-03-700-801Negative Pressure Relief Valve Adjustment/TestPDF p. 724

4. Negative Pressure Relief Valve Adjustment/Test NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. Tools/Equipment

Reference Description STD-753 Scale - Push/Pull, 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram) Capacity, 1/4 pound (113 gram) Accuracy

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 142 Aft Cargo Compartment - Right

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 21-32-03-480-001 (1) On the external surface of the airplane, hold the push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram), STD-753 against the relief valve as shown in View A-A Figure 201. (a) Put the push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram), STD-753 at approximately the center of the relief valve door and 2.92 ±0.20 in. (74.2 ±5.1 mm) above the lower edge of the relief valve door. SUBTASK 21-32-03-720-002 (2) Slowly push the push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram), STD-753 against the relief valve door. (a) Keep the push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram), STD-753 at approximately a 90° angle to the relief valve door. SUBTASK 21-32-03-720-003 (3) Make sure the relief valve door starts to open when the push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram), STD-753 shows between 4 lbf (17.8 N) and 8 lbf (35.6 N). SUBTASK 21-32-03-720-004 (4) Continue to push the relief valve door to the full open position. (a) Make sure the door moves smoothly without any binding. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-32-03-720-005 (5) Make sure the push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram), STD-753 shows between 8 lbf (35.6 N) and 10.5 lbf (46.7 N) when the relief valve door is in the full open position (Figure 202). NOTE: The door in the full open position is a minimum of 40° from its full closed position. NOTE: The straight-line distance is a minimum of 5.7 in. (14.5 cm) from the closed position to open the door fully. SUBTASK 21-32-03-720-006 (6) Slowly release the relief valve door until it is in the closed position. SUBTASK 21-32-03-080-001 (7) Remove the push/pull scale 0-25 pound (0-11 kilogram), STD-753.

F. Cabin Altitude Warning Switch Functional Test

SUBTASK 21-33-00-720-021 (1) Do a test of the cabin altitude warning switch, S128, as follows: (a) Remove the screen port assembly from the cabin altitude warning switch, S128. (b) Install an adapter fitting and matching hose on the cabin altitude warning switch, S128: NOTE: The female threads on the cabin altitude warning switch are 7/16-20-UNJF-3A with a full thread depth of 0.438 in. (1.113 cm) minimum. The total port depth is 0.541 in. (1.374 cm) - 0.551 in. (1.400 cm). Any mating adapter should have threads having a full thread depth of no greater than 0.438 in. (1.113 cm) and an overall length that is less than 0.500 in. (1.270 cm) to avoid false test results. 1) Use one of the following adapters, or equivalent adapter, and matching hose to connect to the cabin altitude warning switch: NOTE: Adapters are considered to be equivalent as long as the mating side with the switch is: • Greater than or equal to 0.265 in. (0.673 cm) X 7/16-20-UNJF-3A and less than or equal to 0.438 in. (1.113 cm) X 7/16-20-UNJF-3A for the flareless end, or • Less than or equal to 0.500 in. (1.270 cm) total with greater than or equal to 0.265 in. (0.673 cm) X 7/16-20-UNJF-3A thread for AN4 flared end. a) SAE J514 P/N 070220 90 Degree Straight Thread Elbow and appropriate sized O-ring (Preferred). <1> Use a Barfield Pitot Hose, or equivalent 25 ft (7.62 m) to 40 ft (12.19 m) long hose, with #4 AN fitting to the adapter and quick disconnect (if applicable) to the air data test set. <2> Make sure that the flat side of the adapter is connected with the cabin altitude warning switch. NOTE: Do not connect the flared side of the adapter with the cabin altitude warning switch. Connecting the flared side of the adapter with the cabin altitude warning switch can bottom out the cabin altitude warning switch, resulting in false test results. b) SAE J514 P/N 070320 45 Degree Straight Thread Elbow and appropriate sized O-ring (Preferred). <1> Use a Barfield Pitot Hose, or equivalent 25 ft (7.62 m) to 40 ft (12.19 m) long hose, with #4 AN fitting to the adapter and quick disconnect (if applicable) to the air data test set. EFFECTIVITY ALL <2> Make sure that the flat side of the adapter is connected with the cabin altitude warning switch. 3. Check of the Cabin Rate of Climb Indicator

A. Location Zones

Zone Area 212 Flight Compartment - Right

B. Cabin Rate of Climb Indicator Check

SUBTASK 21-33-00-212-001 (1) Get access to the cabin rate of climb indicator on the P5-16 cabin pressure control panel. SUBTASK 21-33-00-710-003 (2) Do this check of the cabin rate of climb indicator: (a) Open one of the cabin entry doors to make sure that the cabin is not pressurized. (b) Turn the zero adjustment screw on the lower left corner of the gauge and make sure that the pointer can be adjusted to a minimum of 400 ft/min on both sides of the zero graduation. (c) Reset the pointer to zero.

21-33-01-000-801Cabin Rate of Climb Indicator RemovalPDF p. 753

2. Cabin Rate of Climb Indicator Removal (Figure 401)

A. Location Zones

Zone Area 212 Flight Compartment - Right

B. Preparation Check for Removal

SUBTASK 21-33-01-710-001 (1) Do this check to determine if the cabin rate of climb indicator requires replacement: (a) Make sure that the cabin is not pressurized. (b) Turn the zero adjustment screw on the lower left corner of the gauge to make sure that the pointer can be adjusted to a minimum of 400 ft/min on both sides of the zero graduation. (c) Reset the pointer to zero. SUBTASK 21-33-01-000-001 (2) If the indicator cannot be adjusted as noted in the previous step, continue with the removal procedure.

C. Cabin Rate of Climb Indicator Removal

SUBTASK 21-33-01-860-001 (1) Open this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name E 10 C00328 OVERHEAD 5V SECONDARY SUBTASK 21-33-01-020-001 CAUTION HOLD THE INDICATOR WHEN YOU LOOSEN THE CLAMP. THE INDICATOR CAN FALL WHEN THE CLAMP IS LOOSE. DAMAGE CAN OCCUR TO THE INDICATOR IF IT FALLS. (2) Loosen the clamp tension screw [1]. (a) If necessary, loosen the clamp mount screw [5]. SUBTASK 21-33-01-020-002 (3) Carefully pull the cabin rate of climb indicator [3] out of the P5-16 panel [4]. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-33-01-020-003 (4) Disconnect the electrical connector [2] from the cabin rate of climb indicator [3]. SUBTASK 21-33-01-480-001 (5) Put a dust cap on the cabin pressure port to keep out unwanted objects.

C. Cabin Rate of Climb Indicator Installation

SUBTASK 21-33-01-080-001 (1) Remove the dust cap from the cabin pressure port on the back of the cabin rate of climb indicator [3]. SUBTASK 21-33-01-420-001 (2) Connect the electrical connector [2] to the cabin rate of climb indicator [3]. SUBTASK 21-33-01-820-001 (3) Carefully push the cabin rate of climb indicator [3] into its position in the P5-16 panel [4]. SUBTASK 21-33-01-420-002 (4) Tighten the clamp tension screw [1] to 5.0 in-lb (0.6 N·m) - 8.0 in-lb (0.9 N·m). (a) If loosened, tighten the clamp mount screw [5] to 1.0 in-lb (0.1 N·m) - 6.0 in-lb (0.7 N·m). NOTE: Hold the cabin rate of climb indicator [3] against the P5-16 panel [4] while you tighten the clamp tension screws [1] or clamp mount screw [5]. SUBTASK 21-33-01-860-002 (5) Close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name E 10 C00328 OVERHEAD 5V SECONDARY SUBTASK 21-33-01-700-001 (6) Do this check of the cabin rate of climb indicator [3]: (a) Make sure that the cabin is not pressurized. EFFECTIVITY ALL (b) Turn the zero adjustment screw on the lower left corner of the gauge and make sure that the pointer can be adjusted to a minimum of 400 ft/min on both sides of the zero graduation. (c) Reset the pointer to zero.

E. Cabin Altitude and Differential Pressure Indicator Installation

SUBTASK 21-33-02-080-001 (1) Remove the dust cap from the cabin pressure port on the back of the indicator. SUBTASK 21-33-02-420-003 (2) If you are installing a cabin altitude and differential pressure indicator [6] that does not have a quick-disconnect fitting already installed, do these steps: EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Put a new packing [3] on the male quick-disconnect [2]. (b) Apply anti-seize compound, D50004 to the threads of the male quick-disconnect [2]. (c) Install the male quick-disconnect [2] on the cabin altitude and differential pressure indicator [6]. (d) Tighten the male quick-disconnect [2] to a torque of 120 (± 12) inch-pounds [13.6 (± 1.36) Nm]. SUBTASK 21-33-02-020-009 (3) Connect the static pressure hose [4] to the quick-disconnect [2] on the cabin altitude and differential pressure indicator [6]. SUBTASK 21-33-02-420-001 (4) Connect the electrical connector [5] to the cabin altitude and differential pressure indicator [6]. SUBTASK 21-33-02-820-001 (5) Carefully push the cabin altitude and differential pressure indicator [6] into its position in the P5-16 panel [7]. SUBTASK 21-33-02-420-002 (6) Tighten the clamp tension screws [1] 5 to 8 pound-inches (0.6 to 0.9 newton-meters). NOTE: Hold the indicator [6] against the panel [7] while you tighten the screws [1]. SUBTASK 21-33-02-790-001 (7) If you removed or installed the quick-disconnect fitting on the cabin altitude and differential pressure indicator [6] at any time during this maintenance, do this task: Alternate Static System Low-range Leak Test, TASK 34-11-00-790-808. (a) Note that if the replacement indicator came with the quick-disconnect installed or if the quick-disconnect was never removed from the existing indicator during this maintenance, it is not necessary to do the task: Alternate Static System Low-range Leak Test, TASK 34-11-00-790-808. SUBTASK 21-33-02-860-002 (8) Close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name E 10 C00328 OVERHEAD 5V SECONDARY SUBTASK 21-33-02-710-001 (9) Do this check of the cabin altimeter gauge: (a) Open one of the main entry doors to make sure that the cabin is not pressurized. (b) Set the barometric pressure for the pilot's altimeter to 29.92 inches of Hg. (c) Observe the altitude on the pilot's altimeter. (d) Compare the altitude on the pilot's altimeter to the altitude on the cabin altimeter. (e) If the altitude on the cabin altimeter is within 1000 feet of the altitude on the pilot's altimeter, the cabin altimeter is satisfactory. (f) If the altitude on the cabin altimeter is not within1000 feet of the altitude on the pilot's altimeter, then do these tasks to replace the gauge: Cabin Altitude and Differential Pressure Indicator Removal, TASK 21-33-02-000-801 and Cabin Altitude and Differential Pressure Indicator Installation, TASK 21-33-02-400-801. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-33-02-710-002 (10) Do this check of the cabin differential pressure gauge: (a) Observe the differential pressure on the DIFF PRESS gauge. (b) If the differential pressure is within 0 (± 0.2) psid, the cabin differential pressure gauge is satisfactory. (c) If the differential pressure is not within 0 (± 0.2) psid, then do these tasks to replace the gauge: Cabin Altitude and Differential Pressure Indicator Removal, TASK 21-33-02-000-801 and Cabin Altitude and Differential Pressure Indicator Installation, TASK 21-33-02-400-801.

21-33-07-000-801Cabin Altimeter and Rate of Climb Module Removal Figure 401PDF p. 773

2. Cabin Altimeter and Rate of Climb Module Removal Figure 401

A. Location Zones

Zone Area 212 Flight Compartment - Right

B. Procedure

SUBTASK 21-33-07-000-001 (1) Get access to the electrical connectors on the back of the P5-16 cabin altimeter and rate of climb module on the P5 forward overhead panel: (a) Loosen the 1/4-turn fasteners that hold the P5 forward overhead panel in position and let the panel rotate downward. SUBTASK 21-33-07-020-001 (2) Remove the P5-16 cabin altimeter and rate of climb module from the P5 forward overhead panel as follows: (a) Disconnect the electrical connectors to the cabin rate of climb indicator and the cabin altitude and differential pressure indicator at the back of the module. (b) Disconnect the static pressure hose from the quick-disconnect at the back of the cabin altitude and differential pressure indicator. (c) Hold the cabin altimeter and rate of climb module in position and loosen the 1/4-turn fasteners that hold the module to the P5 forward overhead panel. (d) Remove the cabin altimeter and rate of climb module.

21-33-07-400-801Cabin Altimeter and Rate of Climb Module Installation Figure 401PDF p. 775

3. Cabin Altimeter and Rate of Climb Module Installation Figure 401

A. References

Reference Title 34-11-00-790-808 Alternate Static System Low-range Leak Test (P/B 501)

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 212 Flight Compartment - Right

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 21-33-07-020-002 (1) If it has not already been done, lower P5 forward overhead panel. SUBTASK 21-33-07-420-001 (2) Install the P5-16 cabin altimeter and rate of change module into the P5 forward overhead panel as follows: (a) Put the P5-16 cabin altimeter and rate of climb module into the P5 forward overhead panel. (b) Turn the 1/4-turn fasteners on the cabin altimeter and rate of climb module to hold the module to the P5 forward overhead panel. (c) Connect the electrical connectors to the module. (d) Connect the static pressure hose to the quick-disconnect. SUBTASK 21-33-07-410-001 (3) Lift the P5 forward overhead panel to the closed position and turn the 1/4-turn fasteners. SUBTASK 21-33-07-720-001 (4) Do this task: Alternate Static System Low-range Leak Test, TASK 34-11-00-790-808. NOTE: It is not necessary to do the Alternate Static System Low-range Leak Test, TASK 34–11–00–790–808 if the replacement module has the quick-disconnect already installed on the Cabin Altitude and Differential Pressure Indicator.

E. Prepare for the Test

NOTE: The emergency exit hatch heaters have over-temperature thermostats (Figure 501). The thermostats will turn the heaters off very shortly after they come on when the airplane is on the ground, in the air mode, with an air conditioning pack on. The exit hatch heaters will not operate when the temperature is more than approximately 70 ±5°F (21 ±3°C) (when the overheat thermostat is closed) or 50 ±7°F (10 ±4°C) (when the overheat thermostat is open due to a previous overheat condition). In warm temperatures, the heater thermostats may need to be cooled before the heaters will operate. SUBTASK 21-45-00-860-001 (1) Do this task: Supply External Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-813. (a) Feel the surface of the emergency exit hatch lining along the vertical edges. 1) Make sure that the temperature of the lining is approximately the same as the ambient air temperature. EFFECTIVITY ALL (b) Feel the surface of the trim strips of the emergency exit hatch doorway. 1) Make sure that the temperature of the trim strips is approximately the same as the ambient air temperature. (c) Feel the surface of the closeout panel. 1) Make sure that the temperature of the closeout panel is approximately the same as the ambient air temperature. SUBTASK 21-45-00-860-011 (2) Do this task: Remove Conditioned Air Supplied by a Cooling Pack, TASK 21-00-00-800-804. (3) Do this task: Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-801. NOTE: Have one person turn the air conditioning pack on. Have one or more persons check the operation of the emergency exit hatch heaters. SUBTASK 21-45-00-200-033 (6) If necessary, cool the associated control thermostat and overheat thermostat to make the heater operate. • 70°F (21°C) or less for the hatch heaters and trim heaters. • 80°F (27°C) or less for the closeout panel heater. NOTE: The time to cool the thermostats and the amount of cooling required will vary depending on the ambient temperature. NOTE: Check the heater quickly after cooling the thermostats. The thermostats will shut the hatch and trim heaters down when the heaters reach 80°F (27°C). The closeout heater will shut down at 100°F (38°C). (b) Feel the surface of the trim strips for the emergency exit hatch doorway. 1) Make sure that you feel the warmth from the heater. 21-45-01-400-801Door Area Heater InstallationPDF p. 803

3. Door Area Heater Installation (Figure 401 or Figure 402)

A. General

(1) Some of the ducts and equipment in the air distribution system are wrapped with insulation material. CFR 14 Part 121.312 mandates that insulation material installed in the fuselage as a replacement after September 2, 2005 must meet the flame propagation requirements of CFR Part 25.856, effective September 2, 2003. (2) Existing insulation material can be removed and re-installed if it is not damaged. Replacement insulation material must meet the flame propagation requirement. (3) Melamine foam insulation, G50449, BMS8-385, is the preferred foam insulation material that meets the flame propagation requirement. BMS8-385 Type 4 is the preferred foam insulation material that meets the flame propagation requirement. BMS 8-385 Type 6 and BMS 8-300 Type VIII insulation is optional to BMS8-385 Type 4. (4) Air conditioning ducts with polyimide foam insulation, G02470, must be wrapped with tape, G50327, tape, G51202, or tape, G50789, to meet the flammability/flame propagation requirements. Wrap the tape, G50327, tape, G51202, or tape, G50789, across 100% of the brown hypalon insulation surface on polyimide foam insulation, G02470. (5) Do not use BMS8-39 polyurethane foam insulation for repairs due to the degradation in flammability properties over time. (6) When insulation material is removed and re-installed, any existing tape that does not meet the flame propagation requirement must be removed or completely covered with tape that does meet the requirement. (a) Tape specifications BMS 5-157, Type I, Class 1, Grade B, composition MPVF and BMS 5-157, Type I, Class 2, Grade C, composition MPEEK are qualified tapes used to secure insulation to ducts.

G. Door Area Heater Installation

SUBTASK 21-45-01-420-011 (1) Install the forward door area heater [3] between the flex ducts as follows: EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Put the forward door area heater [3] in position with the electrical connector pointed down and the flow arrow on the heater pointed in the same direction as the flow arrow on the support structure. (b) Install the free ends of the forward and aft flex ducts on the forward door area heater [3] so that the routing of the flex ducts takes up any excess duct length as follows: 1) Use large radius bends to prevent kinking or twisting of the ducts. 2) Compress the flex duct between the support clamps. (c) Make sure the flex ducts overlap the ends of the heater duct 1.00 ±0.13 in. (2.54 ±0.33 cm). (d) Move the clamps [1] and clamp [5] into position 0.38 ±0.13 in. (0.97 ±0.34 cm) from the ends of the flex ducts. (e) Tighten the clamps [1] and clamp [5] to 16.5 ±1.5 in-lb (19.0 ±1.7 kg-cm). SUBTASK 21-45-01-420-001 (2) Install the aft door area heater [3] between the flex ducts as follows: (a) Put the aft door area heater [3] in position with the electrical connector pointed down and the flow arrow on the heater pointed in the same direction as the flow arrow on the support structure. (b) Install the free ends of the forward and aft flex ducts on the aft door area heater [3] so that the ends of the flex ducts overlap the heater duct by 1.25 ±0.13 in. (3.18 ±0.34 cm). (c) Move the clamp [1] and clamp [5] into position so they are 0.38 ±0.13 in. (0.97 ±0.34 cm) from the ends of the heater duct. (d) Tighten the clamp [1] and clamp [5] to 16.5 ±1.5 in-lb (19.0 ±1.7 kg-cm). SUBTASK 21-45-01-420-006 (3) Install the two clamps [1]. SUBTASK 21-45-01-420-007 (4) Connect the electrical connector [2] to the door area heater [3]. SUBTASK 21-45-01-410-001 (5) If the aft door area heater was installed, do this step: (a) Install the wire bundle mounting plate [8], washer [7], and nut [6].

G. Pack Flow Control Valve Operational Test

SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-008 (1) Do these steps to make sure that the left pack and right pack flow control valves are closed with the pack switches in the OFF position: (a) Put the L PACK switch and R PACK switch, on the P5 air conditioning panel, in the OFF position. (b) Make sure that the visual position indicators on the left and right flow control and shutoff valves actuator are in the closed position. SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-009 (2) Do these steps to make sure that the left and right flow control valves are partially open with the pack switches in the AUTO position: (a) Make sure that either the BLEED 1 or BLEED 2 switch, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, is set to the ON position. (b) Set the CONT CAB, FWD CAB, and AFT CAB temperature selectors, on the P5-17 temperature control module, to the AUTO (12:00 o'clock) position. (c) Put the L PACK switch and R PACK switch in the AUTO position. (d) Make sure that the visual position indicators on the left pack and right pack flow control and shutoff valves move to a partially open position. NOTE: The packs will operate. (e) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, to the OFF position. (f) Allow the packs to cool. SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-010 (3) Do these steps to make sure that the left pack and right pack flow control valves are commanded to APU high flow mode with the pack switches in the HIGH position: (a) Disconnect the electrical connector D392, from the left flow control and shutoff valve. (b) Connect a digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, between connector D392, pins 1 and 2 on the ships' wiring. (c) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, in the HIGH positions. (d) Make sure that there is 28 (± 5) VDC between pins 1 and 2 of connector D392. (e) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, to the OFF position. (f) Allow the packs to cool. EFFECTIVITY ALL 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-384 (Continued) (g) Disconnect the electrical connector D394, from the right pack flow control valve. (h) Connect a digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, between connector D394, pins 1 and 2 on the ships' wiring. (i) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, in the HIGH positions. (j) Make sure that there is 28 (± 5) VDC between pins 1 and 2 of connector D394. (k) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, in the OFF positions. (l) If necessary, allow the packs to cool. (m) Re-connect the electrical connector D392, to the left flow control and shutoff valve. (n) Re-connect the electrical connector D394, to the right flow control and shutoff valve. SUBTASK 21-51-00-710-003 (4) Do these steps to make sure that a pack in operation will go to the high flow mode when the other pack shuts down: (a) Put the airplane in the air mode, do this task: Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-801. (b) Retract the trailing edge flaps to the fully up position, do this task: Retract the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-804. (c) Put the L PACK switch to the AUTO position. (d) Put the R PACK switch to the OFF position. (e) Disconnect the connector D962, from the left flow control and shutoff valve. (f) Connect a digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, between connector D962, pins 1 and 2. (g) Make sure that there is 0 (± 5) VDC between connector D962, pins 1 and 2. 1) This makes sure that the left pack is in the engine high flow mode. (h) Re-connect the connector D962, to the left flow control and shutoff valve. (i) Put the R PACK switch to the AUTO position. (j) Put the L PACK switch to the OFF position. (k) Disconnect the connector D964, from the right flow control and shutoff valve. (l) Connect a digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, between connector D964, pins 1 and 2. (m) Make sure that there is 0 (± 5) VDC between connector D964, pins 1 and 2. 1) This makes sure that the R PACK is in the engine high flow mode. (n) Re-connect the connector D964, to the right flow control and shutoff valve. SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-038 (5) Return the airplane to the ground mode, do this task: Return the Airplane to the Ground Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-802. SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-039 (6) If required, extend the trailing edge flaps to the fully extended position, do this task: Extend the Trailing Edge Flaps, TASK 27-51-00-860-803. EFFECTIVITY ALL 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-384 (Continued) SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-011 (7) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches in the OFF position. SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-012 (8) Do this task: Remove Pressure from the Pneumatic System, TASK 36-00-00-860-806.

H. Air Cycle Machine Static Breakaway Torque Check

SUBTASK 21-51-00-010-023 WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE COOLING PACK DUCTS WHEN THEY ARE HOT. HOT DUCTS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (1) To remove the compressor outlet duct, do these steps: (a) Disconnect the flex hose from the duct. (b) Remove the electrical connector [1] from the ram air control sensor. (c) Remove the electrical connector [4] from the compressor discharge overheat switch. (d) Remove the ground clip [32] that hold the bonding jumper [33] to the clamp on the duct. EFFECTIVITY ALL (e) Remove the clamshell clamp [6] at the air cycle machine [5]. NOTE: Lift the latch pawls at the same time to release the clamp. (f) Move the sleeve [7] to the compressor outlet duct [11]. (g) Remove the coupling [2] at the heat exchanger. (h) Remove the compressor outlet duct [11]. (i) Remove and discard the packing [3] at the heat exchanger. (j) Remove and discard the packings [8]. SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-071 (2) Remove the mix muff, do this task: High Pressure Water Separator Mix Muff Removal, TASK 21-51-17-000-801. (a) Remove the flexible duct [36] from the condenser as follows: 1) Loosen the clamps [37] that attach the flexible duct to the water separator condenser. 2) Remove the flexible duct from the water separator condenser. SUBTASK 21-51-00-210-006 (3) Do a check of the flexible duct [36] that is connected to the high pressure water separator condenser for any of the conditions listed below: (a) Fraying (b) discoloration (c) rips (d) splits (e) tears (f) rupture defects. (g) If any of the above conditions are found, discard the flexible duct [36]. SUBTASK 21-51-00-720-001 (4) Do the torque check of the air cycle machine [5] as follows: CAUTION TURN THE ROTATING COMPONENTS OF THE ACM ONLY IN THE DIRECTION THAT THEY TURN WHEN IN OPERATION. IF YOU TURN THE ACM ROTATING COMPONENTS IN THE INCORRECT DIRECTION, YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE FOIL AIR BEARINGS. (a) Use a torque wrench on the nut to turn the turbine wheel in the direction of normal rotation. NOTE: Normal rotation is clockwise when viewed from the turbine end and counterclockwise when viewed from the fan end. (b) The torque necessary to turn the nut must not be more than 20 in-lb (2 N·m). 1) If the torque is more than specified, replacement of the ACM is required. NOTE: Wheel rub, endplay is too tight, dirt on the bearings or shaft, components not seated correctly, shaft surface finish, journal bearing set preload is too high, or housing assembly misalignment are probable cause for incorrect torque. SUBTASK 21-51-00-420-003 (5) Install the flexible duct [36] as follows: EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Loosely position the two clamps [37] onto the flexible duct [36]. (b) Install the flexible duct [36] onto the water separator condenser. (c) Position the forward clamp [37] to retain the flexible duct onto the water separator condenser. (d) Tighten the forward clamp [37] to 15.0 ±2.0 in-lb (1.7 ±0.2 N·m). NOTE: The aft clamp is connected in the installation of the HPWS Mix Muff in the next step. SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-072 (6) Do this task: High Pressure Water Separator Mix Muff Installation, TASK 21-51-17-400-801. SUBTASK 21-51-00-420-004 (7) To install the compressor outlet duct, do these steps: (a) Apply a light coat of grease, D00504, to the packing [3] and packings [8]. (b) Install the new packings [8] on the duct ends. (c) Install the new packing [3] at the heat exchanger. (d) Put the compressor outlet duct [11] into its position. (e) Install the coupling [2] at the heat exchanger. 1) Do not tighten the coupling [2] fully. (f) Move the sleeve [7] over the compressor outlet duct [11] connection. (g) Install the clamshell clamp [6] over the compressor outlet duct [11] connection. (h) Tighten the nut on the coupling [2] to 45.0 in-lb (5.1 N·m) - 50.0 in-lb (5.6 N·m). (i) With hand force, gently push the compressor outlet duct in the direction of the adjacent mix muff duct until the compressor outlet duct reaches the maximum flexed position. (j) Make sure that there is a minimum clearance of 0.20 in. (5.1 mm) to the adjacent mix muff duct when the compressor outlet duct is in the flexed position. (k) Apply a light coat of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the flex hose. (l) Connect the flex hose to the duct. (m) Install the electrical connector [1] for the ram air control sensor. (n) Install the electrical connector [4] for the compressor discharge overheat switch. (o) Install the ground clip [32] that hold the bonding jumper [33] to the clamp on the duct.

I. ACM Installation Test

SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-073 (1) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System (Selection), TASK 36-00-00-860-801. SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-074 (2) Put the applicable pack L PACK or R PACK switch, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, to the AUTO position. SUBTASK 21-51-00-790-001 (3) Do a soap bubble test of all the duct joints at the mix muff and at the ACM. NOTE: No air leakage is permitted. (a) If there is leakage, do these steps: 1) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches to the OFF position. EFFECTIVITY ALL WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE COOLING PACK DUCTS WHEN THEY ARE HOT. HOT DUCTS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. 2) Loosen the clamps. 3) Make sure that the ducts are aligned at the joints. 4) Tighten the clamps. 5) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches to the AUTO position. 6) Make sure that the leak has been repaired. SUBTASK 21-51-00-740-011 (4) Do a BITE test on the left and right pack/zone temperature controllers (M1442 and M1443): NOTE: This will clear any fault introduced during maintenance when power is interrupted. (a) To do the BITE test, do this task: Pack/Zone Temperature Controller BITE Test, TASK 21-61-00-700-806-002 or Pack Flow Temperature Controller BITE Test, TASK 21-61-00-740-801-002.

21-51-00-700-807Ground Pack Run Test - APU AUTO Flow ModePDF p. 876

7. Ground Pack Run Test - APU AUTO Flow Mode

A. General

(1) The objective of this task is to monitor the temperatures on the P5-17 panel while the packs are operating on the ground. The data collected from this procedure can be utilized to trend the health of the system and troubleshoot temperature control issues. The data collected over time can also help operators set the threshold at which maintenance is performed on the pack/system. For this exercise, if the Outside Air Temperature (OAT) is 75°F (24°C) or higher, set the L/R packs to the full COLD setting. If the OAT is below 75°F (24°C), maintain the packs at the 12 o’clock AUTO position for data collection.

(2) Open the access panels in the sequence that follows (TASK 06-41-00-800-801): (a) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 192DR ECS High Pressure Access Door (b) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 192CR ECS Access Door SUBTASK 21-51-00-710-044 (3) Set the LIGHTS switch on the P2-1 center instrument panel momentarily to the TEST position and make sure these lights come on and then go off: (a) MASTER CAUTION, on the P7 panel. (b) AIR COND annunciator lights, on the P7 panel. EFFECTIVITY ALL (c) PACK TRIP OFF lights, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel. SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-128 (4) Do these steps on the Flight Management Computer (FMC) to display the Flight Management Computer System (FMCS) ANALOG page 1/4: (a) Press the INIT REF function key on the Control Display Unit (CDU) front panel. (b) Push the LSK adjacent to <INDEX (LSK 6L) to show the INIT REF INDEX 1/1 page. (c) Push the LSK adjacent to MAINT> (LSK 6R) to show the MAINT BITE INDEX page. (d) Push the LSK adjacent to <FMCS (LSK 1L) to show the FMCS BITE 1/1 page. (e) Push the LSK adjacent to <DISCRETES (LSK 4L) to show the FMCS ANALOG DISC 1/4 page. (f) Use the Environmental Control System (ECS) PACK H/L (high flow, low flow) line entry on the ANALOG DISC 1/4 page. (g) The following information can be displayed on the FMC: 1) ECS PACK ON/OFF (LEFT and RIGHT) a) Indicates if the left or right pack is on or off. 2) ECS PACK H/L LO HI (LEFT and RIGHT) a) Indicates the pack is in the low flow mode or if it has been commanded to the high flow mode. NOTE: A pack can be commanded to the high flow mode even if it is off. 3) ISOLATION VALVE OPEN (CLOSED) a) Indicates if the valve is open or closed. SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-129 (5) Set these switches, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, as follows: (a) Set the BLEED 1 and 2 switches to the OFF position. (b) Set the APU BLEED switch to the OFF position. (c) Set the L and R PACK switches the OFF position. (d) Set the ISOLATION VALVE switch to the CLOSE position. (e) Set the L and R RECIRC FAN switches to the OFF position.

E. Ground Pack Run Test - APU AUTO Flow Mode

SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-130 (1) Do this task to start the APU: APU Starting and Operation, TASK 49-11-00-860-801. SUBTASK 21-51-00-970-004 (2) Make a record of the OAT and dew point (humidity) on the data collection sheet: Table 501. Table 501/21-51-00-993-803 Temperature Data Sheet Outside Air Temperature (OAT): Temperature Panel Selector Setting: Time t= 0 minute t= 5 minutes t= 10 minutes t= 15 minutes R PACK L PACK EFFECTIVITY ALL Table 501/21-51-00-993-803 Temperature Data Sheet (Continued) Outside Air Temperature (OAT): Temperature Panel Selector Setting: Time t= 0 minute t= 5 minutes t= 10 minutes t= 15 minutes PASS CAB FWD AFT SUPPLY DUCT CONT CAB FWD CAB AFT CAB LEFT STCV POSITION LEFT TCV POSITION CONTROL CABIN TAV POSITION IS THERE LEAKAGE FROM THE LEFT HEAT EXCHANGER? IS THERE LEAKAGE FROM THE LEFT CONDENSER? IS THERE ICE ON THE LEFT CONDITIONED AIR CHECK VALVE? RIGHT STCV POSITION RIGHT TCV POSITION FORWARD TAV POSITION AFT TAV POSITION IS THERE LEAKAGE FROM THE RIGHT HEAT EXCHANGER? IS THERE LEAKAGE FROM THE RIGHT CONDENSER? IS THERE ICE ON THE RIGHT CONDITIONED AIR CHECK VALVE? SUBTASK 21-51-00-710-045 (3) Make sure that all doors are closed. SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-131 (4) Set these switches, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, to reflect the APU AUTO flow mode: NOTE: The engines should be OFF when recording temperature readings in APU AUTO flow mode. (a) Set the BLEED 1 switch to the ON position. (b) Set the APU BLEED switch to the ON position. (c) Set the ISOLATION VALVE switch to the AUTO position. (d) Set the L and R RECIRC FAN switches to the AUTO position. (e) Set the L and R PACK switches the AUTO position. (f) Set the TRIM AIR switch to the ON Position. EFFECTIVITY ALL (g) Make sure that the correct FLOW MODE configuration is displayed on the FMC. SUBTASK 21-51-00-970-005 (5) Make a record on the data sheet of Table 501 at t= 0 minute: (a) Record the following temperatures on the P5-17 temperature control panel: 1) R PACK / L PACK 2) PASS CAB: a) FWD b) AFT. 3) SUPPLY DUCT: a) CONT CAB b) FWD CAB c) AFT CAB. (b) Record if the position is OPEN, MODULATING, or CLOSED for the following: 1) Left and right Standby Temperature Control Valve (STCV) 2) Left and right Temperature Control Valve (TCV) 3) Trim Air Valve (TAV) a) Control Cabin b) Forward Cabin c) Aft Cabin SUBTASK 21-51-00-970-006 (6) Repeat the recordings of the temperatures and positions on the data sheet of Table 501 at t= 5 minutes. SUBTASK 21-51-00-970-007 (7) Repeat the recordings of the temperatures and positions on the data sheet of Table 501 at t= 10 minutes. SUBTASK 21-51-00-970-008 (8) Repeat the recordings of the temperatures and positions on the data sheet of Table 501 at t= 15 minutes. SUBTASK 21-51-00-200-003 (9) Make sure that there are no leakages from the Left/Right Heat Exchanger. (a) Make a record on the data sheet of Table 501. SUBTASK 21-51-00-200-004 (10) Make sure that there are no leakages from the Left/Right Condenser. (a) Make a record on the data sheet of Table 501. SUBTASK 21-51-00-200-005 (11) Do a check to see if there is ice on the Left/Right Conditioned Air Check Valve. NOTE: Ice is an indicator that the pack is performing well. (a) Make a record on the data sheet of Table 501.

F. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-132 (1) Set these switches, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, as follows: EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Set the BLEED 1 switch to the OFF position. (b) Set the APU BLEED switch to the OFF position. (c) Set the L and R PACK switches the OFF position. 1) Make sure that the L and R PACK indicate a duct pressure of zero. 2) Make sure that the PACK configuration on the FMC is correct. (d) Set the ISOLATION VALVE switch to the CLOSE position. (e) Set the L and R RECIRC FAN switches to the OFF position. SUBTASK 21-51-00-860-133 (2) Do this task: APU Usual Shutdown, TASK 49-11-00-860-802. SUBTASK 21-51-00-410-032 (3) Close the access panels in the sequence that follows (TASK 06-41-00-800-801): (a) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 192CR ECS Access Door (b) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 192DR ECS High Pressure Access Door NOTE: The ECS high pressure access door, 192DR, will not latch in its position if the ECS access door, 192CR, is not closed. SUBTASK 21-51-00-410-033 (4) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 192CL ECS Access Door

G. Flow Control and Shutoff Valve Installation

SUBTASK 21-51-01-010-042-002 (1) Remove the covers from the duct openings. SUBTASK 21-51-01-020-070-002 (2) Install the bonding jumper on the flow control and shutoff valve [26]. (a) Set the bonding jumper [30] on the flow control and shutoff valve. (b) Install the screw [33], washers [34], and nut [35]. SUBTASK 21-51-01-980-005-002 (3) Put the flow control and shutoff valve [26] in its position. SUBTASK 21-51-01-420-011-002 (4) Loosely install the two clamps [27]. SUBTASK 21-51-01-420-012-002 (5) Install the screw [32] and washer [31] that connect the bonding jumper [30] to the structure. (a) Make sure that you install any other bonding jumpers that you disconnected for this procedure. SUBTASK 21-51-01-020-071-002 (6) Install the sense line on the flow control and shutoff valve [26]. (a) Install a new O-ring [28] on the reducer [29]. (b) Apply a layer of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the reducer [29]. (c) Install the reducer [29] on the flow control and shutoff valve [26]. 1) Tighten the reducer [29] to 140 ±7 in-lb (15.8 ±0.8 N·m). (d) Install the B-nut on the sense line. 1) Tighten the B-nut on the sense line to 170 ±9 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m). (k) Apply a light coat of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the flexhose [2]. (l) Connect the flexhose [2] to the duct. H. Flow Control and Shutoff Valve Installation Test

SUBTASK 21-51-01-860-050-002 (1) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System with the APU, TASK 36-00-00-860-803. SUBTASK 21-51-01-860-051-002 (2) Make sure that the flow control valve is closed with the applicable pack switch in the OFF position. (a) Put the applicable L PACK switch or R PACK switch in the OFF position. (b) Make sure that the position indicator on the flow control and shutoff valve is in the closed position. SUBTASK 21-51-01-860-052-002 (3) Make sure that the flow control valve is partially open with the applicable pack switch in the AUTO position. (a) Put the applicable L PACK switch or R PACK switch in the AUTO position. (b) Make sure that the position indicator on the flow control and shutoff valve moves to a partially open position. SUBTASK 21-51-01-860-053-002 (4) Make sure that the left flow control valve is commanded to HIGH with the pack switch in the HIGH position. (a) Disconnect the electrical connector D392 from the left flow control valve. (b) Connect a digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793, between the electrical connector D392, pins 1 and 2. (c) Put the L PACK switch in the HIGH position. (d) Make sure that there is 28±5 VDC between the electrical connector D392, pins 1 and 2. (e) Put the L PACK switch in the AUTO position. (f) Connect the electrical connector D392 to the left flow control valve. SUBTASK 21-51-01-740-001-002 (5) Do a BITE test on the left and right pack/zone temperature controllers (M1442 and M1443): NOTE: This will clear any fault introduced during maintenance when power is interrupted. (a) Do this task: Pack/Zone Temperature Controller BITE Test, TASK 21-61-00-700-806-002. SUBTASK 21-51-01-790-005-002 (6) Make sure that there is no air leakage at the couplings or the sense line connections you removed for this task. SUBTASK 21-51-01-860-054-002 (7) Put the applicable L PACK switch or R PACK switch in the OFF position. SUBTASK 21-51-01-860-055-002 (8) Do this task: Remove Pressure from the Pneumatic System, TASK 36-00-00-860-806.

F. Right Flow Control and Shutoff Valve Removal

SUBTASK 21-51-01-010-039-002 (1) To get access to the flow control and shutoff valve, remove the Air Cycle Machine (ACM) (TASK 21-51-04-000-802-002). SUBTASK 21-51-01-010-040-002 (3) Remove the compressor inlet duct [52]. CAUTION HOLD THE DUCT WHEN YOU LOOSEN THE CLAMP. THE DUCT CAN FALL WHEN THE CLAMP IS LOOSE. THE DUCT CAN BE DAMAGED IF IT FALLS. (a) Remove the clamshell clamp [53]. 1) Lift the three latch pawls at the same time to release the clamshell clamp [53]. (a) Remove the nut [58] and washer [59] that hold the air line and water line from the High Pressure Water Separator (HPWS) to the trim air duct. SUBTASK 21-51-01-020-086-003 (3) Remove the mix muff, do this task: High Pressure Water Separator Mix Muff Removal, TASK 21-51-17-000-801. (b) Move the bonding jumper [25] away from the air cycle machine. 1) Do not remove the ground clip from the bonding jumper. Config 3 EFFECTIVITY 385-999 (c) Remove the bolts [21] that hold the duct to the air cycle machine. (d) Remove and discard the O-ring [22]. CAUTION HOLD THE DUCT WHEN YOU LOOSEN THE CLAMP. THE DUCT CAN FALL WHEN THE CLAMP IS LOOSE. THE DUCT CAN BE DAMAGED IF IT FALLS. (e) Remove the clamshell clamp [17]. 1) Lift the three latch pawls at the same time to release the clamshell clamp [17]. (f) Move the sleeve [18] to the compressor inlet duct [20]. (g) Remove and discard the seals [19]. SUBTASK 21-51-01-020-077-003 (5) Disconnect these electrical connectors from the flow control and shutoff valve [26]: • D15818 • D15830 • D15832. SUBTASK 21-51-01-020-101-003 (6) Remove the screw [71], washers [72], and nut [73] from the clamps [74] to disconnect the wiring from the flow control and shutoff valve [26]. SUBTASK 21-51-01-020-078-003 (7) Remove the bonding jumper [35] from the valve bonding tab [36] on the flow control and shutoff valve [26] as follows: (a) Remove the nut [34], screw [33], and washers [32]. (b) Remove the bonding jumper [35] from the flow control and shutoff valve [26]. SUBTASK 21-51-01-020-079-003 (8) Remove the flow control and shutoff valve [26] from the ducts as follows: (a) Support the flow control and shutoff valve [26]. (b) Loosen the clamp T-bolts and remove the clamps [29]. (c) Remove the flow control and shutoff valve [26]. SUBTASK 21-51-01-000-001-003 (1) If it is necessary, remove the Air Cycle Machine (ACM), to get access to the flow control and shutoff valve (TASK 21-51-04-000-802-002). SUBTASK 21-51-01-020-091-003 (2) Remove the mix muff duct [51] as follows: (a) Hold the mix muff duct [51] while you remove the coupling [56]. (b) Remove the mix muff duct [51]. SUBTASK 21-51-01-020-090-003 (3) Remove the compressor inlet duct [52] as follows: CAUTION HOLD THE DUCT WHEN YOU LOOSEN THE CLAMP. THE DUCT CAN FALL WHEN THE CLAMP IS LOOSE. Config 3 EFFECTIVITY 385-999 (b) Disconnect the B-nut [57] on the air line and water line. NOTE: The sense lines must be completely disconnected from the HPWS manifold to allow movement of the sense lines. (c) Open the B-nut [57] at the union on the lower sense line [60] to the ACM. (d) Rotate the sense line down to allow clearance to remove the flow control and shutoff valve [61]. SUBTASK 21-51-01-020-081-003 (5) Disconnect these electrical connectors from the flow control and shutoff valve [61]: • D15820 • D15834 • D15836. (b) Remove the bonding jumper [69]. SUBTASK 21-51-01-020-088-003 (7) Remove the flow control and shutoff valve [61] from the ducts as follows: (a) Support the flow control and shutoff valve [61]. (b) Loosen the clamp T-bolts and remove the clamps [63]. (c) Carefully remove the flow control and shutoff valve [61]. NOTE: You may move the sense lines you disconnected to remove the shutoff valve. Be careful not to damage the sense lines. SUBTASK 21-51-01-480-002-003 (8) Put covers on the duct openings to keep out unwanted materials.

H. Flow Control and Shutoff Valve Installation

SUBTASK 21-51-01-080-001-003 (1) Remove the covers from the duct openings. SUBTASK 21-51-01-420-014-003 (2) Put the flow control and shutoff valve [26] in its installed position. SUBTASK 21-51-01-420-020-003 (3) Loosely install the two clamps [29] that attach the valve to the ducts. SUBTASK 21-51-01-420-015-003 (4) Do these steps to install the bonding jumper [35] on the flow control and shutoff valve [26]: (a) Soak a cleaning wiper, G50262, with alcohol, B00068, or alcohol, B50073, until it is saturated with the solvent. (b) Clean all bonding surfaces of the valve bonding tab [36], washer [32] under the bonding tab, and surface of the bonding jumper [35] with wiper, G50262. (c) Use a clean wiper, G50262, to remove all traces of the solvent from the bonding surfaces. (d) Install the screw [33], washers [32], and nut [34] that connect the bonding jumper [35] to the valve bonding tab [36] on the flow control and shutoff valve [26]. (e) Tighten the nut to 33 in-lb (3.7 N·m) - 40 in-lb (4.5 N·m). (f) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the surface of the valve bonding tab [36] and surface of the bonding jumper [35]: 1) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. 2) Make sure that the resistance is 0.010 ohm (10 milliohm) or less. SUBTASK 21-51-01-420-018-003 (5) Install the electrical connectors listed below on the flow control and shutoff valve [26]: • D15818 electrical connector Config 3 EFFECTIVITY 385-999 • D15830 electrical connector • D15832 electrical connector. SUBTASK 21-51-01-420-019-003 (6) Determine the running torque of the nut on each clamp [29] trunnion as follows: NOTE: The running torque is the torque required to just turn the locknut on the trunnion. The running torque should be 7 in-lb (0.8 N·m) - 10 in-lb (1.1 N·m). (a) With an appropriate torque wrench, measure the torque that is required to turn the locknut on the trunnion. 1) Make a record of this value. SUBTASK 21-51-01-420-026-003 (7) Tighten each locknut on the clamp [29] trunnions as follows: (a) Tighten the locknut to 5 in-lb (0.6 N·m) above the running torque. NOTE: If the running torque was measured at 8 in-lb (0.9 N·m), the torque required will be 13 in-lb (1.5 N·m). (b) Make sure that the alignment of the valve flange on the adjoining duct flange is satisfactory. (c) Tighten the locknut to 60 +5 / -0 in-lb (6.8 +0.6 / -0.0 N·m). SUBTASK 21-51-01-420-042-003 (8) Install the screw [71], washers [72], and nut [73] to the clamps [74]. SUBTASK 21-51-01-410-025-003 (9) Do these steps to install the compressor inlet duct [20]: (a) If necessary, apply a light layer of distilled water, G01061, or grease, D00504, or Molykote 44 grease, medium, D50104, to the new O-ring [22]. NOTE: The lubrication will provide easy installation of the new O-ring [22]. (b) Install the O-ring [22]. (c) Put the ground clip [24] over the bolt [23]. (d) Hold the compressor inlet duct [20] in its position. (e) Install the bolt [23] that holds the ground clip [24] to the air cycle machine. (f) Install the bolts [21] that hold the duct to the air cycle machine. (g) Apply a light coat grease, D00504, or Molykote 44 grease, medium, D50104, to the new seals [19]. (h) Install the seals [19]. (i) Move the sleeve [18] over the duct ends. (j) Install the clamshell clamp [17]. 1) Push the two halves of the clamshell clamp [17] together until the three latch pawls are latched. SUBTASK 21-51-01-420-031-003 (10) Install the mix muff [13], do this task: High Pressure Water Separator Mix Muff Installation, TASK 21-51-17-400-801. SUBTASK 21-51-01-410-024-003 (11) Do these steps to install the mix muff duct [4]: (a) Hold the mix muff duct [4] in its position. Config 3 EFFECTIVITY 385-999 (b) Install the couplings [3]. (c) Tighten the couplings [3] to 60 in-lb (6.8 N·m) - 65 in-lb (7.3 N·m). (d) Use wiper, G50262, moist in alcohol, B00130, or solvent, B00184, to clean the mating surfaces of the screw [5], washers [6], nut [7], bonding jumper [36], bonding jumper [37], and bonding tab of the mix muff duct [4]. (e) Put the bonding jumper [36] and bonding jumper [37] on the mix muff duct [4]. (f) Install the nut [7], washers [6], and screw [5] that hold the bonding jumper [36] and bonding jumper [37] to the mix muff duct [4]. 1) Tighten the nut [7] to 33 in-lb (3.7 N·m) - 40 in-lb (4.5 N·m). (g) Measure the electrical resistance between the bonding jumper [36] and bonding tab of the mix muff duct [4]. 1) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. 2) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.001 ohm (1.0 milliohm) or less. SUBTASK 21-51-01-410-023-003 (12) Install the compressor outlet duct [10] as follows: (a) If necessary, apply a light layer of distilled water, G01061, grease, D00504, or Molykote 44 grease, medium, D50104, to the new packing [16] and new O-rings [12]. NOTE: The lubrication will provide easy installation of the new packing [16] and new O-rings [12]. (b) Install the O-rings [12] on the duct ends. (c) Install the packing [16] at the heat exchanger. (d) Put the compressor outlet duct [10] into its position. (e) Apply compound, D50320, to the bolt threads of the clamp [15]. (f) Install the clamp [15] at the heat exchanger. NOTE: Do not tighten the clamp fully. (g) Install the clamp [11] over the outlet duct connection. (h) Tighten the nut on the clamp [15] to 45 in-lb (5.1 N·m) - 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m). (i) With hand force, carefully push the compressor outlet duct [10] in the direction of the adjacent mix muff duct [4] until the compressor outlet duct [10] is at the position of maximum flex. (j) Make sure that there is a minimum clearance of 0.20 in. (5.1 mm) to the adjacent mix muff duct [4] when the compressor outlet duct [10] is at the position of maximum flex. (k) Install the new packing [40] on the compressor outlet duct [10]. 1) Clean the packing [40] with cotton wiper, G00034. 2) Apply lubricant, D00602, to the packing [40]. (l) Apply a light layer of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the flexhose [2]. (m) Connect the flexhose [2] to the duct. (n) Install the electrical connector [1] for the ram air control sensor. (o) Install the electrical connector [14] for the compressor discharge overheat switch. Config 3 EFFECTIVITY 385-999 SUBTASK 21-51-01-440-001-003 (13) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name C 6 C00262 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONT VALVES L SUBTASK 21-51-01-440-002-003 (14) Remove the DO-NOT-OPERATE tags from these switches, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel: • The L PACK and R PACK switches • The BLEED 1 and BLEED 2 switches • The BLEED APU switch.
