F. Air Conditioning Accessory Unit (ACAU) Installation Test

SUBTASK 21-51-02-710-010 (1) Do this test of the ACAU [1]: NOTE: If you replaced the Air Conditioning Accessory Unit (ACAU M324 or M1455) because it had a defect, it is recommended that the complete adjustment/test procedure for the affected system be performed. For example, if an ACAU was replaced to correct a defect in the ram air system, then it is recommended that a test of the ram air system be performed. If the ACAU is being replaced for any other reason you may do just the test that follows: (a) If you installed the M324 ACAU, do this test of the left pack overheat relay: 1) Make sure that the L and R PACK switches, on the P5-10 Air Conditioning Panel, are set to OFF position. 2) Make sure that this circuit breaker is closed: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name C 8 C01176 A/C PACK/ENGINE BLEED AIR OVHT LEFT 3) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 192CL ECS Access Door 4) Disconnect electrical connector D532 from the left compressor discharge overheat switch, S2. 5) Install a jumper wire between pins 1 and 2 of connector D532 on the ships' wiring. 6) Make sure that the left PACK light, on the P5-10 Air Conditioning Panel, comes on. 7) Make sure that the AIR COND and MASTER CAUTION lights, on the P7 glareshield panel, come on. 8) Remove the jumper wire that was installed between pins 1 and 2 of connector D532 on the ships' wiring. 9) Reconnect electrical connector D532 to the left compressor discharge overheat switch, S2. 10) Depress the TRIP RESET switch, on the P5-10 Air Conditioning Panel. 11) Make sure the left PACK light, on the P5-10 Air Conditioning Panel, goes off. 12) If the MASTER CAUTION or AIR COND annunciator lights are on, push and release one of the two MASTER CAUTION lights. 13) Make sure the AIR COND and MASTER CAUTION lights, on the P7 glareshield panel, go off. 14) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 192CL ECS Access Door (b) If you installed the M1455 ACAU, do this test of the right pack overheat relay: 1) Make sure that the L and R PACK switches, on the P5-10 Air Conditioning Panel, are set to OFF position. EFFECTIVITY ALL 2) Make sure that this circuit breaker is closed: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name C 7 C01177 A/C PACK/ENGINE BLEED AIR OVHT RIGHT CAUTION DO NOT OPEN THE ECS ACCESS DOOR 192CR, UNTIL YOU OPEN THE ECS HIGH PRESSURE ACCESS DOOR 192DR. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE ECS HIGH PRESSURE ACCESS DOOR 192DR, ITS LATCHES AND HINGES CAN OCCUR. 3) Do these steps to get access to the Environmental Control System (ECS) Access Door (TASK 06-41-00-800-801): a) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 192DR ECS High Pressure Access Door b) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 192CR ECS Access Door 4) Disconnect electrical connector D538 from the right compressor discharge overheat switch, S5. 5) Install a jumper wire between pins 1 and 2 of connector D538 on the ships' wiring. 6) Make sure the right PACK light, on the P5-10 Air Conditioning Panel, comes on. 7) Make sure that the AIR COND and MASTER CAUTION lights, on the P7 glareshield panel, come on. 8) Remove the jumper wire that was installed between pins 1 and 2 of connector D538 on the ships' wiring. 9) Reconnect electrical connector D538 to the right compressor discharge overheat switch, S5. 10) Depress the TRIP RESET switch, on the P5-10 Air Conditioning Panel. 11) Make sure the right PACK light, on the P5-10 Air Conditioning Panel, goes off. 12) If the MASTER CAUTION or AIR COND annunciator lights are on, push and release one of the two MASTER CAUTION lights. 13) Make sure the AIR COND and MASTER CAUTION lights, on the P7 glareshield, go off. 14) To close these access panels, do these steps (TASK 06-41-00-800-801): a) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 192CR ECS Access Door b) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 192DR ECS High Pressure Access Door NOTE: The ECS high pressure access door, 192DR, will not latch in its position if the ECS access door, 192CR, is not closed. SUBTASK 21-51-02-710-012 (1) Do these checks for the post-installation test of the M324 ACAU No. 1: (a) Do a test of the left pack overheat relay: 1) Set the L PACK and R PACK switches, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, to OFF the position. Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL 2) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name C 8 C01176 A/C PACK/ENGINE BLEED AIR OVHT LEFT 3) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 192CL ECS Access Door 4) Disconnect electrical connector D532 from the left compressor discharge overheat switch, S2. 5) Install a jumper wire between pins 1 and 2 of connector D532 on the ships' wiring. 6) Make sure that the left PACK light, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, comes on. 7) Make sure that the AIR COND and MASTER CAUTION lights, on the P7 glareshield panel, come on. 8) Remove the jumper wire that was installed between pins 1 and 2 of connector D532 on the ships' wiring. 9) Reconnect electrical connector D532 to the left compressor discharge overheat switch, S2. 10) Push the TRIP RESET switch on the P5-10 air conditioning panel. 11) Make sure that the left PACK light, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, goes off. 12) If the MASTER CAUTION or AIR COND annunciator lights are on, push and release one of the two MASTER CAUTION lights. 13) Make sure that the AIR COND and MASTER CAUTION lights, on the P7 glareshield panel, go off. 14) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 192CL ECS Access Door (b) Do a test of the left ram air system relays: 1) Make sure that the left RAM DOOR FULL OPEN light is on. 2) Make sure that the deflector door for the left ram air inlet is extended. 3) Make sure that the AIR/GND logic shows that the airplane is in the GND logic. 4) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 192CL ECS Access Door 006, 007, 013, 014, 018, 019 5) Disconnect electrical connector D486 from the left pack valve. NOTE: A disconnected D486 connector simulates that the left pack valve is open. Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL 020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 6) Disconnect electrical connector D40844 from the left pack valve. NOTE: A disconnected D40844 connector simulates that the left pack valve is open. ALL 7) Extend the trailing edge flaps to Flaps Position 1 (TASK 27-51-00-860-803). 8) Make sure that the deflector door for the left ram air system is fully extended. 9) Put the airplane in the air mode (TASK 32-09-00-860-801). 10) Make sure that these results occur: a) Make sure that the left ram air inlet deflector door retracts fully. b) Make sure that the left RAM DOOR FULL OPEN light remains on. 11) Retract the trailing edge flaps to the fully up position (TASK 27-51-00-860-804). 12) Make sure that these results occur: a) Make sure that the left ram air inlet modulation panels move toward the closed position. b) Make sure that the left RAM DOOR FULL OPEN light goes off. 13) Return the airplane to the ground mode (TASK 32-09-00-860-802). 14) Make sure that these results occur: a) Make sure that the left RAM DOOR FULL OPEN light comes on. b) Make sure that the left ram air inlet modulation panels move to the fully open position. c) Make sure that the left ram air inlet deflector door moves to the extended position. 15) Reconnect all electrical connectors that were disconnected. (c) Do a test of the left engine bleed air overheat relay: 1) Set these switches, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, to the OFF position: a) APU BLEED b) BLEED 1 c) BLEED 2 d) L PACK e) R PACK. 2) Make sure that this circuit breaker is closed: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name C 8 C01176 A/C PACK/ENGINE BLEED AIR OVHT LEFT 3) Get access to the left engine bleed air overtemperature switch: a) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 431CL Forward Strut Fairing, Left Overwing Fairing, Strut 1 Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL 4) Disconnect the electrical connector D526 from the engine 1 bleed air overtemperature switch, S20. 5) Install a jumper cable between pins 1 and 2 of connector D526 on the ships' wiring. 6) Make sure that the left pack BLEED TRIP OFF light, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, comes on. 7) Make sure that the AIR COND and MASTER CAUTION lights, on the P7 glareshield panel, come on. 8) Remove the jumper wire that was installed between pins 1 and 2 of connector D526 on the ships' wiring. 9) Reconnect electrical connector D526 to the left engine air overtemperature switch S20. 10) Depress the TRIP RESET switch on the P5-10 air conditioning panel. 11) Make sure that the left pack BLEED TRIP OFF light, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, goes off. 12) Push and release one of the two MASTER CAUTION lights on the P7 glareshield panel. 13) Make sure that the AIR COND and MASTER CAUTION lights, on the P7 glareshield panel, go off. (d) Do a test of the cabin air recirculation fan relays: 1) Do an operational test of the recirculation system (TASK 21-25-00-710-802-002). (e) Do a test of the left engine start sense relay: WARNING MAKE SURE THAT PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT STAY AWAY FROM THE LEADING EDGE SLATS, TRAILING EDGE FLAPS, AND DRIVE MECHANISMS. THE FLAPS, SLATS, AND DRIVE MECHANISMS MOVE QUICKLY. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. 1) Do this task: Leading Edge Flaps and Slats Retraction, TASK 27-81-00-860-804. 2) Do this task: Leading Edge Flaps and Slats Deactivation, TASK 27-81-00-040-801. 3) Do this task: Thrust Reverser Deactivation For Ground Maintenance, TASK 78-31-00-040-802-F00. 4) For the left thrust reverser, do this task: Open the Thrust Reverser (Selection), TASK 78-31-00-010-801-F00. 5) Do this task: Open the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-010-801-F00. 6) Set these switches, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, to the OFF position: a) APU BLEED b) BLEED 1 c) BLEED 2 7) Disconnect the electrical connector DP1102 from the engine 1 bleed air regulator. 8) Connect a voltmeter set on the DC voltage scale between pin 5 and pin 6 of electrical connector DP1102. 9) Make sure that the voltmeter shows less than 10V dc. 10) Set the BLEED 1 switch, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, to the ON position. Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL 11) Make sure that the voltmeter shows 20 to 29V dc. 12) Manually turn the engine 1 pneumatic start valve 30 degrees clockwise. 13) Make sure that the voltmeter shows less than 10V dc. 14) Move the voltmeter lead from pin 5. 15) Connect the voltmeter positive lead to pin 7. 16) Make sure that the voltmeter shows 20 to 29V dc. 17) Release the pneumatic start valve. 18) Make sure that the voltmeter shows less than 10V dc. 19) Connect the electrical connector DP1102 to the engine 1 bleed air regulator. 20) Set the BLEED 1 switch, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, to the OFF position. 21-51-03-160-811Heat Exchanger - Blowing Out Debris/Blockages with Nitrogen Gas/Compressed AirPDF p. 959

2. Heat Exchanger - Blowing Out Debris/Blockages with Nitrogen Gas/Compressed Air (Figure 201, Figure 202) NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. General

(1) recommends performing this clearing procedure using nitrogen gas/compressed air to effectively clear blocked heat exchangers. (2) This task includes instructions to blow out debris or contaminant blockages trapped within the cool air side heat exchanger grills. (a) This is an effective method for clearing debris/blockages, especially for aircraft operating in challenging environments (cottonwood/bug season, etc.). (b) This method does not clean/break down contaminants (dust, dirt, airborne particles, pollen, etc.) baked onto the heat exchanger grills over time.

I. Heat Exchanger - Blowing Out Debris/Blockages with Nitrogen Gas/Compressed Air

SUBTASK 21-51-03-160-010 (1) To blow out debris/blockages with nitrogen gas/compressed air in the heat exchanger grills with the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, do the following steps: EFFECTIVITY ALL WARNING COMPRESSED GAS CAN BE DANGEROUS. EYE PROTECTION IS MANDATORY. APPLY DRY NITROGEN CAREFULLY IN DIRECTION AWAY FROM EYES AND FACE AND OTHER PERSONNEL TO AVOID POSSIBLE INJURY. (a) Blow out contaminant blockages with compressed clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018 (Figure 202). 1) Connect one end of the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, air hose to either the 0-200psig dry filtered regulated air source, STD-6452, or nitrogen source, STD-1290, outlet. NOTE: The cleaning wand, SPL-14922, includes an air hose, air wand, water hose, water wand, and soap injector. 2) Connect other end of the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, air hose to the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, air wand inlet. NOTE: The adjustable neck of the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, can be lengthened or shortened by its number of beads. It is acceptable to adjust the length by adding or removing the beads as necessary. 3) Adjust the regulator on compressed clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, to supply a recommended pressure of 100 psi (689 kPa) maximum to the cleaning wand, SPL-14922. CAUTION DO NOT TOUCH THE COOLING FINS OF THE HEAT EXCHANGERS WITH THE TIP OF THE CLEANING WAND. DAMAGE TO THE COOLING FINS OF THE HEAT EXCHANGERS CAN OCCUR. 4) Insert the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, through the plenum/diffuser access openings and blow clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, through the cooling fins of the primary and secondary heat exchangers. a) Make sure that the cooling fins of the heat exchanger are not damaged when the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, was inserted through the plenum/diffuser access panel openings. b) Squeeze the handle on the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, air wand to blow the clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, through the heat exchangers until all debris is blown out of the cooling fins. <1> Make sure that the pressure gauge on the regulator does not indicate more than 100 psi (689 kPa) when the cleaning wand, SPL-14922 operates. <2> Blow the clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, through all the areas of the heat exchangers. <3> Make sure that dirt, sand, gravel or plant fiber is no longer being blown out on the opposite side (inlet side) of the heat exchanger. <4> Continue blowing the clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, through the heat exchangers until debris is no longer detected being blown out. c) Make sure that all loose dirt, sand, gravel, and plant fiber is removed from the ram air inlet that was blown out of the heat exchangers. 5) Remove the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, from the inside of the plenum/diffuser access opening. EFFECTIVITY ALL 6) Decrease the compressed clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, pressure to 0 psi (0 kPa). 7) Remove the cleaning wand, SPL-14922. SUBTASK 21-51-03-160-011 (2) To blow out heat exchanger debris/blockage with nitrogen gas/compressed air with the heating exchanger cleaning wand, SPL-10099, do the following steps: WARNING COMPRESSED GAS CAN BE DANGEROUS. EYE PROTECTION IS MANDATORY. APPLY DRY NITROGEN CAREFULLY IN DIRECTION AWAY FROM EYES AND FACE AND OTHER PERSONNEL TO AVOID POSSIBLE INJURY. (a) Attach the heating exchanger cleaning wand, SPL-10099, to the regulator on a clean dry air, G50321, bottle or nitrogen, G00018, bottle. (b) Adjust the regulator on a clean dry air, G50321, bottle or nitrogen, G00018, bottle to supply a maximum of 80 psi (552 kPa) to the heating exchanger cleaning wand, SPL-10099. NOTE: If a clean dry air, G50321, bottle is used, the moisture contaminant or water concentration in the air of 0.00002 grams maximum is not required. CAUTION DO NOT TOUCH THE COOLING FINS OF THE HEAT EXCHANGERS WITH THE TIP OF THE CLEANING WAND. DAMAGE TO THE COOLING FINS OF THE HEAT EXCHANGERS CAN OCCUR. (c) Insert the heating exchanger cleaning wand, SPL-10099, through the plenum/diffuser access openings and blow clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, through the cooling fins of the primary and secondary heat exchangers: 1) Make sure that the cooling fins of the heat exchanger are not damaged when the heating exchanger cleaning wand, SPL-10099, was inserted through the plenum/diffuser access panel openings. 2) Blow the clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, through the heat exchangers until all debris is blown out of the cooling fins. a) Make sure that the pressure gauge on the heating exchanger cleaning wand, SPL-10099, does not indicate more than 80 psi (552 kPa) when the wand operates. b) Blow the clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, through all the areas of the heat exchangers. c) Make sure that dirt, sand, gravel or plant fiber is no longer being blown out on the opposite side (inlet side) of the heat exchanger. d) Continue blowing the clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, through the heat exchangers until debris is no longer detected being blown out. 3) Make sure that all loose dirt, sand, gravel, and plant fiber is removed from the ram air inlet that was blown out of the heat exchangers. (d) Remove the heating exchanger cleaning wand, SPL-10099, from the inside of the plenum/diffuser access opening and decrease the clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, pressure to 0 psi (0 kPa). EFFECTIVITY ALL

I. Air Cycle Machine Inspection

NOTE: recommends to do an inspection of the air cycle machine when you get access to the fan wheel. This inspection makes sure that the component operates correctly and helps to prevent a non-scheduled removal. If you remove the heat exchanger and plenum/diffuser assembly to clean the off-wing heat exchanger and do not have ECS related problems, then the air cycle machine inspection is not necessary. SUBTASK 21-51-03-211-002 (1) When the secondary plenum/diffuser [23] is removed from the air cycle machine [39], do these steps to inspect the impeller blade [74] of the air cycle machine [39]: (a) Make sure that the chord length (width) of each tip of impeller blade [74] is a minimum of 0.38 in. (9.65 mm). (b) Do a visual check that no impeller blade [74] is broken or cracked. Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL (c) Replace the air cycle machine [39] with a new or serviceable unit if the inspection is unsatisfactory. SUBTASK 21-51-03-700-003 (2) Do a check of the torque necessary to turn the rotating assembly of the air cycle machine [39] as follows: (a) Put the air cycle machine [39] in a horizontal position. (b) Put a torque wrench on the nut [73]. NOTE: A torque wrench with a gage that shows the torque applied is recommended. 1) Turn the nut [72] if the air cycle machine [39] was not removed from the secondary plenum/diffuser [23]. CAUTION TURN THE ROTATING COMPONENTS OF THE ACM ONLY IN THE DIRECTION THAT THEY TURN WHEN IN OPERATION. IF YOU TURN THE ACM ROTATING COMPONENTS IN THE INCORRECT DIRECTION, YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE FOIL AIR BEARINGS. (c) Make sure that the nut [72] is turned clockwise or nut [73] is turned counterclockwise while the rotating assembly is turned. (d) Record the torque necessary to turn the rotating assembly. (e) If the torque was more than 20.0 in-lb (2.3 N·m), replace the air cycle machine [39] with a new or serviceable unit.

H. Heat Exchanger and Plenum/Diffuser Assembly

SUBTASK 21-51-03-200-003-002 (1) Make sure that the identification (ID) plates are installed on the primary and secondary plenum. NOTE: The ID plates on the primary and secondary plenum assemblies contain the heat exchange unit information. The configuration of the equipment is shown by the part number, dash number, series number, and change number stamped on the identification plate. It is necessary to order and install ID plates, if the new plenum assemblies are supplied without ID plates. (a) If the new plenum assembly will be installed, make sure that all applicable data from the original identification plate are transferred. NOTE: New assembly means full assembly (Plenum, Diffuser, and Heat Exchanger). SUBTASK 21-51-03-420-019-002 (2) If it is necessary, do these steps to install the primary diffuser assembly [82] in the primary plenum (Figure 402). NOTE: The diffuser assembly with the fan bypass check valve is installed in the primary plenum/diffuser assembly. (a) If the bracket [92] is removed, do these steps: 1) Apply a smooth coat of Dow Corning Q4-2817 sealant, A50035, to the mating surfaces of the bracket [92] and primary plenum. 2) Lubricate the threads of the bolts [90] with anti-seize compound, C00852. 3) Loosely install the bolts [90] and washers [91] to hold the bracket [92] in its place. Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE FAN BYPASS CHECK VALVE IS INSTALLED AT THE BOTTOM OF THE DIFFUSER. THE AIR CONDITIONING PACK WILL OVERHEAT IF THE FAN BYPASS CHECK VALVE IS NOT INSTALLED AT THE BOTTOM OF THE DIFFUSER. (b) Put the primary diffuser assembly [82] in its position in the primary plenum with the smaller diameter end of the primary diffuser assembly [82] forward and with the fan bypass check valve at the bottom with respect to the installed position on the aircraft. 1) Make sure that the smaller diameter end is forward when you install the primary diffuser assembly [82]. (c) Lubricate the threads of the screws [81] and bolts [83] with anti-seize compound, C00852. (d) Align the forward diffuser brackets with the forward plenum brackets and loosely install the bolts [83] and washers [84]. 1) Find the run-on torque as the bolts [83] are installed in the nutplate self-locking feature as follows: NOTE: Run-on torque is the torque required to overcome the nutplate self-locking feature. a) Use a torque wrench to measure the torque required to turn the bolt [83] before the washer [84] contacts the bracket. (e) Loosely install the screws [81] through the holes in the plenum into the aft brackets on the primary diffuser assembly [82]. 1) Find the run-on torque as the screws [81] are installed in the nutplate self-locking feature. NOTE: Run-on torque is the torque required to overcome the nutplate self-locking feature. a) Use a torque wrench to measure the torque required to turn the screw [81] before the screw head contacts the plenum. (f) Position the primary diffuser assembly [82] to the dimension (View C, Figure 402). (g) Loosely install the bolts [90] through the holes in the plenum into the bracket [92]. 1) Find the run-on torque as the bolts [90] are installed in the nutplate self-locking feature. NOTE: Run-on torque is the torque required to overcome the nutplate self-locking feature. a) Use the torque wrench to measure the torque required to turn the bolt [90] before the washer [91] contacts the plenum. (h) Torque the bolts [83], bolts [90], and screws [81] to 22 in-lb (2.5 N·m) - 26 in-lb (2.9 N·m) plus the value of the run-on torque of the fastener. SUBTASK 21-51-03-420-029 (3) If it necessary, do these steps to install the secondary diffuser [85] in the secondary plenum: (a) Put the secondary diffuser [85] in the large end of the secondary plenum with the smaller diameter end of the secondary diffuser [85] forward with respect to the installed position on the aircraft. 1) Make sure that the smaller diameter end is forward when you install the secondary diffuser [85]. Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL (b) Lubricate the threads of the bolts [83] with anti-seize compound, C00852. (c) Align the secondary diffuser brackets with the secondary plenum brackets and loosely install the bolts [83] and washers [84]. 1) Find the run-on torque as the bolts [83] are installed in the nutplate self-locking feature. NOTE: Run-on torque is the torque required to overcome the nutplate self-locking feature. a) Use a torque wrench to measure the torque required to turn the bolt [83] before the washer [84] contacts the bracket. (d) Position the secondary diffuser [85] to the dimension (View E, Figure 402). (e) Torque the bolts [83] to 22 in-lb (2.5 N·m) - 26 in-lb (2.9 N·m) plus the value of the run-on torque of the bolt [83]. SUBTASK 21-51-03-420-020-002 (4) Do these steps to attach the secondary heat exchanger [58] to the secondary plenum/diffuser [23] or the primary heat exchanger [9] to the primary plenum/diffuser [8]: (a) Install a new gasket [69] on the primary heat exchanger [9] or secondary heat exchanger [58]. ALL POST HONEYWELL SB 2215240-21-2806 OR POST HONEYWELL SB 2215280-21-2808; AIRPLANES WITH METAL SHIM (b) For the primary heat exchanger [9], put the metal shim [75] in its position between the primary plenum/diffuser [8] and gasket [69]. ALL (c) Put the primary plenum/diffuser [8] on the primary heat exchanger [9] or the secondary plenum/diffuser [23] on the secondary heat exchanger [58]. (d) Install the clip assembly [65] using the bolts [63] and washers [64] as follows: 1) Lubricate the threads of the bolts [63] with anti-seize compound, C00852. 2) Torque the bolts [63] to 22 in-lb (2.5 N·m) - 26 in-lb (2.9 N·m) plus the value of the run-on torque of the bolt. NOTE: Run-on torque is the torque required to overcome the nutplate self-locking feature. (e) Install the clip assembly [66] with the bolts [63] and washers [64] as follows: 1) Lubricate the threads of the bolts [63] with anti-seize compound, C00852. 2) Align the clip assembly [66] with the primary heat exchanger [9] or the secondary heat exchanger [58]. a) Find the run-on torque as you install the bolts [63] in the nutplate self-locking feature. NOTE: Run-on torque is the torque required to overcome the nutplate self-locking feature. b) Use a torque wrench to measure the torque required to turn the bolt [63] before the washer [64] contacts the clip assembly [66]. 3) Torque the bolts [63] to 22 in-lb (2.5 N·m) - 26 in-lb (2.9 N·m) plus the value of the run-on torque of the bolt [63]. (f) Install the bolts [67] and washers [68] as follows: Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Lubricate the threads of the bolts [67] with anti-seize compound, C00852. 2) Align the primary plenum/diffuser [8] with the primary heat exchanger [9] or the secondary plenum/diffuser [23] with the secondary heat exchanger [58]. a) Find the run-on torque as you install the bolts [67] in the nutplate self-locking feature. NOTE: Run-on torque is the torque required to overcome the nutplate self-locking feature. b) Use a torque wrench to measure required to turn the bolt [67] before the washer [68] contacts the primary plenum. 3) Torque the bolts [67] to 22 in-lb (2.5 N·m) - 26 in-lb (2.9 N·m) plus the value of the run-on torque of the bolt [67]. SUBTASK 21-51-03-020-130-002 (5) Do these steps to join the primary plenum/diffuser [8] to the secondary plenum/diffuser [23]: (a) Put the flexible duct [62] in its position on the end of the secondary plenum/diffuser [23]. (b) Carefully move the heat exchangers together while you align the diffusers and plenum ducts to minimize misalignment. (c) Move the ends of the flexible duct [62] over the ends of the plenums. (d) Install the clamps [61] that attach the flexible duct [62] to the plenum/diffusers. 1) Tighten the clamps [61] until they can not be rotated around the hose under moderate hand pressure. 2) Tighten the clamp nuts an additional four turns. NOTE: There shall be a minimum of three threads protruding from the end of the clamp nut when installation is complete.

21-51-03-160-807Heat Exchanger and Plenum/Diffuser Assembly Cleaning Using Backflush EquipmentPDF p. 1033

2. Heat Exchanger and Plenum/Diffuser Assembly Cleaning Using Backflush Equipment (Figure 701) NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. General

(1) notes that this procedure for cleaning with backflush equipment is not effective for clearing blocked heat exchangers and less effective for dirty heat exchangers. To effectively clear blocked heat exchangers, do this task: Heat Exchanger - Blowing Out Debris/Blockages with Nitrogen Gas/Compressed Air, TASK 21-51-03-160-811. (2) You can use either a ground air source or airplane pneumatic air to do this procedure. If you use airplane pneumatic air, you must operate the APU.

I. Heat Exchanger and Plenum/Diffuser Assembly Cleaning Using Backflush Equipment

SUBTASK 21-51-03-020-002 CAUTION DO NOT USE SOAP OR A DETERGENT SOLUTION TO CLEAN THE HEAT EXCHANGERS. USE COLD WATER ONLY. SOAP OR A DETERGENT SOLUTION CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE AIR CYCLE MACHINE. (1) Use the backflusher, SPL-1607, to clean the heat exchanger. NOTE: You must do these steps for each of the heat exchangers. (a) Connect the air hose to the cleaning head. (b) Connect the water supply hose to the cleaning head. (c) If you use the airplane pneumatic system air for the air source, do this step: 1) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System with the APU, TASK 36-00-00-860-803. (d) If you use a ground pneumatic air for the air source, do this step: EFFECTIVITY ALL CAUTION DO NOT SUPPLY MORE THAN 30 PSIG OF GROUND AIR PRESSURE TO THE HEAT EXCHANGERS. TOO MUCH PRESSURE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE HEAT EXCHANGERS OR THE RAM AIR EXIT DUCTS. 1) Start the ground air source and adjust the pressure regulator to a maximum of 30 psig (207 kPa). WARNING MAKE SURE THAT YOU CORRECTLY ATTACH THE HOSE ASSEMBLY BEFORE YOU SUPPLY PRESSURE. WHEN YOU PUT PRESSURE ON THE HOSE, THE ASSEMBLY CAN MOVE QUICKLY. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, INJURIES TO PERSONNEL AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (e) If installed, slowly open the air supply valve on the manifold of the cleaning tool. (f) Slowly open the water supply valve on the 0 to 60 PSIG regulated cold water source, STD-3926. (g) If installed, slowly open the water supply valve on the manifold of the cleaning tool. (h) Clean the heat exchanger for 5 minutes. (i) Close the water supply valve on the 0 to 60 PSIG regulated cold water source, STD-3926, and continue to supply air for an additional 2 minutes. (j) If you use the airplane pneumatic system air, set the APU BLEED switch, on the P5-10 panel, to the OFF position. (k) If you use a ground pneumatic air for the air source, set the valve on the ground pneumatic cart to the OFF position. WARNING PUT ON GLOVES FOR PROTECTION FROM THE HOT WATER IN THE HOSES. HOT WATER CAN BURN YOU. (l) Disconnect the air hose from the cleaning head. WARNING PUT ON GLOVES FOR PROTECTION FROM THE HOT WATER IN THE HOSES. HOT WATER CAN BURN YOU. (m) Disconnect the water supply hose from the cleaning head. (n) Do the steps above, as necessary, for the other heat exchangers. 21-51-03-160-809Heat Exchanger - Cleaning with Soap-Water-AirPDF p. 1048

3. Heat Exchanger - Cleaning with Soap-Water-Air (Figure 702, Figure 703, Figure 704, Figure 705) NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. General

(1) notes that this procedure for cleaning with soap-water-air is not effective for clearing blocked heat exchangers and less effective for dirty heat exchangers. To effectively clear blocked heat exchangers, do this task: Heat Exchanger - Blowing Out Debris/Blockages with Nitrogen Gas/Compressed Air, TASK 21-51-03-160-811. (2) This procedure can improve heat exchanger performance between scheduled maintenance intervals when internal heat exchanger contamination is present (resulting in decreased performance) due to local environment conditions.

I. Heat Exchanger Cleaning with Soap-Water-Air

SUBTASK 21-51-03-100-007 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT YOU WEAR A FACE MASK, EYE PROTECTION, AND WATER RESISTANT CLOTHING DURING THE OPERATION. PREVENT SOAP AND HEAT EXCHANGER CONTAMINATION ON THE SKIN, EYES, AND HAIR. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY INSTRUCTIONS, INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. (1) To clean the heat exchangers, do the 3 steps that follow: • Step 1: Soak with soap, B50026, and water, G50256, to remove dust or small particles. • Step 2: Rinse off with high pressure clean water, G50256. • Step 3: Blow off water, G50256, for a minimum of 2 minutes to protect the Air Cycle Machine (ACM) from ingesting large water droplets. WARNING COMPRESSED GAS CAN BE DANGEROUS. EYE PROTECTION IS MANDATORY. APPLY DRY NITROGEN CAREFULLY IN DIRECTION AWAY FROM EYES AND FACE AND OTHER PERSONNEL TO AVOID POSSIBLE INJURY. (a) Soak with soap, B50026, and water, G50256, to remove dust/fine particle residue (Figure 703). 1) Connect the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, soap injector to the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water wand water inlet. a) Make sure that the lever on the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water wand is OFF (CLOSE). 2) Put the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, soap injector tube inlet into the soap container. 3) Connect one end of the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water hose to the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, soap injector. a) Make sure that the lever on the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, soap injector is OFF (CLOSE). 4) Connect the other end of the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water hose to the water cart. 5) If using clean dry air, G50321, (Optional – Not Required): a) Make sure that one end of the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, air hose is connected to either the 0-200psig dry filtered regulated air source, STD-6452, or nitrogen source, STD-1290, outlet. b) Connect the other end of the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, air hose to the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water wand air inlet. c) Adjust the regulator on the 0-200psig dry filtered regulated air source, STD-6452, or nitrogen source, STD-1290, to supply 50 psi (345 kPa) maximum to the cleaning wand, SPL-14922. EFFECTIVITY ALL 6) Insert the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, through the plenum/diffuser access openings and spray the soap, B50026, and water, G50256, through the cooling fins of the primary and secondary heat exchangers. a) Make sure that you do not damage the cooling fins of the heat exchangers when you put the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, through the plenum/diffuser access panel openings. NOTE: Since the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, uses an adjustable plastic tip to blow air through the heat exchangers, the tip will not damage the cooling fins upon making contact. b) Move the lever on the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water wand to ON (OPEN). c) Move the lever on the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, soap injector to ON (OPEN). NOTE: Switching the order will most likely cause the user to get wet. d) Spray the soap, B50026, and water, G50256, through the heat exchangers to soak and to remove dust and small particles. <1> Squeeze the handle on the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, air wand to blow the clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, with soap, B50026, and water, G50256, if clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, is needed. <2> Spray through all the areas of the heat exchangers. 7) Remove the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, from the plenum/diffuser access opening. 8) Decrease the 0-200psig dry filtered regulated air source, STD-6452, or nitrogen source, STD-1290, pressure to zero psi (if clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, is used, but not required). 9) Move the lever on the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, soap injector to OFF (CLOSE). 10) Move the lever on the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water wand to OFF (CLOSE). 11) Remove the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water hose from the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, soap injector. 12) Remove the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, soap injector. (b) Rinse with high pressure clean water, G50256 (Figure 704). 1) Make sure that the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, air hose is connected to the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water wand air inlet. 2) Connect the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water hose to the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water wand water inlet. 3) Adjust the regulator on the 0-200psig dry filtered regulated air source, STD-6452, or nitrogen source, STD-1290, to supply 50 psi (345 kPa) maximum to the cleaning wand, SPL-14922. NOTE: Vaporized clean dry air, G50321, is made with use of pressure over 100 psi. 4) Put the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, through the plenum/diffuser access opening. 5) Clean with strong pressure clean water, G50256, through the cooling fins of the primary and secondary heat exchangers. EFFECTIVITY ALL a) Make sure that you do not damage the cooling fins of the heat exchangers when you put the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, through the plenum/diffuser access panel openings. NOTE: Since the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, uses an adjustable plastic tip to blow air through the heat exchangers, the tip will not damage the cooling fins upon making contact. b) Put the lever on the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water wand to ON (OPEN) for water, G50256, to start flowing. c) Squeeze the handle on the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water wand for clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, to start flowing. d) Wash through the heat exchangers with the strong pressure clean water, G50256, to clean the soap, B50026. <1> Clean all the areas of the heat exchangers. 6) Remove the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, from the plenum/diffuser access opening. 7) Decrease the 0-200psig dry filtered regulated air source, STD-6452, or nitrogen source, STD-1290, pressure to zero psi. 8) Put the lever on the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water wand to OFF (CLOSE). 9) Remove the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water hose and cleaning wand, SPL-14922, water wand air inlet. (c) Blow off residual water, G50256, to protect the ACM (Figure 705). 1) Connect the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, air hose to the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, air inlet. 2) Adjust the regulator on 0-200psig dry filtered regulated air source, STD-6452, or nitrogen source, STD-1290, to supply 100 psi (689 kPa) maximum to the cleaning wand, SPL-14922. 3) Put the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, through the plenum/diffuser openings. 4) Blow clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, through the cooling fins of the primary and secondary heat exchangers to dry of remaining water, G50256. a) Make sure that you do not damage the cooling fins of the heat exchangers when you put the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, through the plenum/diffuser access panel. NOTE: Since the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, uses an adjustable plastic tip to blow air through the heat exchangers, the tip will not damage the cooling fins upon making contact. b) Blow the clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, through the heat exchangers until all remaining water, G50256, is blown out of the cooling fins. <1> Make sure that the pressure gage on the regulator does not show more than 100 psi (689 kPa) when you operate the cleaning wand, SPL-14922. <2> Blow the clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, through all the areas of the heat exchangers. <3> Make sure that water, G50256, is fully removed from the heat exchanger. <4> Blow clean dry air, G50321, or nitrogen, G00018, through the heat exchangers until water, G50256, is not being blown out. EFFECTIVITY ALL 5) Remove the cleaning wand, SPL-14922, from the plenum/diffuser access opening. 6) Decrease the 0-200psig dry filtered regulated air source, STD-6452, or nitrogen source, STD-1290, pressure to zero psi.

G. Air Cycle Machine Removal

SUBTASK 21-51-04-010-005-002 WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE COOLING PACK DUCTS WHEN THEY ARE HOT. HOT DUCTS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. (1) Remove the compressor outlet duct [11]. (a) Disconnect the flex hose from the duct. (b) Remove the electrical connector [1] from the control sensor for the ram air. (c) Remove the electrical connector [4] from the overheat switch for the compressor discharge. (d) Remove the clamshell clamp [6] at the air cycle machine [5]. 1) Lift the latch pawls at the same time to release the clamp [6]. (e) Move the sleeve [7] to the compressor outlet duct [11]. (f) Remove the coupling [2] at the heat exchanger. (g) Remove the compressor outlet duct [11]. (h) Remove and discard the packing [3] at the heat exchanger. (i) Remove and discard the packings [8]. SUBTASK 21-51-04-860-014-002 (2) Remove the High Pressure Water Separator (HPWS) mix muff (TASK 21-51-17-000-801). SUBTASK 21-51-04-210-003 (3) Do a check of the flexible duct [36] that is connected to the high pressure water separator condenser for all of the conditions listed below: (a) fraying (b) discoloration (c) rips (d) splits (e) tears Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL (f) rupture defects. (g) If you find one or more of the above conditions, remove the flexible duct [36] from the condenser as follows: 1) Loosen the clamp [37] that attaches the flexible duct [36] to the water separator condenser. 2) Remove and discard the flexible duct [36] from the water separator condenser. SUBTASK 21-51-04-020-002-002 (4) Disconnect the hoses and sense line from the air cycle machine [5]. (a) Remove the flex hose 1 [19] from the air cycle machine [5]. (b) Disconnect the flex hose 2 [23] from the air cycle machine [5]. (c) Disconnect the sense line [12] from the air cycle machine [5]. (d) If you will replace the air cycle machine [5], remove the unions [13] and O-rings [14]. 1) Discard the O-rings [14]. SUBTASK 21-51-04-020-003-002 (5) Remove the air cycle machine [5]. (a) Remove the clamshell clamp [16]. 1) Lift the latch pawls at the same time to release each clamp [16]. (b) Move the sleeve [17] away from the air cycle machine [5] and onto the adjacent duct. (c) Remove and discard the O-rings [18]. (d) Disconnect the compressor inlet duct [9]. 1) Remove the bolt [31] that holds the ground clip [32] to the air cycle machine [5]. 2) Move the bonding jumper [33] away from the air cycle machine [5]. a) Do not remove the ground clip [32] from the bonding jumper [33]. 3) Remove the bolts [29] that hold the compressor inlet duct [9] to the air cycle machine [5]. 4) Remove and discard the O-ring [30]. (e) Remove the bolts [21] and washers [22] that hold the air cycle machine [5] to the secondary heat exchanger. WARNING HAVE A SECOND PERSON HOLD THE ACM WHEN YOU REMOVE THE BOLT OR NUT. THE ACM CAN FALL WHEN THE BOLT OR NUT IS LOOSE. IF THE ACM FALLS, INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (f) Remove the nut [28] and washer [27] from the bolt [24] that holds the air cycle machine [5] to the tie rod. WARNING HAVE A SECOND PERSON HOLD THE ACM WHEN YOU REMOVE THE BOLT OR NUT. THE ACM CAN FALL WHEN THE BOLT OR NUT IS LOOSE. IF THE ACM FALLS, INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (g) Remove the bolt [24] and washer [25] from the tie rod. (h) Carefully move forward then lower the air cycle machine [5] to remove it from the air conditioning bay. Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL (i) Remove the bushing [26] from the tie rod. (j) Remove the gasket [20]. 1) Discard the gasket [20]. SUBTASK 21-51-04-620-002-002 (6) Put covers on the duct openings to prevent the entry of unwanted materials. NOTE: You can use a sheet made of plastic - polyethylene or vinyl (commercially available) sealed with masking tape as a cover for the duct openings. SUBTASK 21-51-04-700-002 (7) Do a check of the torque necessary to turn the rotating assembly of the air cycle machine [5]. (a) Put the air cycle machine [5] in a horizontal position. (b) Put a torque wrench on the nut [35]. NOTE: You must use a torque wrench with a gage that shows the torque applied. CAUTION TURN THE ROTATING COMPONENTS OF THE ACM ONLY IN THE DIRECTION THAT THEY TURN WHEN IN OPERATION. IF YOU TURN THE ACM ROTATING COMPONENTS IN THE INCORRECT DIRECTION, YOU CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE FOIL AIR BEARINGS. (c) Make sure that you turn the nut [35] counterclockwise while you turn the rotating assembly. (d) Record the torque necessary to turn the rotating assembly. (e) If the torque was more than 20 in-lb (2.3 N·m), replace the air cycle machine [5] with a new or serviceable unit.

SUBTASK 21-51-04-200-001-002 (1) If the cause of the air cycle machine [5] failure is unknown, do all of the steps that follow. SUBTASK 21-51-04-200-002-002 (2) If the cause of the air cycle machine [5] failure is known, do applicable steps that follow. SUBTASK 21-51-04-630-010-002 (3) If you replaced the air cycle machine [5] because of bearing failure or damage to the compressor, do these steps: (a) Disconnect the water drain lines from the bottom of the water extractors (TASK 21-51-14-000-801). 1) Use compressed air to remove unwanted material from the water drain lines. 2) Connect the water drain lines to the bottom of the water extractors (TASK 21-51-14-400-801). (b) Disconnect the water line and the air line which are attached to the water spray nozzle (TASK 21-51-16-000-801). 1) Use compressed air to remove unwanted material from the water and air lines. 2) Connect the water line and the air line which are attached to the water spray nozzle (TASK 21-51-16-400-801). (c) Remove the flex hose 1 [19] and flex hose 2 [23]. 1) Use compressed air to remove unwanted material from the flex hoses. 2) Reconnect the flex hose 2 [23]. NOTE: You must install the flex hose 1 after you install the ACM. SUBTASK 21-51-04-630-011-002 (4) If you replaced the air cycle machine [5] because of damage to the compressor, do these steps: (a) Examine the components that follow for damage or unwanted materials: Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Heat Exchangers (TASK 21-51-03-000-805-002) 2) Water Extractor Duct (TASK 21-51-15-000-801) 3) Water Extractors (TASK 21-51-14-000-801) 4) Reheater (TASK 21-51-13-000-801) 5) Condenser (TASK 21-51-12-000-801) 6) Water Spray Nozzle (TASK 21-51-16-000-801). (b) Replace the components that have damage or unwanted materials. SUBTASK 21-51-04-630-012-002 (5) If you replaced the air cycle machine [5] because of damage to the impeller blades [34], do these steps: (a) Remove the plenum/diffuser access panels. 1) Remove the bolts and washers that attach the plenum/diffuser access panels to the plenum diffuser assemblies for the primary and secondary heat exchangers. 2) Remove the bolt, washers, and nut that attach the bonding jumper to the forward access panel. 3) Remove the plenum/diffuser access panels and the gaskets. (b) Examine the plenum for unwanted materials. (c) Install the plenum/diffuser access panels. 1) Install the plenum/diffuser access panels and gaskets with the bolts and washers. 2) Put the bonding jumper in its position and install the bolts, washers, and nut.

I. Air Cycle Machine Installation

SUBTASK 21-51-04-860-031-002 (1) For the left air cycle machine [5], do this step: (a) Make sure that these circuit breakers are open and have safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-348 A 4 C00399 AIR CONDITIONING RAM AIR MOD LEFT 349-999 A 4 C01950 AIR CONDITIONING RAM AIR MOD LEFT ALL A 8 C00555 AIR CONDITIONING RAM AIR MOD CONT L A 9 C01158 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONTROL LEFT DC A 11 C01159 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONTROL LEFT AC C 6 C00262 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONT VALVES L C 8 C01176 A/C PACK/ENGINE BLEED AIR OVHT LEFT SUBTASK 21-51-04-860-027-002 (2) For the right air cycle machine [5], do this step: Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Make sure that these circuit breakers are open and have safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-348 B 4 C00400 AIR CONDITIONING RAM AIR MOD RIGHT 349-999 B 4 C01951 AIR CONDITIONING RAM AIR MOD RIGHT ALL B 8 C01178 AIR CONDITIONING RAM AIR MOD CONT R B 9 C01161 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONT RIGHT DC B 11 C01162 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONT RIGHT AC C 5 C00263 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONT VALVES R C 7 C01177 A/C PACK/ENGINE BLEED AIR OVHT RIGHT SUBTASK 21-51-04-630-002-002 (3) Remove the duct covers. SUBTASK 21-51-04-210-002-002 (4) Make sure that there are no unwanted materials in the ducts. SUBTASK 21-51-04-420-002-002 (5) Install the air cycle machine [5]. (a) Install a new gasket [20]. NOTE: You must align the holes in the gasket with the bolt holes in the ACM and secondary heat exchanger. (b) Install the O-ring [30] for the compressor inlet duct [9]. 1) If a lubricant is necessary to put the O-ring [30] into its installed position, use distilled water, G01061, on the surface of the O-ring [30]. 2) If the use of distilled water, G01061, is not adequate to install the O-ring [30] or if a lubricant is needed to hold the O-ring [30] in place for the installation, apply a light coat of grease, D00504, or Molykote 44 grease, medium, D50104, to the O-ring [30]. (c) Install the bushing [26] in the tie rod. (d) Put the air cycle machine [5] into its position. (e) Put the washer [25] on the shank of the bolt [24]. NOTE: The countersunk side of the washer must be adjacent to the head of the bolt. WARNING HAVE A SECOND PERSON HOLD THE ACM WHEN YOU INSTALL THE BOLT. THE ACM CAN FALL WHEN THE BOLT IS LOOSE. IF THE ACM FALLS, INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (f) Push the bolt [24] and washer [25] through the tie rod and bushing [26]. Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL WARNING HAVE A SECOND PERSON HOLD THE ACM WHEN YOU INSTALL THE NUT. THE ACM CAN FALL WHEN THE NUT IS LOOSE. IF THE ACM FALLS, INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (g) Install the washer [27] and nut [28] on the bolt [24]. 1) Do not tighten the nut [28] fully. (h) Apply a light layer of compound, C00852, to the threads of the bolts [21]. (i) Install the bolts [21] and washers [22] that hold the air cycle machine [5] to the secondary heat exchanger. 1) Do not tighten the bolts [21] fully. (j) Connect the compressor inlet duct [9] to the air cycle machine [5]. 1) Apply a light layer of compound, C00852, to the threads of the bolts [29] and the bolt [31]. 2) Put the ground clip [32] onto the bolt [31]. a) Do not remove the ground clip [32] from the bonding jumper [33]. 3) Install the ground clip [32] and bolt [31] on the inlet flange of the air cycle machine [5] compressor. a) Do not tighten the bolt [31] fully. 4) Install the bolts [29] on the compressor inlet flange of the air cycle machine [5]. a) Do not tighten the bolts [29] fully. (k) Apply a light layer of grease, D00504, on the O-rings [18]. (l) Install the O-rings [18] for the turbine inlet duct. (m) Move the sleeve [17] on the air cycle machine [5] and duct connections. (n) Install the clamp [16] on the duct connections. (o) Do these steps to tighten the bolts [21]: 1) Find the run-on torque as you install the bolts [21] in the nutplate self-locking feature. NOTE: Run-on torque is the torque required to overcome the nutplate self-locking feature. 2) Use a torque wrench to measure the torque required to turn the bolt [21] before the washer [22] contacts the air cycle machine [5]. 3) Tighten the bolts [21] to 40 in-lb (4.5 N·m) - 45 in-lb (5.1 N·m) plus the value of the run-on torque. (p) Tighten the bolts [29] and bolt [31] to 22 in-lb (2.5 N·m) - 26 in-lb (2.9 N·m). (q) Tighten the nut [28] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 65 in-lb (7.3 N·m). SUBTASK 21-51-04-420-003-002 (6) Connect the sense line [12] and hoses to the air cycle machine [5]. (a) If you install the new air cycle machine [5], do these steps: 1) Put new O-rings [14] on each of the unions [13]. 2) Apply a light layer of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the unions [13]. Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL 3) Install the union [13] onto the air cycle machine [5], at three locations. 4) Tighten the union [13] to 170 ±9 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m). (b) Apply a light layer of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the sense line [12]. (c) Connect the sense line [12] to the air cycle machine [5]. 1) Tighten the sense line [12] to 170 ±9 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m). (d) Apply a light layer of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the flex hose 1 [19]. (e) Install the flex hose 1 [19] on the air cycle machine [5]. 1) Tighten the flex hose 1 [19] to 170 ±9 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m). (f) Apply a light layer of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the flex hose 2 [23]. (g) Connect the flex hose 2 [23] to the air cycle machine [5]. 1) Tighten the flex hose 2 [23] to 170 ±9 in-lb (19.2 ±1.0 N·m). SUBTASK 21-51-04-420-004 (7) If you discarded the flexible duct [36] after the inspection, install a new flexible duct [36] as follows: (a) Loosely put the clamps [37] onto the new flexible duct [36]. (b) Install the new flexible duct [36] onto the water separator condenser. (c) Put the forward clamp [37] to keep the flexible duct onto the water separator condenser. (d) Tighten the forward clamp [37] to 13 in-lb (1.5 N·m) - 17 in-lb (1.9 N·m). NOTE: The aft clamp is connected in the installation of the High Pressure Water Separator (HPWS) mix muff in the next step. SUBTASK 21-51-04-860-015-002 (8) Do this task: High Pressure Water Separator Mix Muff Installation, TASK 21-51-17-400-801. SUBTASK 21-51-04-410-003-002 (9) Install the compressor outlet duct [11]. (a) Apply a light coat of distilled water, G01061, or grease, D00504, or Molykote 44 grease, medium, D50104, to the packing [3] and packings [8]. (b) Install the packings [8] on the duct ends. (c) Install the packing [3] at the heat exchanger. (d) Put the compressor outlet duct [11] into its position. (e) Apply compound, D50320, to the bolt threads of the coupling [2]. (f) Install the coupling [2] at the heat exchanger. 1) Do not tighten the coupling [2] fully. (g) Move the sleeve [7] on the connection for the compressor outlet duct [11]. (h) Install the clamp [6] on the connection of the compressor outlet duct [11]. (i) Tighten the nut on the coupling [2] to 45 in-lb (5.1 N·m) - 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m). (j) With hand force, carefully push the compressor outlet duct [11] in the direction of the adjacent mix muff duct until the compressor outlet duct [11] is at the position of maximum flex. Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL (k) Make sure that there is a minimum clearance of 0.20 in. (5.1 mm) to the adjacent mix muff duct when the compressor outlet duct [11] is at the position of maximum flex. (l) Apply a light layer of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the flex hose. (m) Connect the flex hose to the compressor outlet duct [11]. (n) Install the electrical connector [1] for the control sensor for the ram air. (o) Install the electrical connector [4] for the overheat switch for the compressor discharge.

F. Conditioned Air Check Valve Removal

SUBTASK 21-51-07-020-002-002 (1) To disconnect the sense line from the valve, do these steps: (a) Loosen the b-nut to disconnect the sense line. (b) Remove the union [5]. (c) Remove and discard the o-ring [6]. SUBTASK 21-51-07-020-003-002 (2) Remove the conditioned air check valve [1] as follows: (a) Make a record of the position of the check valve to make sure it is installed in the same position. (b) Remove the clamp assembly [2] from the conditioned air check valve [1] as follows: 1) Remove the washers [11] and nuts [12]. 2) Remove the brackets [13]. 3) Loosen the nuts [4] on the clamps of the clamp assembly [2] so that the clamps are free to slide. 4) Slide the flexible duct [3] aft until it is free of the conditioned air check valve [1]. (c) Remove the bolts [10], washers [8], and nuts [9], that hold the check valve to the bulkhead penetration duct assembly [15]. (d) Remove the conditioned air check valve [1]. (e) Leave the flexible duct [3] on the condenser outlet duct [16]. SUBTASK 21-51-07-620-002-002 (3) Put covers on the duct openings to prevent the entry of unwanted materials.

F. Conditioned Air Check Valve Installation

SUBTASK 21-51-07-630-002-002 (1) Remove the duct covers. SUBTASK 21-51-07-420-002-002 (2) Install the conditioned air check valve [1] as follows: (a) Examine the gasket [7] on the flange of the bulkhead penetration duct assembly [15]. (b) Replace the gasket [7] if it is damaged or worn. (c) Put the conditioned air check valve [1] in its position. 1) Make sure the check valve is installed in the same orientation as when it was removed. (d) Install the bolts [10], washers [8], and nuts [9] that attach the check valve [1] to the bulkhead penetration duct assembly [15]. (e) Slide the forward end of the flexible duct [3] forward onto the aft end of the conditioned air check valve [1]. (f) Position the individual clamps [14] so that these conditions are met: 1) Make sure the clamps are not installed on the duct bead. 2) Keep a 0.125 in. (3.175 mm) minimum distance between the clamps and the edge of the flexible duct [3]. 3) Make sure that the two forward clamps [14] are located forward of the bead on the aft end of the check valve [1]. Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL 4) Make sure the aft clamp [14] is located aft of the bead on the forward end of the condenser outlet duct [16]. 5) Make sure that the forward clamp [14] is located inside (aft) of the bead on the flexible duct [3]. 6) Make sure that the aft clamp [14] is located inside (forward) of the bead on the flexible duct [3]. 7) Install the brackets [13] that connect the clamps [14] together. a) If necessary, reposition the clamps [14] axially so that the brackets [13] can be installed. b) Make sure that the clamps [14] are positioned so that the position requirements are still met. c) Install the washers [11] and nuts [12] that retain the brackets [13] to the clamps [14]. d) Tighten the nuts [12] to 63 in-lb (7.1 N·m) - 67 in-lb (7.6 N·m). (g) Install the nuts [4] on the clamps [14]. (h) Determine the run-on torque value of the nuts on the T-bolts for each nut and T-bolt combination as follows: 1) Rotate the nut [4] onto the T-bolt until it is approximately one turn from seating and at least 3 T-bolt threads are protruding from the top of the nut [4]. 2) Measure the torque value required to turn the nut [4] the last revolution before it seats. 3) Make a record of this torque value. NOTE: The torque value must be between 2 in-lb (0.2 N·m) - 18 in-lb (2.0 N·m). (i) Tighten the nuts [4] to 12 in-lb (1.4 N·m) - 14 in-lb (1.6 N·m) plus the run-on torque value determined for each nut [4]. SUBTASK 21-51-07-020-004-002 (3) Do these steps to install the sense line: (a) Install a new o-ring [6] on the union [5]. (b) Apply a layer of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the union [5]. (c) Install the union [5] in the check valve [1]. (d) Connect the sense line to the union [5].

G. Conditioned Air Check Valve Installation Test

SUBTASK 21-51-07-860-013-002 (1) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System (Selection), TASK 36-00-00-860-801. SUBTASK 21-51-07-860-014-002 (2) Remove the DO-NOT-OPERATE TAGs from these switches on the P5-10 air conditioning panel: (a) L PACK and R PACK (b) BLEED 1 and BLEED 2 (c) BLEED APU. SUBTASK 21-51-07-860-015-002 (3) Put the applicable L PACK or R PACK switch on the P5-10 air conditioning panel to the AUTO position. Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-51-07-790-003-002 (4) Check for concentrated air leakage at the ends of the conditioned air check valve. NOTE: A concentrated leak is defined as a leak where air flow can be felt or heard 12 inches away from source.

H. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 21-51-07-010-005-002 (1) When the left conditioned air check valve was replaced close this access panel: Number Name/Location 192CL ECS Access Door SUBTASK 21-51-07-010-006-002 (2) When the right conditioned air check valve was replaced, do these steps (TASK 06-41-00-800-801): (a) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 192CR ECS Access Door (b) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 192DR ECS High Pressure Access Door NOTE: The ECS high pressure access door, 192DR, will not latch in its position if the ECS access door, 192CR, is not closed. SUBTASK 21-51-07-860-016-002 (3) Put these switches on the P5-10 air conditioning panel to the OFF position: (a) L PACK (b) R PACK SUBTASK 21-51-07-860-017-002 (4) Do this task: Remove Pressure from the Pneumatic System, TASK 36-00-00-860-806.

(a) Discard the packing [33] and packing [42] SUBTASK 21-51-08-010-007 (11) To remove the coupling assembly from the condenser, do these steps: (a) Remove the coupling [7]. (b) Move the sleeve [8] and ring [9] onto the duct. (c) Remove the retainer [10]. SUBTASK 21-51-08-010-008 (12) Remove the clamps [11] from the flexible duct [12]. SUBTASK 21-51-08-010-009 (13) Remove the flexible duct [12]. SUBTASK 21-51-08-020-001 (19) For the left high pressure water separator [1], disconnect these electrical connectors: (a) Disconnect the electrical connector D3866 from the pack temperature sensor. (b) Disconnect the electrical connector D3930 from the pack temperature bulb. SUBTASK 21-51-08-020-002 (20) For the right high pressure water separator [1], disconnect these electrical connectors: (a) Disconnect the electrical connector D3876 from the pack temperature sensor. (b) Disconnect the electrical connector D3982 from the pack temperature bulb. SUBTASK 21-51-08-020-003 (21) Do these steps to disconnect the two ducts from the reheater: (a) Remove the bolts [13], washers [14], washers [15], and nuts [16]. (b) Remove and discard the O-rings [17] from each of the two ducts. SUBTASK 21-51-08-020-004 WARNING BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU MOVE THE COMPONENT. THE COMPONENT IS HEAVY. INJURIES TO PERSONS CAN OCCUR. (22) To remove the high pressure water separator [1] from the airplane, do these steps: (a) For the forward attach points do the steps that follow: 1) Remove the nut [21], washer [20], countersunk washer [19], and bolt [18]. 2) Remove the bushing [22] from the bracket. (b) For the aft attach points do the steps that follow: 1) Remove the nut [21], washer [20], countersunk washer [19], and bolt [23]. 2) Remove the bushings [24] from the bracket. (c) Carefully lower the high pressure water separator [1] from the Environmental Control System (ECS) bay. SUBTASK 21-51-08-480-002 (1) Remove the duct and line covers. SUBTASK 21-51-08-420-001 WARNING BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU MOVE THE COMPONENT. THE COMPONENT IS HEAVY. INJURIES TO PERSONS CAN OCCUR. (2) To install the high pressure water separator [1] assembly on the airplane, do these steps: (a) Carefully position the high pressure water separator [1] in the Environmental Control System (ECS) bay. (b) For the forward attach points do the steps that follow: 1) Install the bushing [22] in the bracket. 2) Install the nut [21], washer [20], countersunk washer [19], and bolt [18]. a) Position the countersunk side of the countersunk washer [19] under the head of the bolt [18]. (c) For the aft attach points do the steps that follow: 1) Install the bushings [24] in the bracket. 2) Install the nut [21], washer [20], countersunk washer [19], and bolt [23]. EFFECTIVITY ALL a) Position the countersunk side of the countersunk washer [19] under the bolt head. (d) For the right high pressure water separator [1] installation, make sure that there is a minimum of 0.10 in. (2.54 mm) clearance between the supply duct to the trim air Pressure Regulating and Shutoff Valve (PRSOV) and the water collection manifold. 1) If there is not a minimum of 0.10 in. (2.54 mm) clearance, do one of these steps to provide the minimum clearance: a) Reposition the supply duct to the trim air PRSOV. b) Remove material from the water collection manifold. SUBTASK 21-51-08-420-002 (3) Do these steps to connect the ducts to the reheater: (a) Apply a thin coat of one of these lubricants to the new O-rings [17]: 1) Braycote Micronic 601EF grease, D50380 2) Braycote 601EF Grease, D50203 3) Braycote 815Z lubricant, D50268 4) Fluorolube GR-660 lubricant, D00548 5) Krytox 240AB grease, D50234 6) Krytox 240AZ grease, D50233 7) Krytox 240AC perfluoropolyether grease, D50063. (b) Install the O-ring [17] on each of the duct. (c) Install the bolts [13], washers [14], washers [15], and nuts [16]. SUBTASK 21-51-08-420-003 (4) Install the flexible duct [12] on the mix muff and the condenser. SUBTASK 21-51-08-420-004 (5) Install the clamps [11] on the flexible duct [12]. (a) Apply Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the T-bolt thread of the clamps [11]. (b) Tighten the clamps [11] to 13 in-lb (1.5 N·m) - 17 in-lb (1.9 N·m). (c) Apply an approximately 0.125 in. (3.175 mm) wide torque stripe, G50411, or tamper-proof putty/lacquer, G51905, to the clamps [11]. SUBTASK 21-51-08-400-001 (6) If it is necessary, do these steps to install the union [43]: (a) Lubricate the new packing [44] with lubricant, D00602, or equivalent. I. High Pressure Water Separator Installation Test

SUBTASK 21-51-08-860-004 (1) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System (Selection), TASK 36-00-00-860-801 SUBTASK 21-51-08-860-011 (2) For the left high pressure water separator [1], remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name A 9 C01158 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONTROL LEFT DC A 11 C01159 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONTROL LEFT AC EFFECTIVITY ALL (Continued) F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name D 8 C00076 AIR CONDITIONING TEMP IND SUBTASK 21-51-08-860-012 (3) For the right high pressure water separator [1], remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name B 9 C01161 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONT RIGHT DC B 11 C01162 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONT RIGHT AC D 8 C00076 AIR CONDITIONING TEMP IND SUBTASK 21-51-08-860-005 (4) Do these steps on the P5-10 air conditioning panel (located on the P5 forward overhead panel): (a) Remove the DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858, and set the applicable L or R PACK switch to the AUTO position. (b) Remove the DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858, and set the BLEED 1 and 2 switches to the ON position. (c) Remove the DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858, and set the BLEED APU switch to the ON position. SUBTASK 21-51-08-790-001 (5) Do a soap bubble test of all the applicable duct joints. NOTE: No leakage is permitted. (a) If there is leakage, do these steps: 1) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches in the OFF position. WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE COOLING PACK DUCTS WHEN THEY ARE HOT. HOT DUCTS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONNEL. 2) Loosen the clamps. 3) Make sure that the ducts are aligned at the joints. 4) Tighten the clamps. 5) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches in the AUTO position. 6) Make sure that the leak has been repaired.

SUBTASK 21-51-11-020-011 (9) Remove and discard the packings [18] at the remaining three sense line locations.

SUBTASK 21-51-11-420-001 (1) Install the reducer [19] on the standby temperature control valve [1], do these steps: (a) Install a new packing [20] on the reducer [19]. (b) Apply a thin layer of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the reducer [19]. (c) Install the reducer [19] on the standby temperature control valve [1]. SUBTASK 21-51-11-420-005 (2) Install the union [17] on the standby temperature control valve [1], do these steps: (a) Install a new packing [18] on the union [17]. (b) Apply a thin layer of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the union [17]. (c) Install the union [17] on the standby temperature control valve [1]. SUBTASK 21-51-11-160-002 (3) Carefully put the standby temperature control valve [1] into its position between the air ducts. SUBTASK 21-51-11-020-007 (4) Install the clamps [8] that hold the valve to the ducts. (a) Do not fully tighten the clamps. (b) Install the condenser inlet pressure sense line [10]. (c) Install the ACM turbine muffler sense line [4]. (d) Install the condenser outlet pressure sense line [9]. (e) Install the conditioned air check valve sense line [11]. (f) Align the three sense line clamps and wire bundle clamp with the spacer plate nut on the structure. 21-51-11-710-801Standby Temperature Control Valve Primary Pneumatic Control - Operation CheckPDF p. 1137

2. Standby Temperature Control Valve Primary Pneumatic Control - Operation Check

A. General

(1) The primary function of the Standby Temperature Control Valve (STCV) is to monitor the differential pressure between the inlet and outlet of the High Pressure Water Separator (HPWS)'s Condenser and the Air Cycle Machine (ACM)'s Turbine Outlet and Condition Air Check Valve. This task will make sure that the primary pneumatic control of the STCV is working properly.

B. References

Reference Title 21-51-11-000-801 Standby Temperature Control Valve Removal (P/B 401) 21-51-11-400-801 Standby Temperature Control Valve Installation (P/B 401)

C. Tools/Equipment

NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional. Reference Description SPL-21786 Standby Temperature Control Valve (STCV) Test Equipment Part #: C21013-1 Supplier: 81205 STD-1290 Source - Nitrogen, 0-200 PSIG

D. Location Zones

Zone Area 192 Lower Wing-To-Body Fairing - Under Wing Box 212 Flight Compartment - Right

E. Prepare for the Check

SUBTASK 21-51-11-020-019 (1) Remove the STCV. Do this task: Standby Temperature Control Valve Removal, TASK 21-51-11-000-801. NOTE: It is acceptable to remove the duct in place of the valve. SUBTASK 21-51-11-200-001 (2) Make sure that the ball valve [8] and needle valve [7] on the STCV test equipment, SPL-21786, are in the “CLOSED” position. SUBTASK 21-51-11-820-006 (3) Adjust the nitrogen source, STD-1290, to 150±40 psi. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-51-11-820-001 (4) Connect the nitrogen source, STD-1290, to the jic fitting [6] on the STCV test equipment, SPL-21786. (a) If necessary, adjust the jic fitting [6] so that the relief valve no longer activates. SUBTASK 21-51-11-420-006 (5) Connect the trailing probe hose assembly [10] tube end of the STCV test equipment, SPL-21786, to the trailing probe control valve [5] on the STCV.

F. Test the Low Delta Pressure Servo of the Standby Temperature Control Valve (STCV) - Min

Open SUBTASK 21-51-11-420-007 (1) Connect the turbine muff fitting assembly [11] of the STCV test equipment, SPL-21786, to the turbine muff connection [2] on the STCV as follows: (a) Make sure that the turbine muff fitting assembly [11] is installed on the hose connection of the ss pipe fitting [12]. (b) Install the turbine muff fitting assembly [11] onto the turbine muff connection [2]. (2) Connect the ss pipe fitting [13] of the STCV test equipment, SPL-21786, to the conditioned air check valve connection [1] on the STCV as follows: (a) Install the ss pipe fitting [13] onto the conditioned air check valve connection [1]. SUBTASK 21-51-11-020-016 (3) Open the ball valve [8] to allow the nitrogen into the system. SUBTASK 21-51-11-820-003 (4) Make sure that the pressure gauge reading shows 45±5 psi. (a) If necessary, adjust the pressure regulator [9] until the pressure gauge reading shows 45±5 psi. SUBTASK 21-51-11-820-007 (5) Adjust the needle valve [7] until the digital manometer reads 24±1 in/H2O. (a) Make sure that the butterfly plate begins to open. 1) If the plate doesn't operate correctly, then replace the STCV. This is the task: Standby Temperature Control Valve Removal, TASK 21-51-11-000-801. SUBTASK 21-51-11-410-001 (6) Close the ball valve [8] to stop the nitrogen supply.

G. Test the Low Delta Pressure Servo of the Standby Temperature Control Valve (STCV) - Full

Open SUBTASK 21-51-11-420-008 (1) If not already installed, connect the turbine muff fitting assembly [11] of the STCV test equipment, SPL-21786, to the turbine muff connection [2] on the STCV as follows: (a) Make sure that the turbine muff fitting assembly [11] is installed on the hose connection of the ss pipe fitting [12]. (b) Install the turbine muff fitting assembly [11] onto the turbine muff connection [2]. (2) If not already installed, connect the ss pipe fitting [13] of the STCV test equipment, SPL-21786, to the conditioned air check valve connection [1] on the STCV as follows: (a) Install the ss pipe fitting [13] onto the conditioned air check valve connection [1]. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-51-11-020-017 (3) Open the ball valve [8] to allow the nitrogen into the system. SUBTASK 21-51-11-820-004 (4) Make sure that the pressure gauge reading shows 45±5 psi. (a) If necessary, adjust the pressure regulator [9] until the pressure gauge reading shows 45±5 psi. SUBTASK 21-51-11-820-008 (5) Adjust the needle valve [7] until the digital manometer reads 86±3 in/H2O. (a) Make sure that the butterfly plate fully opens. 1) If the plate doesn't operate correctly, then replace the STCV. This is the task: Standby Temperature Control Valve Removal, TASK 21-51-11-000-801. SUBTASK 21-51-11-410-002 (6) Close the ball valve [8] to stop the nitrogen supply.

H. Test the High Delta Pressure Servo of the Standby Temperature Control Valve (STCV) - Min

Open SUBTASK 21-51-11-420-009 (1) Connect the ss pipe fitting [12] of the STCV test equipment, SPL-21786, to the heat exchanger inlet connection [4] on the STCV as follows: (a) If the turbine muff fitting assembly [11] is installed, remove it from the end of the hose connection so that the ss pipe fitting [12] is accessible. (b) Install the ss pipe fitting [12] onto the heat exchanger inlet connection [4]. (2) Connect the ss pipe fitting [13] of the STCV test equipment, SPL-21786, to the heat exchanger outlet connection [3] as follows: (a) Install the ss pipe fitting [13] onto the heat exchanger outlet connection [3]. SUBTASK 21-51-11-020-018 (3) Open the ball valve [8] to allow the nitrogen into the system. SUBTASK 21-51-11-820-009 (4) Make sure that the pressure gauge reading shows 45±5 psi. (a) If necessary, adjust the pressure regulator [9] until the pressure gauge reading shows 45±5 psi. SUBTASK 21-51-11-820-005 (5) Adjust the needle valve [7] until the digital manometer reads 92±8 in/H2O. (a) Make sure the butterfly plate begins to open. 1) If the plate doesn't operate correctly, then replace the STCV. This is the task: Standby Temperature Control Valve Removal, TASK 21-51-11-000-801. SUBTASK 21-51-11-410-003 (6) Close the ball valve [8] to stop the nitrogen supply.

I. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 21-51-11-020-014 (1) Disconnect the nitrogen source, STD-1290, from the jic fitting [6]. SUBTASK 21-51-11-020-015 (2) Disconnect the STCV test equipment, SPL-21786, from the STCV. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-51-11-420-010 (3) Install the STCV. Do this task: Standby Temperature Control Valve Installation, TASK 21-51-11-400-801.

(b) While the condenser [55] is put in the frame assembly, do these steps: 1) Move the hoses on the water extractors over the ducts on the condenser [55]. (e) Install the clamps [42] on the water extractor hoses. SUBTASK 21-51-12-020-024 (5) Install the water extractor drain lines and manifold, do these steps: (a) Move the six hoses over the drain line ports of the water extractors. (b) Install the screws [51], washers [50], and shim [49] that hold the manifold to the condenser [55]. 1) If a replacement manifold is installed, make sure to remove the plastic plug from the overflow port of the water collection manifold. (c) Install the clamps [41] that connect the drain line hoses to the water extractors. (d) Put the drain line support clamps [48] on the condenser ducts. (e) Align the drain line support clamps [48] with the clamp on the water extractor drain line. (f) Install the screws [45], washers [46], and nuts [47] that connect the drain line support clamps [48]. F. Reheater Installation Test

SUBTASK 21-51-13-860-003 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT PERSONNEL ARE CLEAR OF THE RAM AIR INLET AND EXIT DOORS, LINKAGES AND ACTUATORS BEFORE YOU DO THIS TEST. POSSIBLE INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR. (1) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-811. SUBTASK 21-51-13-780-001 (2) To prepare for a leak check of the reheater [49] installation, do one of these steps, (a) or (b): (a) Supply pneumatic pressure to the packs with the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) as follows: 1) Supply pressure to the pneumatic system with the APU (TASK 36-00-00-860-803). 2) Make sure that the aft outflow valve and a passenger door are open. 3) Set the applicable L PACK or R PACK switch, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, to the AUTO position. (b) Supply pneumatic pressure to the packs with an engine as follows: 1) Supply pressure to the pneumatic system with one or both engines (TASK 36-00-00-860-804). 2) Make sure that the aft outflow valve and a passenger door are open. 3) Set the applicable L PACK or R PACK switch, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, to the AUTO position. SUBTASK 21-51-13-790-001 (3) Do a soap bubble test of all the applicable duct joints. NOTE: No leakage is permitted. (a) If there is leakage, do these steps: 1) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches in the OFF position. WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE COOLING PACK DUCTS WHEN THEY ARE HOT. THE COOLING PACK DUCTS CAN BE HOT AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS. 2) Loosen the clamps. 3) Make sure that the ducts are aligned at the joints. 4) Tighten the clamps. 5) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches in the AUTO position. EFFECTIVITY ALL 6) Make sure that the leak has been repaired.

(d) Connect the air line to the water spray nozzle.
