H. Water Spray Nozzle Check

SUBTASK 21-51-16-860-021 (1) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System with the APU, TASK 36-00-00-860-803. SUBTASK 21-51-16-860-012 (2) Set the L(R) PACK switches, on the P5-10 overhead panel, to the HIGH position. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-51-16-860-013 (3) Set the trim air switch to the ON position. SUBTASK 21-51-16-860-014 (4) Set the CONT CAB, FWD CAB, and AFT CAB zone temperature selectors to the AUTO-C (fully cold) position. SUBTASK 21-51-16-210-001 (5) Use a flashlight to see that a spray of air and water comes of the L(R) water spray nozzle. NOTE: The quantity of water is a function of the air humidity and the pack air flow. (a) Make sure that the water spray pattern from each spray nozzle is approximately the same. (b) Make sure that the water sprays are approximately circular and are continuous. (c) If the water sprays are not satisfactory, do the following steps to examine these parts for leakage or blockage: 1) The water collector manifold 2) The water extractor 3) The water extractor duct 4) The water spray nozzle 5) The air and water supply lines from the water extractor to the water spray nozzle. SUBTASK 21-51-16-860-015 (6) Set the L(R) PACK switches to the OFF position. SUBTASK 21-51-16-210-002 (7) Check the water collection manifold for leakage or blockage. (a) Disconnect the water output port line [2] at the water collection manifold. (b) Set the L(R) PACK switches, on the P5-10 overhead panel, to the HIGH position. (c) Feel for air or water to come out of the hole in the water collection manifold where you removed the line. (d) If there is no air or water, examine the water collection manifold for leakage or blockage. SUBTASK 21-51-16-420-002 (8) Connect the water output port line [2] at the water collection manifold. SUBTASK 21-51-16-860-016 (9) Set the L(R) PACK switches to the OFF position. SUBTASK 21-51-16-210-003 (10) Check the water extractor for leakage or blockage. (a) Disconnect the water drain lines [1] at each water drain nipple of the water extractors. (b) Set the L(R) PACK switches, on the P5-10 overhead panel, to the HIGH position. (c) Feel for air or water to come out of the hole in the water extractor where you removed the line. (d) If there is no air or water, examine the water extractor for leakage or blockage. SUBTASK 21-51-16-420-003 (11) Connect the water drain lines [1] at each water drain nipple of the water extractors. SUBTASK 21-51-16-860-017 (12) Set the L(R) PACK switches to the OFF position. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-51-16-210-004 (13) Check the water extractor duct for leakage or blockage. (a) Disconnect the drain line [3] at the water extractor duct. (b) Set the L(R) PACK switches, on the P5-10 overhead panel, to the HIGH position. (c) Feel for air or water to come out of the hole in the water extractor duct where you removed the line. (d) If there is no air or water, examine the water extractor duct for leakage or blockage. SUBTASK 21-51-16-420-004 (14) Connect the drain line [3] at the water extractor duct. SUBTASK 21-51-16-110-001 (15) If the water spray nozzle is blocked or clogged, do the steps that follow to clean the nozzle: (a) Remove the nozzle from the airplane, do this task: Water Spray Nozzle Removal, TASK 21-51-16-000-801. (b) Soak the nozzle assembly in solvent degreasing solvent, B50126. (c) Use compressed air to blow out loose particles from the nozzle. (d) Do steps (b) and (c) again if necessary to clean the inner areas of the nozzle. (e) Use a soft bristle brush, STD-123, to remove external particles from the nozzle. (f) Soak the nozzle in general detergent, B50117, and water, G50256, to remove the solvent. (g) Dry the nozzle with compressed air. (h) Examine the nozzle to make sure that there is no external damage. (i) Use a low pressure air source of between to 0.5 psi (34.5 mBar) - 1 psi (69 mBar) to blow air through the nozzle. 1) Make sure that air flows freely through the air inlet and water inlet. (j) Install the nozzle, do this task: Water Spray Nozzle Installation, TASK 21-51-16-400-801.

(b) Disconnect the electrical connector [2] from the ram air control temperature sensor. (c) Loosen the B-nut to remove the hose [9] from the compressor outlet duct [3]. (d) Remove the clamshell clamp [6]. 1) Lift the three latch pawls at the same time to release the clamshell clamp [6]. (e) Move the sleeve [7] to the adjacent duct. CAUTION HOLD THE DUCT WHEN YOU LOOSEN THE CLAMP. THE DUCT CAN FALL WHEN THE CLAMP IS LOOSE. THE DUCT CAN BE DAMAGED IF IT FALLS. (f) Remove the clamp [4] that holds the compressor outlet duct [3] to the heat exchanger. (g) Remove the compressor outlet duct [3]. (h) Remove and discard the O-rings [8]. (i) Remove and discard the O-ring [5].

F. Mix Muff Removal

SUBTASK 21-51-17-020-002 (1) To remove the mix muff [16], do these steps: (a) Disconnect the flex hose [10] from the mix muff [16]. (b) Loosen the clamps [14] that attach the flexible duct [15] to the mix muff [16]. (c) Move the flexible duct [15] off the mix muff [16]. (d) Remove the clamp [13]. CAUTION HOLD THE MIX MUFF WHEN YOU LOOSEN THE CLAMP. THE MIX MUFF CAN FALL WHEN THE CLAMP IS LOOSE. THE MIX MUFF CAN BE DAMAGED IF IT FALLS. (e) Loosen the clamp [11] that attaches the mix muff [16] to the air cycle machine. (f) Remove the mix muff [16]. (g) Remove and discard the O-ring [12]. SUBTASK 21-51-17-620-001 (2) Put covers on the duct openings to prevent the entry of unwanted materials.

G. Compressor Outlet Duct Installation

SUBTASK 21-51-17-020-004 (1) To install the compressor outlet duct [3], do these steps: (a) Apply a light coat grease, D00504, or Molykote 44 grease, medium, D50104, to the O-ring [5] and O-rings [8]. (b) Install the new O-ring [5]. (c) Install the new O-rings [8] on the duct ends. (d) Put the compressor outlet duct [3] into its position. 1) Hold the compressor outlet duct [3] in position when you install the clamps. NOTE: The duct connections are not self aligning. EFFECTIVITY ALL (e) Apply compound, D50320, to the bolt threads of the clamp [4]. (f) Install the clamp [4] that holds the compressor outlet duct [3] to the heat exchanger. 1) Do not fully tighten the clamp [4]. (g) Move the sleeve [7] over the duct ends. (h) Install the clamshell clamp [6]. 1) Push the two halves of the clamshell clamp [6] together until the three latch pawls are latched. (i) Tighten the clamp [4] to 45 in-lb (5.1 N·m) - 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m). (j) With hand force, gently push the compressor outlet duct in the direction of the adjacent mix muff duct until the compressor outlet duct reaches the maximum flexed position. (k) Make sure that there is a minimum clearance of 0.20 in. (5.1 mm) to the adjacent mix muff duct when the compressor outlet duct is in the flexed position. (l) Install the electrical connector [2] on the ram air control temperature sensor. (m) Install the electrical connector [1] on the compressor outlet overheat switch. (n) Apply a light coating of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the hose [9]. (o) Reconnect the hose [9] to the compressor outlet duct [3]. (c) Install the bonding jumper [5] to the ground tab [19] on the actuator [15] as follows: EFFECTIVITY ALL 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 1) Clean the mating surfaces of the screw [1], washer [3], washers [4], nut [6], and ground tab [19] as follows: a) Use a sealant removal tool, COM-2481, and sealant removal tool handle, COM-4746, to remove the majority of the adhesive. b) Use a cotton wiper, G00034, soaked in solvent, B00666, solvent, B00184, or solvent, B00148, until all the adhesive is removed as follows: <1> Pour the solvent onto the wiper to avoid contamination of the solvent container. <2> Wipe or scrub the surface to be cleaned with the solvent soaked wiper. <3> Immediately wipe the cleaned surfaces with a clean cotton wiper, G00034. c) Use a clean cotton wiper, G00034, to remove all excess solvent that may remain on the parts. d) Repeat the cleaning action until no discoloration shows on the wiper. e) Dry surface before the solvent evaporates. 2) Install the screw [1], washer [3], bonding jumper [5], washers [4], and nut [6] to the ground tab [19]. F. Ram Air Inlet Deflector Door Installation

SUBTASK 21-51-22-420-001 (1) Put the ram air inlet deflector door [1] in its position. SUBTASK 21-51-22-420-002 (2) Install the bolts [2] and the washers [3] that attach the hinge of ram air inlet deflector door [1] to the airplane. SUBTASK 21-51-22-100-001 (3) Prepare the mating surfaces (SWPM 20-20-00). (a) Do abrasive cleaning procedure for mating surface of deflector door [1], washers [6], and bonding jumper [7]. (b) Do the solvent cleaning procedure for the mating surfaces of the terminal of deflector door [1], washers [6], and bonding jumper [7]. SUBTASK 21-51-22-420-003 (4) Do the steps that follow to install the bonding jumper [7]: (a) Install the washer [6]. (b) Put the bonding jumper [7] in its position and install the screw [4]. (c) Tighten the screw [4] to 32 in-lb (3.6 N·m) - 38 in-lb (4.3 N·m). SUBTASK 21-51-22-760-001 (5) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the bonding jumper [7] and the structure. (a) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. (b) Make sure that the electrical bounding resistance is not greater than 0.001 ohms (1 milliohms). SUBTASK 21-51-22-640-001 (6) Apply PR-1776M Class B Sealant, A50345, on the terminal of bonding jumper [7], washer [6], and screw [4]. SUBTASK 21-51-22-420-004 (7) Install the bolt [9], washer [10], washer [8], and nut [11] that attach the ram air inlet deflector door [1] to the links. (a) Make sure that the spring is in its position on the support assembly and around the inboard link (Figure 401). (b) Make sure that the links are in the correct positions (View A-A, Figure 401). SUBTASK 21-51-22-820-004 (8) If it is necessary, adjust the air inlet deflector door [1] (TASK 21-51-22-400-803).

F. Ram Air Inlet Deflector Door Shaft Assembly Installation

SUBTASK 21-51-22-420-005 (1) Do these steps to install the shaft [48]: NOTE: You must remove the link [49] from the shaft assembly before you can install the shaft [48] into the ram air inlet. (a) Remove the nut [33], washer [32], and bolt [31], that attach the links [49] to the shaft [48]. EFFECTIVITY ALL (b) Remove the links [49] from the shaft [48]. (c) Put the links [49] in their positions. 1) Make sure that the inboard and outboard links are opposite for the left and right side. NOTE: The circular edge of each link should point down after the installation. (d) Do a abrasive clearing procedure for surfaces contacting mating parts, shafts and crankarms or collars (TASK 20-10-34-120-801). (e) Do a solvent clearing procedure for surfaces contacting mating parts, shafts and crankarms or collars (TASK 20-10-34-110-802). (f) Apply Loctite 7471 Primer T Activator, A50086, and Loctite 641 compound, A50463, to surfaces contacting mating parts, shafts and crankarms or collars. 1) Air dry primer/activator for five minutes minimum prior to the application of retaining compounds. 2) Cover locking surfaces with retaining compound by a continuous fillet visible at the parting line of the assembled joint. a) Remove excess material. 3) Do not move joined parts to handling, vibration or shock until cured. 4) Cure parts for one hour, if temperature is or more than 70°F (21°C). a) Cure parts for 72 hours, if temperature is 40°F (4°C) - 70°F (21°C). NOTE: Locking materials do not cure sufficiently at temperatures below 40°F (4°C). (g) Install the bushing [47], washer [35], bolt [36], and washer [35]. 1) Make sure that the links [49] are in the correct positions (View A-A, Figure 402). (h) While you hold the links [49], insert the shaft [48] into the ram air inlet in an outboard through the spring [50] and the holes in the top ends of the links [49]. 1) Make sure that you insert the shaft [48] so that the end without the hole goes in first. (i) Install the bolt [31], washer [32], and nut [33] that attach the links [49] to the shaft [48]. (j) Make sure that the spring [50] is in its position on the support assembly and around the inboard link. 1) Make sure that shaft assembly rotates freely and not bind. CAUTION DO NOT LUBRICATE THE BEARING WITH GREASE OR WD-40. IF YOU LUBRICATE, THE BEARING LINER CAN SWELL, DECREASING THE CLEARANCE AND LEADING TO INCREASED ROTATIONAL BREAK￾AWAY TORQUE. (k) Install the bolts [54], washers [52], and nuts [51] that attach the bearing support assembly [53] and spring [50] to the support assembly. SUBTASK 21-51-22-420-025 (2) Do these steps to install the arm assembly [40]: (a) Put the arm assembly [40] in its position on the end of the shaft [48]. (b) Install the bolt [38], washer [39], washer [43], and nut [44]. (c) Put the link extension [37] in its position and install the bolt [42], washer [41], washer [45], and nut [46]. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-51-22-820-005 (3) If it is necessary, adjust the air inlet deflector door (TASK 21-51-22-400-803).

21-51-22-200-802Ram Air Inlet Door Linkage InspectionPDF p. 1275

2. Ram Air Inlet Door Linkage Inspection (Figure 601)

A. General

(1) This task has the steps to inspect the ram air inlet door linkage inspection.

B. References

Reference Title 21-51-21-000-801 Ram Air Inlet Actuator Removal (P/B 401) 21-51-21-400-801 Ram Air Inlet Actuator Installation (P/B 401)

C. Tools/Equipment

Reference Description STD-7173 Gage - Force, 0-50 lbs. capacity

D. Prepare for the Inspection

SUBTASK 21-51-22-020-030 (1) Disconnect the actuator from the arm assembly [31] (TASK 21-51-21-000-801).

E. Ram Air Inlet Door Linkage Inspection

SUBTASK 21-51-22-710-001 (1) Use a force gage, STD-7173, to check the bearings in the ram air inlet door linkages assembly. (a) Connect the force gage, STD-7173, to the arm assembly [31]. (b) Pull the force gage, STD-7173, to rotate the arm assembly [31]. 1) Make sure that the direction of the force is perpendicular to the arm assembly [31]. (c) Record the initial force (lbf or N) required to move the ram air inlet linkage assembly and share the results with . NOTE: Although a maximum force required has not yet been determined, preliminary data shows that an initial force over 20 lbf (89 N), may indicate that the self-lubricating bearings within the ram air inlet linkage assembly may be degraded.

F. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 21-51-22-420-026 (1) Connect the actuator to the arm assembly [31] (TASK 21-51-21-400-801).

E. Ram Air Inlet Modulation Panels Removal

NOTE: The ram air inlet modulation panels have a forward panel and an aft panel. It is necessary to remove the forward panel before you can remove the aft panel. SUBTASK 21-51-23-020-001 (1) Remove the forward modulation panel [1] as follows: (a) Remove the bolts [3] that attach the forward end of the aft modulation panel [2] to the aft end of the forward modulation panel [1]. NOTE: Let the forward modulation panel come down. This will permit access to the bolts and washers that attach the forward end of the forward modulation panel to the ram air inlet forward fairing support. (b) Hold the panel while removing bolts and washers. After the last bolt is removed the forward panel will fall out of the airplane. EFFECTIVITY ALL (c) Remove the bolts [4] and washers [5] from the forward hinge on the forward modulation panel [1]. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU HOLD THE PANEL WHEN YOU REMOVE BOLTS AND WASHERS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, THE FORWARD PANEL WILL FALL OUT OF THE AIRPLANE WHEN YOU REMOVE THE LAST BOLT. (d) Remove the forward modulation panel [1] from the ram air inlet. SUBTASK 21-51-23-020-002 (2) Remove the aft modulation panel [2] as follows: (a) If it is necessary, disconnect the ram air inlet actuator arm from the shaft of the aft modulation panel [2] (TASK 21-51-21-000-801). (b) Disconnect the clevis assemblies [8] from the aft modulation panel [2]: 1) Remove the nut [12], washers [10], bushing [11], and bolt [9] that connect each clevis assembly [8] to the aft modulation panel [2]. (c) Pull the aft modulation panel [2] out of the ram air inlet.

(b) Move the aft end of the flexible duct [40] forward off of the ram air exit duct [26]. (c) Disconnect the bonding jumper [36] and bonding jumper [37] from the rear spar [35] as follows: 1) Remove the nut [39] and washer [38]. 2) Remove the bonding jumper [36] and bonding jumper [37]. (g) Put a cover on the opening to the plenum/diffuser to keep out unwanted material. ALL

21-51-24-340-801Resin Damage - Fiberglass DuctsPDF p. 1323

2. Resin Damage - Fiberglass Ducts

A. General

(1) This procedure gives instructions for the repair of a fiberglass ram air duct with an application of resin. (2) A resin damage repair is applicable when there are no holes or punctures in the ram air duct but one of these defects are present: (a) Exposed fibers (b) Soft areas from impact damage (c) Delamination (d) Loss of resin or voids

To remove the duct, do this task: Ram Air Ducts - Removal, TASK 21-51-24-000-801 SUBTASK 21-51-24-840-002 (3) Do these steps to prepare the damaged area of the duct: WARNING DO NOT GET METHYL ETHYL KETONE (MEK) IN YOUR MOUTH OR EYES, OR ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM MEK. PUT ON A PROTECTIVE SPLASH GOGGLE AND GLOVES WHEN YOU USE MEK. KEEP MEK AWAY FROM SPARKS, FLAME AND HEAT. MEK IS A POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE SOLVENT WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (a) Use the solvent, B00148 and a cotton wiper, G00034 to clean the duct repair area. (b) Sand the damaged area to remove any unwanted contamination from the duct. (c) Use the solvent, B00148 and a cotton wiper, G00034 to clean the duct joint area. SUBTASK 21-51-24-840-003 (4) Prepare the applicable resin: (a) Ram air inlet duct repair - resin, G50400 (b) Ram air exhaust duct repair - resin, G02451

F. Repair the Air Conditioning Duct

SUBTASK 21-51-24-340-001 (1) Use resin, G50400 to repair the damaged area of the ram air inlet duct: (a) Use a brush, STD-122 or hypodermic syringe, STD-854 to apply the resin to the damaged area of the duct. (b) Apply a thin, smooth layer of the resin to the damaged area of the duct. (c) Put a piece of solid parting film, G50104 on the duct and press lightly to remove any bubbles or any wrinkles and to remove unwanted resin. (d) Remove the solid parting film, G50104 from the duct and remove any unwanted resin with a wiping cloth. (e) Do one of these steps to cure the resin: 1) Permit the resin, G50400 to cure for a minimum of 30 minutes at 150°, ± 10° F. 2) Permit the resin, G50400 to cure for 24 hours at room temperature (70° F minimum). SUBTASK 21-51-24-340-002 (2) Use resin, G02451 to repair the damaged area of the ram air exhaust duct. (a) Use a brush, STD-122 or hypodermic syringe, STD-854 to apply the resin to the damaged area of the duct. (b) Apply a thin, smooth layer of the resin to the damaged area of the duct. EFFECTIVITY ALL (c) Put a piece of solid parting film, G50104 on the duct and press lightly to remove any bubbles or any wrinkles and to remove unwanted resin. (d) Remove the solid parting film, G50104 from the duct and remove any unwanted resin with a wiping cloth. (e) Permit the resin, G02451 to cure for 3 hours, ± 10 minutes at 150°, ± 10° F. 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999; 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169 POST SB 737-47-1003 SUBTASK 21-51-24-340-027 (3) If the repair was made to the outer surface of the ram air inlet duct access panel, do the steps that follow: (a) Hand sand the surface with 180 grit abrasive paper, G50381 or finer abrasive paper to remove the glossy finish. (b) Remove the dust with a cotton wiper, G00034. (c) Prior to the application of the coating, C00767, clean the surface with solvent, B00094 and a cotton wiper, G00034. (d) Apply the coating, C00767 by spray to a dry film thickness of 0.4 to 0.8 mils. (e) Allow the coating, C00767 to cure a minimum of 2 hours at 60°F (16°C) or 30 minutes at 140°F (60°C). (f) Hand sand the surface with 150 grit abrasive paper, G02428 or finer abrasive paper. (g) Remove the dust with a cotton wiper, G00034. (h) Apply the primer, C00766 by spray to a dry film thickness of 0.5 to 0.8 mils. (i) Allow the primer, C00766 to cure a minimum of 6 hours at 60°F (16°C) or 40 minutes at 140°F (60°C). ALL

21-51-24-340-803Structural Repair - Fiberglass DuctsPDF p. 1331

4. Structural Repair - Fiberglass Ducts (Figure 801)

A. General

(1) This procedure gives instructions for making a structural repair to a fiberglass air conditioning duct. (2) A structural repair is applicable when the damage to the air conditioning duct is a cut or a hole that is more than 0.25 in. (6.35 mm) wide and more than 3 in. (76.2 mm) long but less than 5 percent of the total surface area of the duct. If the damage is more than 5 percent of the total surface area of the duct, then replace the duct section.

For example, if there are 6 plies, sand 3 in. (76.2 mm) from the opening on all sides (1/2 x 6 = 3 inches)(12.7 x 6 = 76.2 millimeters). H. Ram Air Exhaust Actuator Installation

SUBTASK 21-51-27-910-002 CAUTION DO NOT TOUCH THE COMPONENT BEFORE YOU DO THE PROCEDURE FOR DEVICES THAT ARE SENSITIVE TO ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE. ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE COMPONENT. (1) Do the necessary steps to protect the ram air exhaust actuator [2] from electrostatic discharge, do this task: ESDS Handling for Metal Encased Unit Installation, TASK 20-40-12-400-802. SUBTASK 21-51-27-020-021 CAUTION DO NOT TOUCH THE CONDUCTOR PINS OR OTHER CONDUCTORS ON THE COMPONENT. IF YOU TOUCH THESE CONDUCTORS, ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE COMPONENT. (2) Remove protective caps or bags from the ram air exhaust actuator [2], do this task: Conductive Dust Cap and Connector Cover Removal, TASK 20-40-12-000-804. SUBTASK 21-51-27-420-001 (3) Put the ram air exhaust actuator [2] in its position on the ram air exhaust duct [1]. SUBTASK 21-51-27-420-004 (4) Attach the aft end of the ram air exhaust actuator [2] to the ram air exhaust duct assembly as follows: (a) Put the countersunk side of the washer [5] below the head of the bolt [4]. (b) Put the bolt [4] through the ram air exhaust duct assembly and the boss on the ram air exhaust actuator [2] in the outboard direction. (c) Install the washer [6] and nut [7]. SUBTASK 21-51-27-420-002 (5) Do not attach the forward end of the ram air exhaust actuator [2] to the actuator drive arm [16] at this time. SUBTASK 21-51-27-160-001 (6) Prepare the bonding tab and bonding jumper [3] for installation as follows: EFFECTIVITY 349-999 (a) Use 180 grit wet/dry silicon carbide sandpaper, G50221, to remove all signs of the adhesive on the washer [5], washer [6], washer [14], screw [15], nut [7], nut [12], nut [13], bonding jumper [3], and bonding tab used for the previous installation of the bonding jumper [3]. (b) Use solvent, B00666, to clean all surfaces until the wipes are no longer discolored. (c) Use MicroCare fiber wipes, G50637, to remove all signs of the solvent. SUBTASK 21-51-27-420-003 (7) Attach the bonding jumper [3] to the bonding tab on the ram air exhaust actuator [2] as follows: (a) Put the washer [14] on the screw [15] and put the screw [15] through the blue end of the bonding jumper [3]. (b) Put the washer [14] on the screw [15] adjacent to the bonding jumper [3]. (c) Insert the screw [15] through the bonding tab on the ram air exhaust actuator [2]. (d) Install the washer [14] and nut [13] on the screw [15]. (e) Tighten the nut [13] to 40 ±5 in-lb (4.5 ±0.6 N·m). SUBTASK 21-51-27-760-001 (8) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the bonding tab and the bonding jumper [3]: (a) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. (b) Make sure that the bonding resistance is not more than 0.001 ohm (1.0 milliohm). SUBTASK 21-51-27-390-001 (9) Apply adhesive, A01076, to fully encapsulate the fasteners.

I. Ram Air Exhaust Actuator Adjustment

SUBTASK 21-51-27-820-001 (1) Make sure that the rod end [17] of the ram air exhaust actuator [2] is not attached to the actuator drive arm [16]. SUBTASK 21-51-27-420-007 (2) Connect electrical connectors, D14390, and D14392, to the left ram air exhaust actuator, M2796. SUBTASK 21-51-27-420-008 (3) Connect electrical connectors, D14398, and D14400, to the right ram air exhaust actuator, M2798. SUBTASK 21-51-27-860-002 (4) Close these circuit breakers: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name A 4 C01950 AIR CONDITIONING RAM AIR MOD LEFT A 8 C00555 AIR CONDITIONING RAM AIR MOD CONT L A 9 C01158 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONTROL LEFT DC A 11 C01159 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONTROL LEFT AC EFFECTIVITY 349-999 SUBTASK 21-51-27-860-003 (5) Close these circuit breakers: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name B 4 C01951 AIR CONDITIONING RAM AIR MOD RIGHT B 8 C01178 AIR CONDITIONING RAM AIR MOD CONT R B 9 C01161 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONT RIGHT DC B 11 C01162 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONT RIGHT AC SUBTASK 21-51-27-860-009 (6) Extend the trailing edge flaps to position 1 (TASK 27-51-00-860-803). SUBTASK 21-51-27-860-010 (7) Do this task: Put the Airplane in the Air Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-801. SUBTASK 21-51-27-860-011 CAUTION MAKE SURE TO FOLLOW THE STEPS TO ADJUST THE LOUVERS TO THE FULLY CLOSED POSITION CORRECTLY. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, THIS CAN CAUSE AN INCORRECT RIGGING CONDITION AND POSSIBLE DAMAGE TO THE AIR CYCLE MACHINE. (8) Retract the left and right trailing edge flaps to the flaps fully up position (TASK 27-51-00-860-804). SUBTASK 21-51-27-820-002 (9) Do one of the following steps to set the louvers to the flight fully closed position: NOTE: The preferred steps use rigging clips. The alternate steps use non-metallic shims. (a) Use rigging clips of gap tool, SPL-20203, to set the louvers to the flight fully closed position as follows (Figure 402): 1) Move the actuator drive arm [16] to turn the exhaust louvers until a rigging clip can be inserted on the forward and mid louvers. 2) Insert one rigging clip on the forward louver, and insert another rigging clip on the mid louver. 3) Position the rigging clips with slight separation between them. 4) Manually turn the louvers to the closed position until one of the rigging clips touches the adjacent louver. NOTE: This position of the exhaust louvers is the flight fully closed position with the louvers set at approximately 12 degrees. 5) Make sure that the rigging clip that touched the adjacent louver does not become loose or fall out during the connection of the actuator rod end [17] to the actuator drive arm [16]. (b) Use non-metallic shims of gap tool, SPL-20203, or non-metallic shims, G51239, to set the louvers to the flight fully closed position as follows (Figure 403): NOTE: Non-metallic shims can be machined or sanded to get a completed dimension of 0.680 ±0.010 in. (17.272 ±0.254 mm) thick x 7 in. (177.8 mm) long x 2 in. (50.8 mm) wide. Multiple thinner laminations can be bonded together to get the correct thickness. EFFECTIVITY 349-999 1) Move the actuator drive arm [16] to turn the exhaust louvers until a shim (0.680 ±0.010 in. (17.272 ±0.254 mm) thick x 7 in. (177.8 mm) long x 2 in. (50.8 mm) wide) can be inserted between each pair of louvers. 2) Insert one shim between the forward and mid louvers, and insert another shim between the mid and aft louvers. 3) Position the shims with slight separation between them. 4) Manually turn the louvers to the closed position until one of the shims is caught between the louvers. NOTE: This position of the exhaust louvers is the flight fully closed position with the louvers set at approximately 12 degrees. 5) Make sure that the shim that was caught between the louvers does not become loose or fall out during the connection of the actuator rod end [17] to the actuator drive arm [16]. SUBTASK 21-51-27-420-006 (10) Connect the rod end [17] of the ram air exhaust actuator [2] to the actuator drive arm [16] as follows: (a) If the hole in the rod end [17] does not align with the holes in the actuator drive arm [16], do these steps: 1) Remove the lockwire from the jamnut on the rod end [17]. 2) Adjust the length of the rod end [17] by maximum of ±0.125 in. (3.2 mm) (or 4 turns in either direction) until the holes in the rod end [17] and actuator drive arm [16] align. 3) Hold the rod end [17] and tighten the jamnut until it is seated against the rod end. 4) Tighten the jamnut to 110 ±10 in-lb (12.4 ±1.1 N·m). 5) Install lockwire to keep the jamnut in its position. (b) Put the countersunk side of the washer [10] below the head of the bolt [9]. (c) Put the bolt [9] through the actuator drive arm [16], bushing [19], rod end [17] of the actuator drive arm [16], and spacer [18] in the inboard direction. (d) Install the washer [11] and nut [12]. SUBTASK 21-51-27-080-001 (11) Remove the rigging clips of gap tool, SPL-20203, or shims of gap tool, SPL-20203, or shims, G51239, from the louvers.

J. Ram Air Exhaust Actuator Adjustment Check

SUBTASK 21-51-27-860-014 (1) Extend the left and right trailing edge flaps to position 1 (TASK 27-51-00-860-803). SUBTASK 21-51-27-710-006 (2) Make sure that the inlet doors move to the open position smoothly without hanging or binding. SUBTASK 21-51-27-710-014 (3) Retract the trailing edge flaps to the fully up position (TASK 27-51-00-860-804). SUBTASK 21-51-27-710-015 (4) Make sure that the left (right) ram air inlets doors move towards the closed position. SUBTASK 21-51-27-860-015 (5) Do this task: Return the Airplane to the Ground Mode, TASK 32-09-00-860-802. EFFECTIVITY 349-999 SUBTASK 21-51-27-710-010 (6) Make sure that the deflector door extends. SUBTASK 21-51-27-710-007 (7) Make sure that the ram air exit louvers move to the most open position without hanging or binding.

(4) To get access to the right SRADA, do these steps (TASK 06-41-00-800-801): (a) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 192DR ECS High Pressure Access Door (b) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 192CR ECS Access Door (c) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 192JR Air Conditioning Panel - Aft SUBTASK 21-51-27-020-015 (5) To prepare for the installation of the SRADA stowage link for the left pack, do this step: (a) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name A 4 C01950 AIR CONDITIONING RAM AIR MOD LEFT A 8 C00555 AIR CONDITIONING RAM AIR MOD CONT L A 9 C01158 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONTROL LEFT DC A 11 C01159 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONTROL LEFT AC SUBTASK 21-51-27-020-016 (6) To prepare for the installation of the SRADA stowage link for the right pack, do this step: EFFECTIVITY 349-999 (a) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name B 4 C01951 AIR CONDITIONING RAM AIR MOD RIGHT B 8 C01178 AIR CONDITIONING RAM AIR MOD CONT R B 9 C01161 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONT RIGHT DC B 11 C01162 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONT RIGHT AC

G. Smart Ram Air Door Actuator Rod End Disconnect

SUBTASK 21-51-27-020-017 (1) If you install the SRADA stowage link on the left side, disconnect, cap, and stow electrical connectors D14390 and D14392 on the left SRADA, M2796. SUBTASK 21-51-27-020-018 (2) If you install the SRADA stowage link on the right side, disconnect, cap, and stow electrical connectors D14398 and D14400 on the right SRADA, M2798. SUBTASK 21-51-27-020-019 (3) Disconnect the rod end [17] of the ram air exhaust actuator [2] from the actuator drive arm [16] as follows: (a) Remove the nut [12], washer [11], spacer [18], bushing [19], washer [10], and bolt [9] that retain the rod end [17] to the actuator drive arm [16].

H. Secure Exit Louvers Open

SUBTASK 21-51-27-020-020 (1) Remove the nut, washers, and bolt that attach the most forward louver drive arm to the link assembly. SUBTASK 21-51-27-420-016 (2) Move the link assembly to open the exit louvers until the most forward hole in the link assembly lines up with the hole in the most forward louver drive arm. SUBTASK 21-51-27-420-017 (3) In the same sequence that they were removed, install the nut, washers, and bolt through the most forward hole in the link assembly and the hole in the most forward louver drive arm.

I. Smart Ram Air Door Actuator Stowage Link Installation

SUBTASK 21-51-27-420-018 (1) Connect one end of the Link - Stowage SRADA, SPL-14767, to the actuator drive arm [16] as follows: (a) Put the countersunk side of the washer [10] under the head of the bolt [9]. (b) Put the bolt [9] through the actuator drive arm [16], bushing [19], Link - Stowage SRADA, SPL-14767, and the spacer [18] in the inboard direction. (c) Install the washer [11] and nut [12]. SUBTASK 21-51-27-420-019 (2) Connect the other end of the Link - Stowage SRADA, SPL-14767, to the rod end [17] of the ram air exhaust actuator [2] as follows: (a) Put the countersunk side of the washer under the head of the bolt. (b) Put the bolt through the rod end [17] and the Link - Stowage SRADA, SPL-14767. (c) Install the plain washer and locknut. EFFECTIVITY 349-999

J. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 21-51-27-410-008 (1) For the left SRADA, do these steps: (a) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 192CL ECS Access Door (b) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 192JL Air Conditioning Panel - Aft SUBTASK 21-51-27-410-009 (2) For the right SRADA, do these steps (TASK 06-41-00-800-801): (a) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 192JR Air Conditioning Panel - Aft (b) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 192CR ECS Access Door (c) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 192DR ECS High Pressure Access Door NOTE: The ECS high pressure access door, 192DR, will not latch into place if the ECS access door, 192CR, is not closed. SUBTASK 21-51-27-410-007 (3) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breakers for the SRADA stowage link for the left pack: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name A 4 C01950 AIR CONDITIONING RAM AIR MOD LEFT A 8 C00555 AIR CONDITIONING RAM AIR MOD CONT L A 9 C01158 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONTROL LEFT DC A 11 C01159 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONTROL LEFT AC SUBTASK 21-51-27-410-010 (4) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breakers for the SRADA stowage link for the right pack: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name B 4 C01951 AIR CONDITIONING RAM AIR MOD RIGHT B 8 C01178 AIR CONDITIONING RAM AIR MOD CONT R B 9 C01161 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONT RIGHT DC B 11 C01162 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONT RIGHT AC

E. Overheat Switch Removal

SUBTASK 21-51-40-020-001 WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE COOLING PACK DUCTS WHEN THEY ARE HOT. THE COOLING PACK DUCTS CAN BE HOT AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS. (1) Disconnect the electrical connector [2] from the compressor discharge overheat switch [1]. (a) If it is necessary to remove the turbine inlet overheat switch at the same time as the compressor discharge overheat switch [1], mark the electrical connector [2]. NOTE: The electrical connectors of the compressor discharge overheat switch and turbine inlet overheat switch are very close and two plugs are completely consistent. Marking the electrical connector will help distinguish the connectors in the installation task. SUBTASK 21-51-40-020-002 (2) Remove and discard the lockwire from the compressor discharge overheat switch [1]. SUBTASK 21-51-40-020-003 CAUTION USE TWO WRENCHES TO REMOVE THE OVERHEAT SWITCH FROM THE BOSS. IF YOU USE ONLY ONE WRENCH TO REMOVE THE OVERHEAT SWITCH, IT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE DUCT. (3) Use two wrenches to remove the compressor discharge overheat switch [1]. NOTE: Use one wrench to hold the boss. Use the other wrench to turn the compressor discharge overheat switch. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-51-40-020-004 (4) Remove and discard the O-ring [3] from the compressor discharge overheat switch [1].

F. Overheat Switch Installation

SUBTASK 21-51-40-640-002 (1) Apply a light coat of Molykote 44 grease, medium, D50104, to a new O-ring [3]. SUBTASK 21-51-40-420-001 (2) Install the lubricated O-ring [3] on the compressor discharge overheat switch [1]. SUBTASK 21-51-40-160-001 (3) Make sure that the mating surfaces of the boss and overheat switch nut are clean. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-51-40-640-001 (4) Apply a thin layer of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the compressor discharge overheat switch [1]. SUBTASK 21-51-40-420-005 (5) Put the compressor discharge overheat switch [1] in the boss on the duct. SUBTASK 21-51-40-420-002 CAUTION USE TWO WRENCHES TO INSTALL THE OVERHEAT SWITCH IN THE BOSS. IF YOU USE ONLY ONE WRENCH TO INSTALL THE OVERHEAT SWITCH, IT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE DUCT. (6) Use two wrenches to install the compressor discharge overheat switch [1]: NOTE: Use one wrench to hold the boss. Use the other wrench to turn the compressor discharge overheat switch. (a) Tighten the compressor discharge overheat switch [1] to 133 in-lb (15.0 N·m) - 147 in-lb (16.6 N·m). SUBTASK 21-51-40-420-003 (7) Install a new MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, on the compressor discharge overheat switch [1]. SUBTASK 21-51-40-420-004 CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT YOU CONNECT THE CORRECT ELECTRICAL CONNECTOR TO THE OVERHEAT SWITCH FOR COMPRESSOR DISCHARGE. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (8) Connect the electrical connector [2] to the compressor discharge overheat switch [1]. (a) If it is installed, remove the marking from the electrical connector [2].

Reference Description SPL-1552 Kit - Heater Probes, TEMPCAL Part #: BH24944-7 Supplier: 98869 SPL-3924 Tester - Thermo Switch, K-Type Thermocouple Switches Part #: H394R Supplier: 98869 Opt Part #: H294 Supplier: 98869 Opt Part #: H394 SERIES Supplier: 98869

C. Location Zones

Zone Area 192 Lower Wing-To-Body Fairing - Under Wing Box

D. Compressor Discharge Overheat Switch - Functional Test (Method I)

SUBTASK 21-51-40-020-009 (1) Remove the compressor discharge overheat switch, do this task: Compressor Discharge Overheat Switch Removal, TASK 21-51-40-000-801. (a) Re-connect the electrical connector to the compressor discharge overheat switch. SUBTASK 21-51-40-480-003 (2) Prepare K-Type thermocouple switch tester, SPL-3924, and TEMPCAL heater probe kit, SPL-1552, to test the compressor discharge overheat switch. NOTE: Use the correct heater probe to test overheat switch part number 572756–1. SUBTASK 21-51-40-710-013 (3) Use the test equipment to increase the temperature of the compressor discharge overheat switch as follows: (a) Set the test temperature on the tester to 370 ±5°F (188 ±3°C). (b) Increase the test temperature on the tester at a rate of not more than 2°F (1°C) per minute to 390 ±10°F (199 ±6°C). (c) Move the tester POWER switch to the ON position. SUBTASK 21-51-40-710-014 (4) When the temperature reaches 390 ±10°F (199 ±6°C), make sure that these lights come on: (a) PACK light, on the P5-10 panel. EFFECTIVITY ALL (b) MASTER CAUTION light, on the pilots' glareshield. SUBTASK 21-51-40-710-015 (5) Remove the heat from the compressor discharge overheat switch probe. SUBTASK 21-51-40-710-016 (6) Let the compressor discharge overheat switch probe cool down at a rate of not more than 2°F (1°C) per minute. NOTE: The compressor discharge overheat switch will reset when the probe temperature is 350°F (177°C). SUBTASK 21-51-40-710-017 (7) Push the TRIP RESET button, on the P5-10 panel. SUBTASK 21-51-40-710-018 (8) Push the MASTER CAUTION reset button, on the P7 glareshield panel. SUBTASK 21-51-40-710-019 (9) Make sure that the MASTER CAUTION light goes off. SUBTASK 21-51-40-420-010 (10) Install the compressor discharge overheat switch, do this task: Compressor Discharge Overheat Switch Installation, TASK 21-51-40-400-801.

E. Compressor Discharge Overheat Switch - Functional Test (Method II)

SUBTASK 21-51-40-020-010 (1) Remove the compressor discharge overheat switch, do this task: Compressor Discharge Overheat Switch Removal, TASK 21-51-40-000-801. SUBTASK 21-51-40-420-011 (2) Install a new or serviceable compressor discharge overheat switch, do this task: Compressor Discharge Overheat Switch Installation, TASK 21-51-40-400-801. NOTE: The compressor discharge overheat switch that was removed, should be tested according to the vendor CMM before it is put back into service. SUBTASK 21-51-40-020-011 (3) Remove the electrical connector from the compressor discharge overheat switch. SUBTASK 21-51-40-480-004 (4) Connect a jumper wire between pin 1 and pin 2 of the electrical connector. SUBTASK 21-51-40-210-003 (5) Make sure that these lights come on: (a) PACK light, on the P5-10 panel. (b) MASTER CAUTION light, on the pilots' glareshield. SUBTASK 21-51-40-080-002 (6) Disconnect the jumper wire. SUBTASK 21-51-40-860-031 (7) Push the TRIP RESET button, on the P5-10 panel. SUBTASK 21-51-40-860-032 (8) Push the MASTER CAUTION reset button, on the P7 glareshield panel. SUBTASK 21-51-40-210-004 (9) Make sure that the MASTER CAUTION light goes off. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-51-40-420-012 (10) Connect the electrical connector to the compressor discharge overheat switch.

D. Turbine Inlet Thermal Switch - Functional Test (Method I)

EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) PACK light, on the P5-10 panel. (b) MASTER CAUTION light, on the pilots' glareshield. SUBTASK 21-51-41-710-015 (5) Remove the heat from the turbine inlet thermal switch probe. D. Pack Discharge Overheat Switch - Functional Test (Method I)

SUBTASK 21-51-42-020-023-002 (1) If installed, remove the pack overheat discharge switch (TASK 21-51-42-000-803-002). (a) Re-connect the electrical connector to the pack discharge overheat switch. SUBTASK 21-51-42-480-001-002 (2) Prepare the K-Type thermocouple switch tester, SPL-3924, and TEMPCAL heater probe kit, SPL-3952, to test the pack discharge overheat switch. NOTE: Use the correct heater probe to test the pack discharge overheat switch. SUBTASK 21-51-42-720-001-002 (3) Use the test equipment to increase the temperature of the turbine inlet thermal switch as follows: (a) Set the test temperature on the tester to 230°F (110°C). (b) Wait for a minimum of five minutes. (c) Increase the test temperature on the tester at a rate of not more than 5°F (2.8°C) per minute to 250 ±10°F (121 ±6°C). Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-51-42-720-002-002 (4) Make sure that the PACK light, on the P5-10 panel, comes on when the temperature of the pack discharge overheat switch probe gets to 250 ±10°F (121 ±6°C). SUBTASK 21-51-42-020-024-002 (5) Remove the heat from the turbine inlet thermal switch probe. SUBTASK 21-51-42-720-003-002 (6) Let the turbine inlet thermal switch probe cool down at a rate of not more than 5°F (2.8°C) per minute. NOTE: The reset temperature for the pack discharge overheat switch is 150°F (66°C). SUBTASK 21-51-42-720-004-002 (7) Push the TRIP RESET light on the P5-10 panel. SUBTASK 21-51-42-420-023-002 (8) Do this task: Pack Discharge Overheat Switch Installation, TASK 21-51-42-400-803-002.

E. Pack Discharge Overheat Switch - Functional Test (Method II)

SUBTASK 21-51-42-020-025-002 (1) If installed, remove the pack overheat discharge switch (TASK 21-51-42-000-803-002). SUBTASK 21-51-42-420-024-002 (2) Install a new or serviceable pack overheat discharge switch (TASK 21-51-42-400-803-002). NOTE: The pack discharge overheat switch that was removed should be tested according to the vendor CMM before it is put back into service. SUBTASK 21-51-42-020-026-002 (3) Remove the electrical connector from the pack discharge overheat switch. SUBTASK 21-51-42-420-025-002 (4) Connect a jumper wire between pin 1 and pin 2 of the electrical connector. SUBTASK 21-51-42-720-005-002 (5) Make sure that the PACK light, on the P5-10 panel, comes on. SUBTASK 21-51-42-020-027-002 (6) Disconnect the jumper wire. SUBTASK 21-51-42-720-006-002 (7) Push the TRIP RESET button on the P5-10 panel. SUBTASK 21-51-42-420-026-002 (8) Connect the electrical connector to the pack discharge overheat switch.

21-51-45-100-801Pack Inlet Pressure Sensor Sense Line CleaningPDF p. 1411

2. Pack Inlet Pressure Sensor Sense Line Cleaning (Figure 701)

A. General

(1) This task provides instructions to clean the left pack pressure sensor, right pack pressure sensor, and sense lines.

B. References

Reference Title 21-51-45-000-801 Pack Inlet Pressure Sensor Removal (P/B 401) 21-51-45-400-801 Pack Inlet Pressure Sensor Installation (P/B 401)

C. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification G02314 Air - Compressed, Breathing BB-A-1034 Source I Grade A G50256 Water, Regular

D. Prepare for the Cleaning

SUBTASK 21-51-45-000-001 (1) Remove the pack pressure sensor [5]. (a) Do this task: Pack Inlet Pressure Sensor Removal, TASK 21-51-45-000-801. SUBTASK 21-51-45-000-002 (2) Remove the sense line [6] as follows: (a) Remove the three clamps [7]. 1) Remove the screw [8] and washers [9] that secure the clamps [7] to the structure. 2) Remove the clamps [7]. (b) Disconnect the sense line [6] from the duct connector [10] as follows: 1) Use a second wrench to hold the duct connector [10] when you disconnect the sense line [6]. (c) Remove the sense line [6]. SUBTASK 21-51-45-000-003 (3) Remove the sense line [12] and sense line [18] as follows: (a) Remove the clamp [15] and clamps [21]. 1) Remove the screw [13], washer [14], screw [19], and washer [20] that secure clamp [15] and each clamps [21] to the structure. 2) Remove the clamp [15] and clamps [21]. (b) Disconnect the sense line [18] from the duct connector [10] as follows: 1) Use a second wrench to hold the duct connector [10] when you disconnect the sense line [18]. EFFECTIVITY 385-999 (c) Remove the sense line [12] and sense line [18]. (d) If it is necessary, disconnect the nut [17] from the union [16] to disconnect sense line [18] from sense line [12].

E. Pack Inlet Pressure Sensor Sense Line Cleaning

SUBTASK 21-51-45-100-002 (1) If it is necessary, remove any ice buildup in the pack pressure sensor [5]. SUBTASK 21-51-45-100-003 (2) If it is necessary, remove any ice buildup in the sense line with warm water, G50256. SUBTASK 21-51-45-100-004 (3) Blow air, G02314, through the sense line weep hole [11] with compressed air. (a) Make sure that there is no debris, dirt, or unwanted materials in the sense line.

F. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 21-51-45-400-001 (1) Install the sense line [6] as follows: (a) Connect the sense line [6] to the duct connector [10] as follows: 1) Use a second wrench to hold duct connector [10] when you tighten the sense line [6]. 2) Tighten the B-nut on the sense line [6] to 160 in-lb (18 N·m). - 180 in-lb (20 N·m). (b) Install the clamps [7]. 1) Install the clamps [7] with the screws [8] and washers [9]. SUBTASK 21-51-45-400-003 (2) Install the sense line [12] and sense line [18] as follows: (a) If it was disconnected, reconnect the nut [17] to the union [16]. (b) Connect the sense line [18] to the duct connector [10] as follows: 1) Use a second wrench to hold duct connector [10] when you tighten the sense line [18]. 2) Tighten the B-nut on the sense line [18] to 160 in-lb (18 N·m) - 180 in-lb (20 N·m). (c) Install the clamp [15] and clamps [21]. 1) Install the clamp [15] with the screw [13] and washer [14]. 2) Install the clamps [21] with the screws [19] and washers [20]. SUBTASK 21-51-45-400-002 (3) Install the pack pressure sensor [5]. (a) Do this task: Pack Inlet Pressure Sensor Installation, TASK 21-51-45-400-801. (b) Tighten the B-nuts on the sense line [6] and sense line [12] to 90 in-lb (10 N·m). - 100 in-lb (11 N·m).

D. Prepare For The Resistance Test

SUBTASK 21-51-51-860-006 (1) Do this task: Aft Cargo Compartment Forward Bulkhead Liner - Removal, TASK 25-52-18-000-801. SUBTASK 21-51-51-860-007 (2) To do a test of the left mix manifold sensor, remove the left pack/zone temperature controller (TASK 21-61-20-000-801 or TASK 21-61-17-020-801). SUBTASK 21-51-51-860-008 (3) To do a test of the right mix manifold sensor, remove the right pack/zone temperature controller (TASK 21-61-20-000-801 or TASK 21-61-17-020-801). SUBTASK 21-51-51-710-001 (4) Make sure the pack has been off for 20 minutes or until it has reached ambient temperature.

E. Resistance Check Procedure

SUBTASK 21-51-51-700-001 (1) Use a digital thermometer, COM-3955 or equivalent, to measure the temperature adjacent to the applicable mix manifold temperature sensor. (a) Write down the temperature. SUBTASK 21-51-51-760-001 (2) Use the digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793 (preferred) to measure resistance between the following pin connections. NOTE: An equivalent meter can be used as long as the digital multimeter minimizes self-heating of the sensor element. The instrument must limit the current through the sensor to less than 100 microamperes when set to the 10K ohms scale. If you use resistance measuring instruments without this current-limiting feature you will get an error in resistance value due to self-heating of the sensor element. 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-384 SUBTASK 21-51-51-700-002 (3) For the right mix manifold temperature sensor, measure the resistance from pin A7 to pin B7 on connector D3860A for the right pack/zone temperature controller (WDM 21-51-22). 385-999 SUBTASK 21-51-51-700-005 (4) For the right mix manifold temperature sensor, measure the resistance from pin F9 to pin F10 on connector D15816B for the right pack/flow temperature controller (WDM 21-51-12). EFFECTIVITY ALL 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-384 SUBTASK 21-51-51-700-003 (5) For the left mix manifold temperature sensor, measure the resistance from pin A7 to pin B7 on connector D3858A for the left pack/zone temperature controller (WDM 21-51-12). 385-999 SUBTASK 21-51-51-700-006 (6) For the left mix manifold temperature sensor, measure the resistance from pin F9 to pin F10 on connector D15814B for the left pack/flow temperature controller (WDM 21-51-12). ALL SUBTASK 21-51-51-700-004 (7) Write down the resistance in Ohms that you measure. (a) For the mix manifold temperature sensors, find the temperature on (Figure 501) that is nearest to the temperature that you wrote down. (b) Compare the permitted range of resistance for that temperature to the resistance you wrote down. (c) If the resistance is out of range, replace the sensor. C. Preparation for the Resistance Test

SUBTASK 21-51-52-864-001 (1) Do this task: Remove Pressure from the Pneumatic System, TASK 36-00-00-860-806. SUBTASK 21-51-52-020-005 (2) To do a test of the left pack temperature sensor, remove the left pack/zone temperature controller as follows: (a) Do this task: Pack/Zone Temperature Controller - Removal, TASK 21-61-20-000-801 or Pack Flow Temperature Controller - Removal, TASK 21-61-17-020-801. SUBTASK 21-51-52-020-006 (3) To do a test of the right pack temperature sensor, remove the right pack/zone temperature controller as follows: (a) Do this task: Pack/Zone Temperature Controller - Removal, TASK 21-61-20-000-801 or Pack Flow Temperature Controller - Removal, TASK 21-61-17-020-801. SUBTASK 21-51-52-800-001 (4) Decrease the temperature in the pack bay until it agrees with the external ambient temperature.

D. Sensor Resistance Check Procedure

SUBTASK 21-51-52-700-001 (1) Measure the temperature adjacent to the applicable pack temperature sensor in the pack bay: (a) Use a digital thermometer, COM-3955 or equivalent, to measure the temperature adjacent to the applicable pack temperature sensor. (b) Record the temperature for later use. SUBTASK 21-51-52-700-002 (2) Use the digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793 (preferred) to measure resistance between connector pins. NOTE: Use an equivalent meter only if it gives a minimum quantity of heat to the sensor element. Make sure that the meter can give a limit of current through the sensor element of less than 100 microamperes. If the meter gives more than this limit of current, it could give too much heat to the sensor element. Too much heat on the sensor element can give an incorrect resistance value. SUBTASK 21-51-52-700-003 (3) For the Pack Zone Temperature Controller: (a) Measure the resistances for the left pack zone temperature sensor T471 as follows: 1) Measure the resistance from pin A6 to B6 on connector D3858A for the pack zone temperature controller (WDM 21-51-12). 2) Measure the resistance from pin D11 to D12 on connector D3860A for the pack zone temperature controller (WDM 21-51-13). (b) Measure the resistances for the right pack zone temperature sensor T474 as follows: EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Measure the resistance from pin D11 to D12 on connector D3858A for the pack zone temperature controller (WDM 21-51-23). 2) Measure the resistance from pin A6 to B6 on connector D3860A for the pack zone temperature controller (WDM 21-51-22). SUBTASK 21-51-52-700-004 (4) For the Pack Flow Temperature Controller: (a) Measure the resistances for the left pack flow temperature sensor T471 as follows: 1) Measure the resistance from pin J9 to J10 on connector D15814B for the pack flow temp controller (WDM 21-51-12). 2) Measure the resistance from pin 22 to 16 on connector D15816C for the pack flow temp controller (WDM 21-51-13). (b) Measure the resistances for the right pack flow temperature sensor T474 as follows: 1) Measure the resistance from pin J9 to J10 on connector D15816B for the pack flow temp controller (WDM 21-51-12). 2) Measure the resistance from pin 22 to 16 on connector D15814C for the pack flow temp controller (WDM 21-51-13). SUBTASK 21-51-52-700-005 (5) Make a record of the resistances for each sensor that you measured. SUBTASK 21-51-52-700-006 (6) Find the temperature on Figure 501 that is nearest to the temperature that you recorded. SUBTASK 21-51-52-700-007 (7) Compare the serviceable range of resistance for that temperature to the resistance you recorded. (a) The serviceable range of resistance is between the two parallel lines on the graph. SUBTASK 21-51-52-960-001 (8) If the resistance does not agree with the serviceable range, replace the sensor: (a) To replace the sensor, do these tasks: Pack Temperature Sensor Removal, TASK 21-51-52-000-801 and Pack Temperature Sensor Installation, TASK 21-51-52-400-801.

E. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

EFFECTIVITY 006, 007, 013, 014, 018, 019, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-430 POST SB 737-21-1208; 431-999 POST SB 737-21-1209 SUBTASK 21-51-55-640-003 (5) Apply a thin layer of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the heat exchanger temperature sensor [1]. SUBTASK 21-51-55-860-002 (9) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: CAPT Electrical System Panel, P18-2 Row Col Number Name C 9 C00109 FLIGHT RECORDER AC C 10 C00468 FLIGHT RECORDER DC SUBTASK 21-51-55-740-001 (10) Do a Flight Data Recorder System (FDRS) Built-In-Test Equipment (BITE) Test, do these steps: (a) Put the FLIGHT RECORDER TEST switch, on the P5 flight recorder panel, to the TEST position. (b) After 8 seconds, make sure that the flight recorder OFF light, on the P5 aft overhead panel, is extinguished. (c) Make sure that all fail lamps on the Digital Flight Data Acquisition Unit (DFDAU) front panel are extinguished (M675 on E3-2 shelf). (d) Put the FLIGHT RECORDER TEST switch, on the P5 flight recorder panel, to the NORM position. (e) Make sure that the flight recorder OFF light, on the P5 aft overhead panel, is on.

(d) Make sure that the ISOLATION VALVE switch is in the CLOSED position. (e) Position the APU BLEED switch to ON. (f) Make sure that there is pressure indication for the left pneumatic system. (g) Position the L PACK switch to AUTO. (h) Make sure that the indication on the pressure gauge increases. (i) Make sure that the left pack flow control valve opens. 1) Use a dental mirror, STD-3907, if necessary to view the valve position. (j) Position the L PACK switch to OFF. (k) Position the ISOLATION VALVE switch to OPEN. EFFECTIVITY ALL (l) Make sure that there is pressure indication for the right pneumatic system. (m) Position the R PACK switch to AUTO. (n) Make sure that the indication on the pressure gauge increases. (o) Make sure that the right pack flow control valve opens. 1) Use a dental mirror, STD-3907, if necessary to view the valve position. (p) Set the R PACK switch to OFF. (q) Remove pressure from the pneumatic system, do this task: Remove Pressure from the Pneumatic System, TASK 36-00-00-860-806. SUBTASK 21-51-65-710-006 (11) If testing of the engine bleed switches functionality is desired, then do the following test: NOTE: It is recommended to test the engine bleed switches functionality after P5-10 panel replacement due to bleed switch failure. (a) Supply pressure to the pneumatic system with the engine on the applicable side, do these steps: WARNING YOU MUST FIRST ISOLATE THE PNEUMATIC USER SYSTEMS BEFORE YOU PRESSURIZE THE PNEUMATIC SYSTEM. IF YOU DO NOT ISOLATE THEM, THEY CAN OPERATE AND CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. IT CAN ALSO CAUSE THE PNEUMATIC SYSTEM TO DECREASE PRESSURE. 1) Do this task: Start the Engine Procedure (Selection), TASK 71-00-00-800-807-F00. 2) Put the applicable BLEED switch on the P5-10, forward overhead panel to the ON position. 3) Put the ISOLATION VALVE switch on the P5-10, forward overhead panel to the OPEN position. 4) Monitor the dual duct pressure indicator on the P5-10, forward overhead panel. a) Make sure that each duct pressure needle indicates 10 psi (68.9 kPa) - 25 psi (172.4 kPa). NOTE: The duct pressure pointers on the dual duct pressure indicator may fluctuate without user systems in operation. NOTE: Duct pressure can be 10 psi (68.9 kPa) - 25 psi (172.4 kPa) with the engine(s) at idle and no demand for pneumatic air from other user systems. (b) Set these pneumatic system control switches to the positions shown: 1) APU BLEED switch to OFF 2) ISOLATION VALVE switch to CLOSE. (c) If applicable, remove any external pneumatic source. (d) Set the pack switches to AUTO. (e) Do these steps to do a check of the operation of the engine BLEED switch Pressure Regulating and Shutoff Valve (PRSOV): NOTE: The engine BLEED switch will be cycled in these steps to make sure that there are no intermittent malfunctions in the system operation. 1) Set the applicable engine BLEED 1 or 2 switch to the OFF position. EFFECTIVITY ALL 2) Make sure that the Pointer for the applicable system on the Dual Duct Pressure Indicator decreases to less than 10 psi (68.9 kPa). 3) Set the applicable engine BLEED switch to the ON position. 4) Make sure that the Manifold Pressure Pointer for the applicable system increases to 10 psi (68.9 kPa) - 25 psi (172.4 kPa) with the engine at steady idle without user systems in operation. NOTE: The engine operation at high power is not necessary. NOTE: The Duct Pressure Pointers on the Dual Duct Pressure Indicator may fluctuate without user systems in operation. 5) Set the applicable engine BLEED switch to the OFF position. 6) Make sure that the applicable pointer on the Dual Duct Pressure Indicator decreases to less than 10 psi (68.9 kPa). (f) Set the pack switches to OFF. (g) Remove pressure from the pneumatic system, do this task: Remove Pressure from the Pneumatic System, TASK 36-00-00-860-806.

WARNING MOVE ALL PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT AWAY FROM THE RAM AIR INLET DOOR. WHEN YOU PUSH THE VERIFY SWITCH, THE RAM AIR COMPONENTS WILL MOVE AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. NOTE: The VERIFY switch will initiate a real time test of the pack and zone temperature control components. 1) Wait for the green GO light to come on. 2) If a red light comes on for a component, the component does not operate. a) Write down the component that does not operate. 21-61-00-740-801-002Pack Flow Temperature Controller BITE TestPDF p. 1483

3. Pack Flow Temperature Controller BITE Test (Figure 502)

A. General

(1) This task does a BITE test on the pack flow temperature controller. (2) The BITE test does a check on the following components: (a) Pack Flow Temperature Controller (PFTC) (b) Flight deck temperature sensor (c) Zone temperature sensor (d) Standby zone sensor (e) Flight deck duct sensor (f) Pack temperature sensor (g) Standby pack temperature sensor (h) Mix manifold temperature sensor (i) Flight deck sensor (j) Zone selector (k) Standby selector (l) Pack inlet pressure (m) Pack flow sensor (n) Flow control valve (o) Temperature control valve (p) Flight deck trim valve (q) Zone trim valve (r) Standby temperature control valve (s) Flight deck sensor (t) SRADA control (u) SRADA inlet (v) SRADA exit (w) SRADA ram sensor (3) There are two identical PFTC located on the E3-3 rack. (4) If the PFTC shows FAULT on the front panel display, there is a fault currently being detected by the controller. There may also be faults recorded in the FAULT HISTORY mode of the PFTC. (5) This BITE procedure must be done on both PFTC. (6) The steps that follow provide a summary of the function of the buttons on the front of the PFTC: (a) ON/OFF button 1) The ON/OFF button will activate or de-activate the BITE functions on the PFTC. (b) MENU button Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL 385-999 (Continued) 1) The MENU button will display the BITE menus in the PFTC. If you push the MENU button, you will go up to the previously displayed MENU. 2) You can select DOWN or NO at a MENU item to go to the next MENU item. 3) You can only select DOWN to go to the next item if it is not a MENU item. (c) YES button 1) If you select YES at a MENU item, you will go to details of the item. 2) Used to respond YES to questions on the PFTC. (d) NO button 1) You can select NO at a MENU item to go to the next item. 2) If you keep selecting NO, you will get to END OF LIST. 3) Used to respond NO to questions on the PFTC. (e) UP button 1) Used to scroll up through the menu or the results of a BITE test. (f) DOWN button 1) If you keep selecting DOWN, you will get to END OF LIST. 2) Used to scroll down through the menu or the results of a BITE test. (7) The BITE has five modes of operation as listed below: (a) Manual press ON/OFF (b) EXISTING FAULTS (c) FAULT HISTORY (d) GROUND TEST (e) OTHER FUNCTIONS (8) The steps that follow provide a summary of the main menu selections: (a) Manual press ON/OFF 1) Manually pressing the ON/OFF button will power the front panel displays. (b) EXISTING FAULTS 1) The EXISTING FAULTS main menu selection provides a list of all faults that are currently detected by the PFTC. a) Maintenance action is required to resolve those maintenance messages that show in the EXISTING FAULTS. (c) FAULT HISTORY 1) The FAULT HISTORY state is activated by selecting the DOWN arrow button or NO button when the front panel display is showing EXISTING FAULTS or scrolling up/down from the front panel display MENU button. 2) Fault memory is read and Flight Leg Fault Records are displayed in reverse chronological order; that is, the last fault on the last flight leg is displayed first and the first fault on the first flight leg is displayed last. (d) GROUND TESTS Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL 385-999 (Continued) 1) The front panel display state “Ground Test” is activated by selecting the DOWN button or the NO button when the front panel display is showing FAULT HISTORY or by scrolling up or down from the MENU. 2) The GROUND TEST state has 6 modes of operation as listed below: a) BITE Instruction b) Start GROUND TEST c) Start Display Test d) Ground Test in Progress e) Ground Test Complete f) Ground Test Results 3) During the GROUND TEST state, the BITE operator will drive the display by his inputs in response to indicated text. 4) The front panel display OTHER FUNCTIONS state has the two modes of operation listed below: a) System Config b) I/O Monitor (e) OTHER FUNCTIONS 1) The OTHER FUNCTIONS state is activated by selection at the main menu.

F. BITE Procedure for EXISTING FAULTS

SUBTASK 21-61-00-740-003-002 (1) If the front panel display is blank, then do these steps: (a) Push the ON/OFF button on the front panel. (b) If EXISTING FAULTS does not show, do these steps: 1) Push UP to go to TOP OF LIST. 2) Push MENU to go up in the menu list. SUBTASK 21-61-00-740-004-002 (2) Push the YES button on the front panel. SUBTASK 21-61-00-740-007-002 (3) Find and record the existing faults as follows: NOTE: The text of the fault will be the same as one of the maintenance messages listed in the applicable BITE Message Index in the Fault Isolation Manual (FIM). These existing faults are referred to as maintenance messages. (a) Make a record of the existing fault (maintenance message). (b) Make a record of each fault detail (fault number) for the maintenance message as follows: Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL 385-999 (Continued) 1) Push the YES button on the PFTC front panel to see the fault details (fault numbers) for the maintenance message. NOTE: The fault details for a maintenance message will be the same as one or more of the fault numbers that are listed in the PFTC Fault Number List. The number of fault details (fault numbers) varies with each maintenance message. 2) Make a record of the fault detail (fault number) for the maintenance message. 3) Push the DOWN arrow button on the PFTC front panel to find the next fault detail (fault number). NOTE: When the end of the list is reached, END OF LIST will show for two seconds and the PFTC will return to the maintenance message. (c) Push the DOWN arrow button on the PFTC front panel to find the next maintenance message in the EXISTING FAULTS list. NOTE: If there are no more faults, the display will show END OF LIST for two seconds, then the previous maintenance message will show. SUBTASK 21-61-00-740-006-002 (4) Push the MENU button on the PFTC front panel. SUBTASK 21-61-00-740-008-002 (5) Refer to the applicable BITE Message Index in the FIM to find the fault isolation task for the applicable maintenance message.

G. BITE Procedure for FAULT HISTORY

SUBTASK 21-61-00-740-010-002 (1) Make a record of all the faults in each flight leg: (a) Push the DOWN arrow button on the PFTC front panel until FAULT HISTORY shows. (b) Push the YES button on the PFTC front panel. 1) Make sure that the PFTC front panel display shows FLIGHT LEG XX. NOTE: XX is the last flight leg that faults were recorded in history. (c) If there are FLIGHT LEGS displayed on the PFTC front panel, do the steps for each flight leg as follows: NOTE: FLIGHT LEGS will not be displayed if there are no faults recorded in FAULT HISTORY. 1) Push the YES button on the PFTC front panel. 2) Find and record each fault in the flight leg fault list as follows: NOTE: The text of the fault will be the same as one of the maintenance messages listed in the applicable BITE Message Index in the FIM. These faults are referred to as maintenance messages. a) Make a record of the fault (maintenance message). b) Make a record of each fault detail (fault number) for the maintenance message as follows: <1> Push the YES button on the PFTC front panel to see the fault details (fault numbers) for the maintenance message. Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL 385-999 (Continued) <2> Make a record of the fault detail (fault number) for the maintenance message. <3> Push the DOWN arrow button on the PFTC front panel to find the next fault detail (fault number). NOTE: When the end of the list is reached, END OF LIST will show for two seconds and the PFTC will return to the maintenance message. c) Push the DOWN arrow button on the PFTC front panel to find the next fault (maintenance message) for the flight leg. NOTE: If there are no more faults, the display will show END OF LIST for two seconds, then the previous maintenance message will show. 3) Push the MENU button on the PFTC front panel until the display shows FLIGHT LEG XX. 4) Push the DOWN button on the PFTC front panel to find the next flight leg that recorded faults in fault history. SUBTASK 21-61-00-740-018-002 (2) Refer to the applicable BITE Message Index in the FIM to find the fault isolation task for the applicable maintenance message to find which FIM task(s) to use to fault isolate the maintenance message(s) that was recorded. NOTE: While PFTC stores fault history for the most recent 64 flight legs, it is recommended that operators only perform the relevant FIM task for the maintenance messages recorded in the last (most recent) flight leg. SUBTASK 21-61-00-740-019-002 (3) If the PFTC front panel display is not at a main menu selection, push the MENU button until you are in the main menu.

21-61-00-700-807-002Cabin Temperature Control and Indication - Operational TestPDF p. 1496

4. Cabin Temperature Control and Indication - Operational Test

A. General

(1) This task does an operational test of the cabin temperature control and indication components.

B. References

Reference Title 21-00-00-800-803 Supply Conditioned Air with a Cooling Pack (P/B 201) 21-00-00-800-804 Remove Conditioned Air Supplied by a Cooling Pack (P/B 201)

C. Tools/Equipment

Reference Description STD-1122 Thermometer - Alcohol/Mercury (or equivalent meter meets task requirements)

D. Location Zones

Zone Area 212 Flight Compartment - Right

E. Procedure

SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-013-002 (1) Do this task: Supply Conditioned Air with a Cooling Pack, TASK 21-00-00-800-803. SUBTASK 21-61-00-860-026-002 (2) Do these steps at the P5-17 Cabin Temperature Panel: (a) Put the CONT CAB temperature selector to the full COLD position. (b) Put the FWD CAB and AFT CAB temperature selectors to the AUTO (12:00) position. (c) Let the pack operate for 1 to 3 minutes to let the output temperature become stable. SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-014-002 (3) Do these steps to check temperature indication for the forward passenger cabin: (a) Use a thermometer, STD-1122, to measure the ambient temperature in the forward passenger cabin near the cabin temperature sensor panel. (b) Put the AIR TEMP selector on the P5-17 Cabin Temperature Panel to the FWD PASS CABIN position. (c) Make sure that the temperature shown on the indicator is approximately the same as the ambient temperature in the forward passenger cabin. (d) Move the FWD CAB temperature selector to the fully WARM position. (e) Make sure that the temperature indicator shows an increase in temperature. (f) Move the FWD CAB temperature selector to the AUTO (12:00) position. (g) Let the pack operate for 1 to 3 minutes to let the output temperature become stable. SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-015-002 (4) Do these steps to check temperature indication for the aft passenger cabin: (a) Use a thermometer, STD-1122, to measure the ambient temperature in the aft passenger cabin near the cabin temperature sensor panel. Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL (b) Put the AIR TEMP selector on the P5-17 Cabin Temperature Panel to the AFT PASS CABIN position. (c) Make sure that the temperature shown on the indicator is approximately the same as the ambient temperature in the aft passenger cabin. (d) Move the AFT CAB temperature selector to the fully WARM position. (e) Make sure that the temperature indicator shows an increase in temperature. (f) Move the AFT CAB temperature selector to the full COLD position. (g) Let the pack operate for 1 to 3 minutes to let the output temperature become stable. SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-016-002 (5) Do these steps to check temperature control for the control cabin: (a) Put the CONT CABIN temperature selector to the AUTO (12:00) position. (b) Let the pack operate for 1 to 3 minutes to let the output temperature become stable. (c) Put the AIR TEMP selector on the P5-17 Cabin Temperature Panel to the SUPPLY DUCT CONT CAB position. (d) Make a record of the temperature shown on the indicator. (e) Move the CONT CAB temperature selector to the fully WARM position. (f) Make sure that the temperature indicator shows an increase in temperature. (g) Move the CONT CAB and AFT CAB temperature selectors to the AUTO (12:00) position.

F. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-017-002 (1) Do this task: Remove Conditioned Air Supplied by a Cooling Pack, TASK 21-00-00-800-804.

F. Operational Test of the Control Cabin Duct Overheat Switch (Method I)

SUBTASK 21-61-00-020-013-002 (1) Remove the duct overheat switch. To remove the switch, do this task: Duct Overheat Switch Removal, TASK 21-61-05-000-801. (a) Re-connect the electrical connector to the duct overheat switch. SUBTASK 21-61-00-480-003-002 (2) Prepare the K-Type thermocouple switch tester, SPL-3924 and the TEMPCAL heater probe kit, SPL-1552 (Probe P/N BH17336A) or Duct Overheat Switch Adapter Probe, SPL-11497 to test the overheat switch. NOTE: Use the correct heater probe to test the overheat switch part number 641121-1. SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-058-002 CAUTION DO NOT LET THE TEMPERATURE OF THE OVERHEAT SWITCH PROBE BECOME MORE THAN 200 DEGREES F (93 DEGREES C). THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE OVERHEAT SWITCH. (3) Use the test equipment to increase the temperature of the overheat switch to 190°F (88°C). SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-059-002 (4) Make sure that these lights come on when the temperature of the overheat switch probe gets to 190±10°F (88±5°C): (a) ZONE TEMP light on the P5-17 panel (b) MASTER CAUTION and AIR COND lights on the pilots' glareshield. SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-060-002 (5) Remove the heat from the overheat switch probe. SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-061-002 (6) Let the overheat switch probe become cool. NOTE: The reset temperature for the duct overheat switch is 150°F (66°C) Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-062-002 (7) Push the TRIP RESET button on the P5-10 panel. SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-063-002 (8) Push the MASTER CAUTION reset button on the P7 glareshield panel. SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-064-002 (9) Make sure that the ZONE TEMP, MASTER CAUTION and AIR COND lights go off. SUBTASK 21-61-00-420-003-002 (10) Install the duct overheat switch. To install the switch, do this task: Duct Overheat Switch Installation, TASK 21-61-05-400-801.

G. Operational Test of the Control Cabin Duct Overheat Switch (Method II)

SUBTASK 21-61-00-020-016 (1) Remove the duct overheat switch. To remove the switch, do this task: Duct Overheat Switch Removal, TASK 21-61-05-000-801. SUBTASK 21-61-00-420-005 (2) Install a new or serviceable duct overheat switch. To install the switch, do this task: Duct Overheat Switch Installation, TASK 21-61-05-400-801 NOTE: The duct overheat switch that was removed should be tested according to the vendor CMM before it is put back into service. SUBTASK 21-61-00-020-015 (3) Remove the electrical connector from the duct overheat switch. SUBTASK 21-61-00-480-005 (4) Connect a jumper wire between pin 1 and pin 2 of the electrical connector. SUBTASK 21-61-00-210-005 (5) Make sure that these lights come on: (a) ZONE TEMP light on the P5-17 panel. (b) MASTER CAUTION and AIR COND lights on the pilots' glareshield. SUBTASK 21-61-00-080-001 (6) Disconnect the jumper wire. SUBTASK 21-61-00-860-089 (7) Push the TRIP RESET button on the P5-10 panel. SUBTASK 21-61-00-860-090 (8) Push the MASTER CAUTION reset button on the P7 glareshield panel. SUBTASK 21-61-00-210-006 (9) Make sure that the ZONE TEMP, MASTER CAUTION, and AIR COND lights go off. SUBTASK 21-61-00-420-006 (10) Connect the electrical connector to the duct overheat switch.

H. Operational Test of the Passenger Cabin Duct Overheat Switch (Method I)

SUBTASK 21-61-00-020-014-002 (1) Remove the forward passenger cabin duct overheat switch. To remove the switch, do this task: Duct Overheat Switch Removal, TASK 21-61-05-000-801. (a) Re-connect the electrical connector to the duct overheat switch. Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-61-00-480-004-002 (2) Prepare the K-Type thermocouple switch tester, SPL-3924 and the TEMPCAL heater probe kit, SPL-1552 (Probe P/N BH17336A) or Duct Overheat Switch Adapter Probe, SPL-11497 to test the overheat switch. NOTE: Use the correct heater probe to test overheat switch part number 641121-1. SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-065-002 CAUTION DO NOT LET THE TEMPERATURE OF THE OVERHEAT SWITCH PROBE BECOME MORE THAN 200 DEGREES F (93 DEGREES C). THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE OVERHEAT SWITCH. (3) Use the test equipment to increase the temperature of the overheat switch to 190°F (88°C). SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-066-002 (4) Make sure that these lights come on when the temperature of the overheat switch probe gets to 190±10°F (88±5°C): (a) ZONE TEMP light on the P5-17 panel (b) MASTER CAUTION and AIR COND lights on the pilots' glareshield SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-067-002 (5) Remove the heat from the overheat switch probe. SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-068-002 (6) Let the overheat switch probe become cool. NOTE: The reset temperature for the duct overheat switch is 150°F (66°C) SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-069-002 (7) Push the TRIP RESET button on the P5-10 panel. SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-070-002 (8) Push the MASTER CAUTION reset button on the P7 glareshield panel. SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-071-002 (9) Make sure that the ZONE TEMP, MASTER CAUTION and AIR COND lights go off. SUBTASK 21-61-00-420-004-002 (10) Install the duct overheat switch. To install the switch, do this task: Duct Overheat Switch Installation, TASK 21-61-05-400-801. SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-072-002 (11) Repeat the test for the aft passenger cabin duct overheat switch.

I. Operational Test of the Passenger Cabin Duct Overheat Switch (Method II)

SUBTASK 21-61-00-020-017 (1) Remove the duct overheat switch. To remove the switch, do this task: Duct Overheat Switch Removal, TASK 21-61-05-000-801. SUBTASK 21-61-00-420-007 (2) Install a new or serviceable duct overheat switch. To install the switch, do this task: Duct Overheat Switch Installation, TASK 21-61-05-400-801 NOTE: The duct overheat switch that was removed should be tested according to the vendor CMM before it is put back into service. SUBTASK 21-61-00-020-018 (3) Remove the electrical connector from the duct overheat switch. Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-61-00-480-006 (4) Connect a jumper wire between pin 1 and pin 2 of the electrical connector. SUBTASK 21-61-00-210-007 (5) Make sure that these lights come on: (a) ZONE TEMP light on the P5-17 panel. (b) MASTER CAUTION and AIR COND lights on the pilots' glareshield. SUBTASK 21-61-00-080-002 (6) Disconnect the jumper wire. SUBTASK 21-61-00-860-091 (7) Push the TRIP RESET button on the P5-10 panel. SUBTASK 21-61-00-860-092 (8) Push the MASTER CAUTION reset button on the P7 glareshield panel. SUBTASK 21-61-00-210-008 (9) Make sure that the ZONE TEMP, MASTER CAUTION, and AIR COND lights go off. SUBTASK 21-61-00-420-008 (10) Connect the electrical connector to the duct overheat switch. SUBTASK 21-61-00-710-073 (11) Repeat the test for the aft passenger cabin duct overheat switch.

J. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 21-61-00-410-017-002 (1) Install the ceiling panels that you removed to do the test. SUBTASK 21-61-00-410-018-002 (2) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door

SUBTASK 21-61-04-860-051-002 (4) To do a test of the forward duct temperature sensor or the control cabin sensor, remove the right pack/zone temperature controller (TASK 21-61-20-000-801 or TASK 21-61-17-020-801).
