F. Resistance Check Procedure

SUBTASK 21-61-04-700-007-002 (1) Use a digital thermometer, COM-3955 or equivalent, to measure the temperature adjacent to the applicable duct temperature sensor. (a) Write down the temperature. SUBTASK 21-61-04-760-002-002 (2) Use a digital/analog multimeter, COM-1793 to measure resistance between the following pin connections. NOTE: The digital multimeter must be specifically selected to minimize self-heating of the sensor element. The instrument must limit the current through the sensor to less than 100 microamperes. If you use resistance measuring instruments without this current-limiting feature you will get an error in resistance value due to self-heating of the sensor element. Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044, 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-384 SUBTASK 21-61-04-700-008-002 (3) For the control cabin duct temperature sensor, measure the resistance from pin A5 to pin B5 on connector D3860A for the zone temperature controller No. 2 (WDM 21-61-11). SUBTASK 21-61-04-700-009-002 (4) For the forward cabin duct temperature sensor, measure the resistance from pin C6 to pin C7 on connector D3860A for the zone temperature controller No. 2 (WDM 21-61-13). SUBTASK 21-61-04-700-010-002 (5) For the control cabin backup duct temperature sensor, measure the resistance between pin A5 and pin B5 on connector D3858A for the zone temperature controller No. 1 (WDM 21-61-12). SUBTASK 21-61-04-700-011-002 (6) For the aft cabin duct temperature sensor, measure the resistance from pin C6 to pin C7 on connector D3858A for the zone temperature controller No. 1 (WDM 21-61-14). 385-999 SUBTASK 21-61-04-700-013-002 (7) For the control cabin duct temperature sensor, measure the resistance from pin E9 to pin E10 on connector D15816B for the right pack flow temperature controller (WDM 21-61-11). SUBTASK 21-61-04-700-014-002 (8) For the forward cabin duct temperature sensor, measure the resistance from pin B8 to pin B9 on connector D15816B for the right pack flow temperature controller (WDM 21-61-13). SUBTASK 21-61-04-700-015-002 (9) For the control cabin backup duct temperature sensor, measure the resistance between pin E9 and pin E10 on connector D15814B for the left pack flow temperature controller (WDM 21-61-12). SUBTASK 21-61-04-700-016-002 (10) For the aft cabin duct temperature sensor, measure the resistance from pin B8 to pin B9 on connector D15814B for the left pack flow temperature controller (WDM 21-61-14). ALL SUBTASK 21-61-04-700-012-002 (11) Write down the resistance in Ohms that you measure. (a) For the duct temperature sensors for the control cabin, the passenger cabin, the SC or the MDCC, find the temperature on Figure 504 that is nearest to the temperature that you wrote down. (b) Compare the permitted range of resistance for that temperature to the resistance you wrote down. (c) If the resistance is out of range, replace the sensor. To replace the sensor, These are the tasks: Duct Temperature Limit Sensor Removal, TASK 21-61-04-000-803-002, Duct Temperature Limit Sensor Installation, TASK 21-61-04-400-803-002. Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL

G. Cabin Temperature Sensor Assembly Grille Cleaning

SUBTASK 21-61-06-110-003 (1) Prepare a cleaning solution of water and general purpose household detergent cleaner, B00541, or Brulin Formula 815MX cleaner, B00039. (a) Follow the mixing instructions for the cleaner. SUBTASK 21-61-06-110-004 (2) Clean the grille with the cleaning solution. SUBTASK 21-61-06-100-005 (3) If the cleaning solution did not remove all dirt or contamination from the grille, clean the grille with cotton wiper, G00034, that is moist with alcohol, B00130. SUBTASK 21-61-06-100-006 (4) Flush the grille with clean water until all of the cleaning solution or alcohol has been removed. SUBTASK 21-61-06-100-007 (5) Dry the grille with cotton wiper, G00034.

Zone Area 212 Flight Compartment - Right

B. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 21-61-07-840-005-002 (1) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name C 5 C00263 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONT VALVES R C 6 C00262 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONT VALVES L SUBTASK 21-61-07-860-010-002 (2) Put the L PACK switch and R PACK switch, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, to the OFF position.

C. Cabin Temperature Selector Removal

SUBTASK 21-61-07-010-002-002 (1) Do these steps to get access to the electrical connector [1] on the back of the cabin temperature panel [3] (P5-17). (a) Loosen the 1/4-turn fasteners that hold the aft end of the P5 forward overhead panel in place. NOTE: The forward end of the P5 panel is hinged. The aft end of the P5 panel will rotate downward when the fasteners are loose. (b) Release the safety latch and carefully lower the P5 forward overhead panel to the open position. SUBTASK 21-61-07-020-007-002 (2) Do the steps that follow to remove the cabin temperature selector [2] from the cabin temperature panel [3] (P5-17): (a) Disconnect the electrical connector [1] from the cabin temperature selector [2]. (b) Loosen the setscrew that hold the knob [6] to the cabin temperature selector [2]. (c) Remove the knob [6] from the cabin temperature selector [2]. (d) Remove the nut [5] and washer [4] from the cabin temperature selector [2]. Config 2 EFFECTIVITY ALL (e) Carefully pull the cabin temperature selector [2] out of the cabin temperature panel [3] (P5-17).

E. Cabin Temperature Selector Test

SUBTASK 21-61-07-840-006-002 (1) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name C 5 C00263 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONT VALVES R C 6 C00262 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONT VALVES L SUBTASK 21-61-07-860-012-002 (2) Do this task: Supply Conditioned Air to the Airplane, TASK 21-00-00-800-801. SUBTASK 21-61-07-710-013-002 (3) Put the R PACK switch and L PACK switch, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel, to the AUTO position. SUBTASK 21-61-07-710-014-002 (4) Put the TRIM AIR switch, on the P5-17 cabin temperature panel, to the ON position. SUBTASK 21-61-07-710-015-002 (5) Put the cabin temperature selector [2] to the AUTO position. (a) Make sure that the airflow from the conditioned air outlets in the applicable cabin/zone becomes warm. SUBTASK 21-61-07-710-016-002 (6) Put the cabin temperature selector [2] in the fully Cool position. (a) Make sure that the airflow from the conditioned air outlets in the applicable cabin/zone becomes cool. SUBTASK 21-61-07-710-017-002 (7) Hold the cabin temperature selector [2] in the fully Warm position. (a) Make sure that the airflow from the conditioned air outlets in the applicable cabin/zone becomes warm. SUBTASK 21-61-07-810-003-002 (8) If you find a problem with the cabin temperature selector [2], do the steps in the FIM and do the applicable procedure(s) to correct the problem. SUBTASK 21-61-07-740-001 (9) Do a BITE test on the left and right pack/zone temperature controllers (M1442 and M1443): NOTE: This will clear any fault introduced during maintenance when power is interrupted. (a) To do the BITE test, do this task: Pack/Zone Temperature Controller BITE Test, TASK 21-61-00-700-806-002 or Pack Flow Temperature Controller BITE Test, TASK 21-61-00-740-801-002.

F. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 21-61-07-710-018-002 (1) Put the cabin temperature selector [2] to the NORMAL position. SUBTASK 21-61-07-860-013-002 (2) Do this task: Remove Conditioned Air from the Airplane, TASK 21-00-00-800-802.

F. Trim Air Check Valve Installation

SUBTASK 21-61-09-420-001 (1) Install the trim air check valve [5] as follows: (a) Install the orifice plate [14] using one of the two methods below: 1) Method 1, install the orifice plate [14] un-bonded to the outlet side of the trim air check valve [5]. 2) Method 2, install orifice plate [14] bonded to the outlet side of the trim air check valve [5]. NOTE: Bonding is optional and not required for proper operation. a) If bonding is preferred, bond the orifice plate [14] to the trim air check valve [5] as follows: <1> Use wiper, G50262, moist in alcohol, B00130, to clean the mating surfaces of the orifice plate [14] and trim air check valve [5]. <a> If it is necessary, use clean wiper, G50262, to remove remaining solvent. <2> Clean the mating surface of the orifice plate [14] with 150 grit abrasive paper, G02428. <a> Use wiper, G50262, moist in alcohol, B00130, to clean the mating surface of the orifice plate [14]. <b> If it is necessary, use clean wiper, G50262, to remove remaining solvent. <3> Apply PR 1204 primer, A50126, or Dow Corning PR-1204 prime coat, C50242, to mating surfaces of the orifice plate [14] and trim air check valve [5]. <a> Let the primer dry for a minimum of 60 minutes at 65°F (18.3°C) - 100°F (37.8°C). <4> Apply Dow Corning 3145 RTV adhesive, A00281, to the mating surfaces of the orifice plate [14] and trim air check valve [5]. <5> Attach the orifice plate [14] to the outlet flange of the trim air check valve [5]. <a> Make sure that the orifice plate [14] is centered on the outlet flange of trim air check valve [5]. <6> Apply the pressure to the bonding surfaces. <a> Make sure that there is no squeeze out. <7> Let adhesive dry under pressure for a minimum of 24 hours at 65°F (18.3°C) - 100°F (37.8°C) and at more than 30 percent relative humidity. (b) Put the trim air check valve [5] in its position. 1) Make sure that the flow arrow on the trim air check valve [5] points in the forward direction. 2) Make sure that the ports of the trim air check valve [5] point up. (c) Move the clamps [6] to the duct connections. (d) Tighten the nuts on the two clamps [6] to 55 in-lb (6 N·m) - 60 in-lb (7 N·m). 1) Make sure that the loop bands do not touch. G. Trim Air Check Valve Leakage Check

SUBTASK 21-61-09-860-003 (1) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System (Selection), TASK 36-00-00-860-801. SUBTASK 21-61-09-860-004 (2) Do these steps on the P5-10 air conditioning panel (located on the P5 forward overhead panel): EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Set the L PACK and R PACK switches to the AUTO position and remove the DO-NOT-OPERATE tags. (b) Set the ENG 1 BLEED and ENG 2 BLEED switches to the ON position and remove the DO-NOT-OPERATE tags. (c) Set the APU BLEED switch to the ON position and remove the DO-NOT-OPERATE tag. SUBTASK 21-61-09-790-001 (3) Do a soap bubble test of the duct joints of the trim air check valve [5], duct assembly [9], and duct assembly [12]. NOTE: No air leakage is permitted. (a) If there is leakage, do these steps: 1) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches to the OFF position. WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE COOLING PACK DUCTS WHEN THEY ARE HOT. THE COOLING PACK DUCTS CAN BE HOT AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS. 2) Loosen the clamps. 3) Make sure that the ducts are aligned at the joints. 4) Tighten the clamps. 5) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches to the AUTO position. 6) Make sure the leak has been repaired.

D. Trim Air Check Valve Inspection

SUBTASK 21-61-09-200-001 (1) Inspect the trim air check valve for these defects: (a) The valve body [1] has cracks or corrosion. (b) The valve flappers [2] do not move freely. (c) The valve flappers [2] do not touch the valve body equally. (d) There are carbon particles at the valve flappers [2] and body interface. (e) The valve flappers [2] are bent. (f) The stop pin tube [3] has cracks or deterioration. (g) If the trim air check valve has one or more of the defects, replace the trim air check valve. SUBTASK 21-61-10-860-036 (1) Remove the cabin temperature sensor [1] in the flight compartment as follows (Figure 201 or Figure 202): (a) Loosen the access panel on the aft ceiling lining in the flight compartment and let it hang on the straps. NOTE: The access panel on the aft ceiling lining is held in position by hook and loop strips. (b) Disconnect the electrical connector (D10958) from the sensor [1]. (c) Remove the screws [2] and washers [3] that attach the sensor [1] to the temperature sensor assembly. NOTE: The notches in the outboard flange of the MCD/PSU rail show the locations of the clips. 3) Turn the bullnose cover [21] inboard to remove it. 4. Cabin Temperature Sensor Cleaning

A. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification B00130 Alcohol - Isopropyl TT-I-735 G00034 Cotton Wiper - Process Cleaning Absorbent Wiper (Cheesecloth, Gauze) AMS3819 Class 1 Grade A or B Form 1 (Supersede BMS15-5 CL A)

B. Preparation for Cabin Temperature Sensor Cleaning

SUBTASK 21-61-10-020-008 (1) Remove the temperature sensor for the flight compartment. To remove the temperature sensor, do this task: Cabin Temperature Sensor Removal, TASK 21-61-10-000-802. SUBTASK 21-61-10-020-009 (2) Remove the temperature sensor for the passenger compartment. To remove the temperature sensor, do this task: Cabin Temperature Sensor Removal, TASK 21-61-10-000-802.

C. Cabin Temperature Sensor Cleaning

SUBTASK 21-61-10-100-002 (1) Do these steps to clean the temperature sensor: (a) Prepare a cleaning solution of a commercially available mild liquid detergent diluted with water in accordance with the instructions on the detergent container. (b) Clean the sensor with a cotton wiper, G00034 that is moist with the cleaning solution. (c) If the cotton wiper, G00034 with the cleaning solution did not remove all dirt deposits or contamination from the sensor, clean the sensor with a cotton wiper, G00034 that is moist with alcohol, B00130. (d) Flush the sensor with clean water until all traces of the detergent solution or alcohol are removed. (e) Dry the sensor with dry, clean cotton wiper, G00034.

D. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 21-61-10-420-008 (1) Install the flight compartment temperature sensor. To install the flight compartment temperature sensor, do this task: Cabin Temperature Sensor Installation, TASK 21-61-10-400-802. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-61-10-420-009 (2) Install the passenger compartment temperature sensor. To install the temperature sensor, do this task: Cabin Temperature Sensor Installation, TASK 21-61-10-400-802.

E. Flight Compartment Cabin Temperature Sensor Fan Installation

SUBTASK 21-61-11-420-001 (1) Install the cabin temperature sensor fan [3] in the flight compartment as follows (Figure 401): (a) Put the fan [3] in its position with the other components of the temperature sensor assembly. (b) Install the clamps [10], washers [11], and screws [12] to attach the fan [3] to the cabin temperature sensor assembly. NOTE: The orientation of the screws on the temperature sensor fan can vary. Either direction of the fastener is acceptable. (c) Install the fan wires [4] on the fan terminal board [13] with the screws [5] and washers [6]. NOTE: Use the tags on the fan wires to put the fan wires in the correct locations. 1) Clean the mating surfaces on the terminal board [13] with wiper, G50262, soaked in aliphatic naphtha, B50079, or aliphatic naphtha, B50078, or solvent, B00316. 2) Wipe dry with wiper, G50262, before solvent evaporates. a) If it is necessary repeat steps to completely remove contaminants. b) Coat 0.05 ±0.03 in. (1.3 ±0.8 mm) thick of compound, A50589, on the fan wires [4]. NOTE: Coatings that are thinner than 0.04 in. (1.0 mm) are difficult to remove in-service and should be avoided. (d) To install the aft ceiling panel [7] in the flight compartment, do this task: Flight Compartment Aft Ceiling Panel Installation, TASK 25-11-21-400-806. (e) Connect the electrical connector [1] and electrical connector [2] (D10958 and D10956) to the temperature sensor and the fan [3]. (f) To install the access panel, lift it to its position and push firmly to make sure the hook and loop strips are fully engaged.

SUBTASK 21-61-12-630-002 (1) Remove the covers from the duct openings and make sure that there is no unwanted materials inside the duct. SUBTASK 21-61-12-420-006 (2) If you removed the trim air duct [3] that penetrates through the pressure bulkhead, do these steps to reinstall it (Figure 401): (a) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 821 Forward Cargo Door (b) Remove the aft bulkhead liner in the forward cargo compartment (TASK 25-52-17-000-801). (c) Slide the trim air duct [3] through the pressure bulkhead hole. (d) Support the trim air duct [3]. (e) Loosely install the aft coupling [11] in the mix manifold bay to connect trim air duct [3] to trim air duct [12]. SUBTASK 21-61-12-100-002 (3) Use a clean wiper and solvent, B00083, to clean the pressure seal support [3A] area on the trim air duct [3] that penetrates through the pressure bulkhead (Figure 401). SUBTASK 21-61-12-420-008 (4) Slide the pressure seal [5] onto the trim air duct [3]. SUBTASK 21-61-12-420-009 (5) For installation of the pressure seal [5], do the following steps (Figure 401): (a) Push the pressure seal [5] to the mating surface of the pressure bulkhead. (b) Apply antiseize compound, D00010, to the threads of the bolt [7]. (c) Install the two seal ring havles [6] on the pressure seal [5] with the twelve bolts [7] and washers [8]. NOTE: The two bolts at 11 and 12 o'clock positions attach the duct overheat sensor to the pressure bulkhead and are longer than the other bolts. The duct overheat sensor support bracket must be installed on top of the seal ring half [6]. (d) Tighten the bolts [7] to 32.5 ±2.5 in-lb (3.67 ±0.28 N·m) in the sequence shown in Figure 401. (e) Install the clamp [9] loosely to the pressure seal [5]. EFFECTIVITY ALL (f) Do these steps to tighten the clamp [9]: 1) Turn the torque wrench to tighten the clamp [9] and observe the torque needed to turn the nut on the clamp T-bolt before the clamp becomes tight. NOTE: The observed torque should be 8.5 ±6.5 in-lb (0.96 ±0.73 N·m). This torque is referred to as run-on torque. 2) Add the observed run-on torque to 20 ±2 in-lb (2.26 ±0.23 N·m). For example, if the run-on torque needed to turn the T-bolt nut was 10 in-lb (1 N·m), then the torque needed to tighten the clamp is 30 ±2 in-lb (3.39 ±0.23 N·m). This is the calculated torque needed to tighten the clamp. 3) Tighten the clamp [9] to the torque calculated in the previous step. 4) Wait a minimum of 2 hours, then retighten the clamp [9] to the torque calculated in the previous step. D. Prepare for the Flight Compartment Temperature Sensor Assembly Housing Cleaning

SUBTASK 21-61-14-020-024 (1) Remove the cabin temperature assembly housing for the flight compartment. To remove the housing, do this task: Flight Compartment Temperature Sensor Assembly Housing Removal, TASK 21-61-14-000-802.

E. Procedure

SUBTASK 21-61-14-160-001 (1) Prepare a weak solution of general purpose household detergent cleaner, B00541 mixed with warm water, G50256. (a) Obey the instructions on the detergent container. SUBTASK 21-61-14-160-002 (2) Clean the inner and external surfaces of the housing with a cotton wiper, G00034 that is moist with the cleaning solution. SUBTASK 21-61-14-160-003 (3) If the cotton wiper, G00034 with the cleaning solution did not remove all dirt deposits or contamination, clean the housing with a cotton wiper, G00034 that is moist with alcohol, B00130. SUBTASK 21-61-14-160-004 (4) Wipe the housing with a cotton wiper, G00034 that is moist with clean water until all of the detergent solution or alcohol are removed. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-61-14-160-005 (5) Dry the housing with a dry, clean cotton wiper, G00034.

F. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 21-61-14-210-001 (1) Before the installation of the temperature sensor assembly housing, do the steps that follow: (a) Examine the temperature sensor [14] for unwanted material. (b) If unwanted material is found, clean the sensor: Cabin Temperature Sensor Cleaning, TASK 21-61-10-100-801. SUBTASK 21-61-14-420-021 (2) Install the temperature sensor assembly housing, do this task: Flight Compartment Temperature Sensor Assembly Housing Installation, TASK 21-61-14-400-802.

Reference Title 36-00-00-860-802 Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System with an External Ground Air Source (P/B 201) 36-00-00-860-803 Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System with the APU (P/B 201) 36-00-00-860-806 Remove Pressure from the Pneumatic System (P/B 201)

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 192 Lower Wing-To-Body Fairing - Under Wing Box 211 Flight Compartment - Left

C. Trim Air Pressure Regulating and Shutoff Valve Operational Test

SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-001 (1) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System with the APU, TASK 36-00-00-860-803 or Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System with an External Ground Air Source, TASK 36-00-00-860-802. SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-002 (2) Make sure that these circuit breakers are closed: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name C 5 C00263 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONT VALVES R C 6 C00262 AIR CONDITIONING PACK CONT VALVES L D 9 C01172 AIR CONDITIONING TRIM AIR PRESS SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-003 (3) Do these steps, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel: (a) Set the L RECIRC switch to the AUTO position. (b) Set the R RECIRC switch to the AUTO position. (c) Set the L PACK switch to the AUTO position. (d) Set the R PACK switch to the OFF position. (e) Set the BLEED APU switch to the ON position. (f) Set the BLEED 1 switch to the OFF position. (g) Set the BLEED 2 switch to the OFF position. (h) Set the ISOLATION VALVE switch to the OPEN position. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-004 (4) Do these steps, on the P5-17 cabin temperature panel: (a) Set the TRIM AIR switch to the OFF position. (b) Set the AIR TEMP selector to the L PACK position. (c) Set the CONT CAB selector to the full WARM position. (d) Set the FWD CAB selector to the full WARM position. (e) Set the AFT CAB selector to the full WARM position. SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-005 (5) Operate the pack for 3 to 5 minutes to let the output temperature become stable. SUBTASK 21-62-00-970-001 (6) Make a record of the temperature shown on the AIR TEMP gage, on the P5-17 panel, for the L PACK. SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-006 (7) Do these steps, on the P5-17 cabin temperature panel: (a) Set the CONT CAB selector to the full COLD position. (b) Set the FWD CAB selector to the full COLD position. (c) Set the AFT CAB selector to the full COLD position. SUBTASK 21-62-00-970-002 (8) Make sure that the temperature shown on the AIR TEMP gage, on the P5-17 panel, for the L PACK decreases. SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-007 (9) Set the TRIM AIR switch to the ON position. SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-008 (10) Operate the pack for 3 to 5 minutes to let the output temperature become stable. SUBTASK 21-62-00-970-003 (11) Make a record of the temperature shown on the AIR TEMP gage for the L PACK. SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-009 (12) Set the AIR TEMP selector to the FWD SUPPLY DUCT position. SUBTASK 21-62-00-970-004 (13) Make a record of the temperature shown on the AIR TEMP gage for the FWD SUPPLY DUCT. SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-010 (14) Move the FWD CAB temperature selector to the full WARM position. SUBTASK 21-62-00-970-005 (15) Make sure that the temperature shown on the AIR TEMP gage for the FWD SUPPLY DUCT increases. SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-011 (16) Move the AIR TEMP selector to the L PACK position. SUBTASK 21-62-00-970-006 (17) Make sure that the L PACK temperature stays approximately the same.

D. Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-012 (1) Do these steps, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel: EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Set the L and R PACK switches to the OFF position. (b) Set the L RECIRC switch to the OFF position. (c) Set the R RECIRC switch to the OFF position. (d) Set the BLEED APU switch to the OFF position. (e) Make sure that the BLEED 1 and BLEED 2 switches are in the OFF position. SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-013 (2) Do these steps, on the P5-17 cabin temperature panel: (a) Set the TRIM AIR switch to the ON position. (b) Set the CONT CAB selector to the AUTO position. (c) Set the FWD CAB selector to the AUTO position. (d) Set the AFT CAB selector to the AUTO position. SUBTASK 21-62-00-860-014 (3) If it is not necessary, remove pneumatic power, do this task: Remove Pressure from the Pneumatic System, TASK 36-00-00-860-806.

(b) Move the bonding jumper away from the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1]. 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 SUBTASK 21-62-01-020-010 (3) Do these steps to remove the bonding jumper: EFFECTIVITY ALL 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 (Continued) (a) Remove the screw [8], washer [5], and nut [4] that attach the bonding jumper to the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1]. NOTE: The end fittings on the sense line are not always the same. (b) Loosen the B-nut and disconnect the sense line from the union [6]. SUBTASK 21-62-01-020-004 (5) Do these steps to remove the hose assembly: (a) Loosen the B-nut to disconnect the hose assembly from the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1]. (b) Remove the union [6] from the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1]. (c) Remove and discard the packing [7]. SUBTASK 21-62-01-020-005 WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE COOLING PACK DUCTS WHEN THEY ARE HOT. THE DUCTS CAN BE HOT AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS. (6) To remove the shutoff valve, do these steps: (a) Loosen the two clamps [2]. (b) Move the clamps [2] to the adjacent ducts. (c) Remove the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1] from the Environmental Control System (ECS) bay.

G. Trim Air Pressure Regulating and Shutoff Valve Installation

SUBTASK 21-62-01-420-001 (1) To install the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1], do these steps: (a) Put the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1] in its position between the ducts. 1) Make sure that the flow arrow on the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1] points in the forward direction. (b) Rotate the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1] to make sure that there is a minimum distance of 0.75 in. (1.90 cm) between the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1] and bottom of the keel beam. 1) Make sure that there is a minimum clearance of 0.15 in. (0.38 cm) between the structure, tubes, and clamps [2]. (c) Loosely install the clamps [2]. SUBTASK 21-62-01-420-002 (2) To install the sense line on the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1], do these steps: (a) Install a new packing [7] on the union [6]. EFFECTIVITY ALL (b) Apply a thin layer of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the union [6]. (c) Install the union [6] on the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1]. (d) Install the sense line on the union [6]: 1) Make sure that you install the same end of the sense line to the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1] as you noted at the removal. NOTE: Some sense lines have different end fittings. SUBTASK 21-62-01-020-006 (3) Do these steps to install the hose assembly: (a) Install a new packing [7] on the union [6]. (b) Apply a thin layer of Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads of the union [6]. (c) Install the union [6] on the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1]. (d) Install the sense line on the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1]. 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044 SUBTASK 21-62-01-020-007 (4) Do these steps to install the bonding jumper: (a) Put the bonding jumper in its position on the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1]. (b) Install the screw [8], washer [5], and nut [4] that hold the bonding jumper to the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1]. (c) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1] and bonding jumper (SWPM 20-20-00). 1) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. 2) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.0025 ohm (2.5 milliohm) or less. 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 SUBTASK 21-62-01-020-009 (5) Do these steps to install the bonding jumper: (a) Put the bonding jumper in its position on the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1]. (b) Install the screw [8], washer [5], and nut [4] that hold the bonding jumper to the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1]. (c) Measure the electrical bonding resistance between the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1] and bonding jumper (SWPM 20-20-00). 1) Use an intrinsically safe approved bonding meter, COM-1550. 2) Make sure that the electrical bonding resistance is 0.0025 ohm (2.5 milliohm) or less. ALL EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-62-01-020-008 (6) Install the electrical connector [3] on the shutoff trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1]. (7.874 mm). 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 (c) Make sure that the clearance between the retainers is 0.050 in. H. Trim Air Pressure Regulating and Shutoff Valve Operational Check

SUBTASK 21-62-01-860-005 (1) Remove the safety tag and close this circuit breaker: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name D 9 C01172 AIR CONDITIONING TRIM AIR PRESS SUBTASK 21-62-01-860-006 (2) Do this task: Supply Pressure to the Pneumatic System (Selection), TASK 36-00-00-860-801. SUBTASK 21-62-01-860-007 (3) Do these steps, on the P5-10 air conditioning panel: (a) Set the L and R PACK switches to the AUTO position and remove the DO-NOT-OPERATE tags. (b) Set the BLEED 1 and 2 switches to the ON position and remove the DO-NOT-OPERATE tags. (c) Set the BLEED APU switch to the ON position and remove the DO-NOT-OPERATE tag. SUBTASK 21-62-01-860-008 (4) Do these steps, on the P5-17 Cabin Temperature Panel: (a) Set the TRIM AIR switch to the ON position and remove the DO-NOT-OPERATE tag. (b) Set the CONT CAB selector to the fully WARM position and remove the DO-NOT-OPERATE tag. (c) Set the FWD CAB selector to the fully COLD position and remove the DO-NOT-OPERATE tag. (d) Set the AFT CAB selector to the fully COLD position and remove the DO-NOT-OPERATE tag. SUBTASK 21-62-01-860-009 (5) Operate the pack for a minute to let the output temperature become stable. SUBTASK 21-62-01-860-010 (6) Do these steps, on the P5-17 Cabin Temperature Panel: EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Set AIR TEMP selector to the each of the three SUPPLY DUCT positions (AFT, FWD and CONT CAB) (b) Record the temperature shown on the indicator for each of the three SUPPLY DUCT positions. (c) Make sure that the supply duct temperature for the CONT CAB is higher than the supply duct temperatures for the FWD and AFT.

I. Trim Air Pressure Regulating and Shutoff Valve Leakage Check

SUBTASK 21-62-01-790-001 (1) Do a soap bubble test of the duct joints at the trim air pressure regulating and shutoff valve [1]. NOTE: No air leakage is permitted. (a) If there is leakage, do these steps: 1) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches to the OFF position. WARNING DO NOT TOUCH THE COOLING PACK DUCTS WHEN THEY ARE HOT. THE COOLING PACK DUCTS CAN BE HOT AND CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS. 2) Loosen the clamps. 3) Make sure that the ducts are aligned at the joints. 4) Tighten the clamps. a) Make sure that the loop bands do not touch. 006, 007, 013, 014, 018-020, 043, 044 b) Make sure that the clearance between the retainers is 0.050 in. (1.270 mm) - 0.310 in. (7.874 mm). 056-063, 067-078, 081, 083-103, 111-114, 121-129, 131, 132, 135, 138-169, 174-179, 182-187, 189-203, 205-209, 212-220, 223, 224, 231-236, 239-298, 301-304, 306, 308, 315-317, 322-341, 343, 346-999 c) Make sure that the clearance between the retainers is 0.050 in. (1.270 mm) - 0.410 in. (10.414 mm). ALL 5) Put the L PACK and R PACK switches to the AUTO position. 6) Make sure that the leak has been repaired.

EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 21-62-01-860-011 (2) Remove pneumatic power if it is not necessary (TASK 36-00-00-860-806).
